News.title: Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it
News.content:
England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

News.title: What is the XFG Covid strain? Symptoms and what to know as the variant hits the UK
News.content:
Cases of Covid-19 have risen sharply across the UK this month, driven largely by a variant of the virus known as ‘XFG’.

Sometimes referred to as ‘Stratus’ and the ‘American strain’, owing to the fact that it is now the most common strain in North America, it was first identified in January 2025 and has since spread worldwide.

Between August and September, Covid cases in Britain jumped 230 per cent, from 1,374 to 4,589 new infections, half of which were caused by the XFG strain.

Hospitalisation rates have also increased by 15 per cent in the same period, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

The true number of cases is likely to be much higher, as most people who contract Covid-19 experience a milder illness and will not visit hospital or receive an official diagnosis via their GP.

What are the symptoms, and how is it different from other variants?

Symptoms of XFG are similar to other variants of Covid-19 like Delta and Omicron, and typically begin with a sore throat, before developing into a cough and fever.

However, experts have noted that patients diagnosed with XFG tend to present with a characteristic hoarse, croaky voice, which is distinctive from older strains.

More than 30 other symptoms have been known to be associated with XFG and other Covid strains, including diarrhoea, vomiting, loss of taste and smell, shortness of breath, headache, and muscle aches.

Why are cases rising?

Current data does not suggest that XFG leads to more severe illness than any other variant in circulation, according to the UKHSA.

As the UK moves into winter, colder and wetter weather naturally influences the rise in respiratory illnesses like Covid-19 and the flu, given people spend more time indoors and in closer proximity to each other, where viruses can more easily transmit between them.

It has also been roughly a year since the last significant wave of Covid-19 cases, meaning that the population-wide immunity has somewhat waned, making people more susceptible to the disease, the UKHSA said.

Can you be vaccinated against XFG?

The current Covid-19 vaccine is designed to protect against XFG and related strains specifically, after modelling suggested it would become the dominant variant this season.

Those eligible for a Covid-19 autumn booster include adults over the age of 75, residents in care homes, and anyone over six months old with a weakened immune system, due to a health condition or treatment.

Covid vaccines are also available to buy privately for those who are not eligible for a free jab, and typically cost around £98 per dose.

What should you do if you suspect you have XFG?

The NHS no longer advises that people with symptoms of Covid-19 take a test, unless they want to do so.

If you feel unwell or have a high temperature, health authorities advise you to try and stay home and avoid contact with people until you feel better.

They also recommend avoiding contact with vulnerable people, like those undergoing chemotherapy or the elderly, for at least 10 days.

Sports.title: Eagle-eyed fans fear Bruno Fernandes has ‘given up’ on Man Utd after spotting in-game moment & him storming out ground

BRUNO FERNANDES could not hide his frustration after Manchester United threw away a one-goal lead against ten-man Tottenham in the depths of injury-time.

Bryan Mbeumo found the back of the net with 20 minutes on the clock, but ultimately saw his efforts cancelled out by Dominic Solanke‘s 92nd-minute goal.



The Portugal international was clearly vexed as he was the first to storm out of ground after the 1-1 draw, uncharacteristically ignoring the waiting fans.

And some are wondering whether Fernandes is thinking about throwing in the towel.



To make matters worse, a huge ruckus burst on the touchline, seeing Rodrigo Bentancur sent off and Luke Shaw escaping with just a yellow.

But as a sea of red shirts rushed into the melee, Fernandes opted to sit down away from the drama in a pool of pity.



It was not the night for the 32-year-old, who took 23 minutes to complete his FIRST pass against the north London side.

And unfortunately for the Red Devils, they needed more than Mbeumo slotting it home to beat Roberto De Zerbi‘s men.

Solanke outmuscled Lisandro Martinez in the area to steal a point from Old Trafford as they went 18th, while United went 12th.

The late equaliser means that United have just one win from their total six league games this season.

GAME-CHANGER The rise of digital football collectibles: Everything you need to know







Next

FORGET football stickers or your team’s football shirts – there are new ways to get involved with the beautiful game.

A large fanbase is building around digital collectibles in football.

Think of the football stickers or rare baseball cards that you may have collected in the past.

Platforms such as Crypto.com NFT are bringing this concept into the 21st century by giving fans both an asset and access to exclusive events.



Nicholas Christ, global head of sponsorships at Crypto.com, says: “The idea that the value of a digital collectable is like a piece of art has really been replaced by the concept of utility – what does this asset give you access to?”

Here is what you need to know about digital football collectibles.

What are digital collectibles?

A digital collectible is a non-fungible token (NFT).

It’s basically a Web3 version of a rare baseball card, limited-edition comic book or football sticker.

There are several ways for football fans to engage with digital collectibles, depending on their team and the level of interaction they want to have.

Usually, a club or sporting entity partners with a platform such as Crypto.com NFT to offer digital collectibles.

But Crypto.com NFT has gone further by pairing physical sporting memorabilia with a digital collectible.

This past season, the platform launched a digital collectible programme, turning the silver Crypto.com NFT-branded Champions League Match Coins used for the referee’s coin toss into a fan-focused activation.

Fans could claim a limited supply of digital silver, gold and premium blue coins at different stages of the tournament, giving them an NFT and the chance to access benefits such as matchday prizes.

Christ explains: “We used these hexagonal coins as digital and physical prizes, giving fans the chance to claim an NFT of the official match coin, with the top prize of presenting the physical match coins to the referee on the pitch before their chosen Champions League match, along with two match tickets.”

This culminated in a world-first partnership with Fanatics Collectibles to turn the physical coin from the Champions League Final into a limited edition “Relic” Trading Card, which was handed to one lucky winner.

How can football fans get involved with digital collectibles? The Champions League Final coin is also authenticated on the Cronos Blockchain as a digital collectible, unlocking perks for this upcoming season. This includes tickets for the UEFA Super Cup Final, a League Phase Pass to every single one of your chosen club’s eight games. You can even get the opportunity to deliver the Match Coin at your chosen club’s first game of the season. You can buy, sell and trade these collectibles seamlessly on Crypto.com.

Christ adds: “The popularity increases depending on the scarcity and the utility, and on top of that we’ve attached unique rewards or prizes specific to that digital collectible.

“What we’ve seen when it comes to the sporting collectibles in particular is that it’s a way to increase fan engagement in a match or a sporting event; [it’s] a way for them to feel connected to it and own a part of that experience.”

What can fans do with a digital collectible?

The perks of each digital collectible will be different.

Some have physical prizes or perks attached to them, like exclusive merchandise or VIP experiences, and because it’s on the blockchain, you can hold, sell or trade.

For example, in the 2025/26 NBA season, Crypto.com NFT worked with the Philadelphia 76ers and renowned artist Victor Solomon on the “Heart and Hustle” Collection, commemorating 25 years since the iconic 2000-2001 Eastern Conference Championship season.

With four exclusive drops, fans were able to collect contemporary pieces of art containing historic 76ers memorabilia as both digital and physical collectibles.

One of the drops included custom sneakers designed with authentic game-used basketballs from Hardwood Classic Edition matchups – a special nod to that 25th anniversary.

What are the plans for next season?

Christ adds that we’re nowhere near the final whistle on digital football collectibles.

He says: “We see huge promise in linking physical items with corresponding digital collectibles, and, in certain instances, giving them utility with linked fan rewards – like the Match Coin experience.

“It’s the idea of a tangible connection to a team or an event; being part of a moment or an experience.

“For us it’s about giving global supporters a unique way to own a piece of the match and build a sense of community around an event and a moment in history.”

Sports.title: How Alan Sugar used High Court threat to beat FA in blueprint for Man City’s Premier League battle after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY might want to take a page out of Alan Sugar’s book as they step up their fight with the Premier League.

The club face a likely unprecedented punishment after being found guilty of more than 100 charges of breaking financial regulations.



An independent commission found that, over a nine-year period, City were responsible for substantive rule breaches regarding contracts and payments — including booking £830million in “sham” sponsorship deals.

But more than 30 years ago, when faced with a similar major punishment, then Tottenham chairman and future Apprentice star Sugar, 79, bulldozed the FA with the sort of no-holds-barred approach that would surely appeal to City’s hierarchy.



An FA investigation into alleged illegal payments made by Spurs between 1985 and 1989 — before Sugar bought them — had the club in serious trouble.

According to The Black Book, written by veteran football journalist Harry Harris, the deals included Gary Lineker’s £850,000 move to Japanese outfit Nagoya Grampus Eight.



Sugar believed Tottenham were to receive £4m for the former England captain — not barely 20 per cent of that sum.

While neither Lineker nor his agent Jon Holmes were implicated in any questionable conduct, intermediaries Christian Flood and Yoshio Aoyama had cashed in.

Documents on other deals suggested cash amounting to £400,000 to leading managers and invoices to agents, with suggestions they hid other payments. Sugar’s bitter feud with his manager and co-executive Terry Venables, which ruptured the club, had been at the heart of the issue.

The tech businessman’s determination to run a clean house saw him realising Spurs had been less than upfront — and led to the subsequent High Court case in which Sugar recalled Venables telling him Brian Clough “likes a bung” over the deal for Teddy Sheringham to join Tottenham.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Unsure what he should do, Sugar was persuaded to confess all to the FA, taking the paperwork he had uncovered to the then-headquarters at Lancaster Gate.

But while — three decades later — Chelsea’s admissions of guilt over illegal payments made under Roman Abramovich saw the club’s new owners escape with a £10m fine, Sugar’s honesty backfired. Tottenham were fined £600,000, booted out of the 1994-95 FA Cup and deducted 12 points.

Sugar and Spurs appealed, which saw the fine more than doubled to £1.5m — although they were given six points back and reinstated into the FA Cup.

Gerry Francis’ team went on to lose an Elland Road semi-final against Everton. But that was not enough for Sugar, who had basically declared war on the suits.



Sugar, like Chelsea more than 30 years later, argued the misconduct had been under a previous regime and that his full cooperation had been ignored.

Threatening to take the FA to the High Court and engaging hotshot City lawyers Herbert Smith, Sugar challenged the FA’s right to impose the punishment.

Spooked by that threat, Lancaster Gate chiefs buckled and agreed to an independent arbitration process. On December 9, 1994, the tribunal — which saw the Amstrad tycoon taking direct charge of the defence — ruled firmly in the club’s favour.

It said the charges had been “misconceived, bad in law and should not have been proceeded with… and it was irrational to impose any penalty other than a fine”.



For Sugar it was vindication and victory, with the FA’s own regulations proven to be clearly inadequate. The now Lord Sugar being “hired” by City to help their battle with the Prem — with potential High Court action on the table — is unlikely.

Any such case would see all the evidence from both sides played out in public in open court, with City legal beaks likely to question the validity of the Prem’s rules and regulations.

One potential avenue would be the rules that allow “shareholder loans” from owners at favourable rates until 2024 and the previous Associated Party Transaction regulations that were amended after a City legal challenge.

Likewise, the deals that allowed Chelsea and Aston Villa to “sell” their women’s teams, plus other transactions involving stadiums and training grounds that were allowed under Prem rules — but not in Uefa Financial Fair Play calculations — could also be brought up.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Should City prevail, the costs, running well north of £100m — plus any compensation awards to the club — would be split between the 20 top-flight clubs.

For more than 50 years, Fleet Street legend Harry Harris was inside the stories that made the biggest football headlines. Now, in his landmark 100th book, he reveals what really happened. The Black Book: Secrets from the Heart of Football is available now on pre-order.

Sports.title: Jordan Pickford faces England fight as David Seaman fires warning despite Everton’s hunt for fourth-straight clean sheet

JORDAN PICKFORD is facing the fight of his career to keep his England shirt.

The Everton stopper, 32, heads into Sunday’s Premier League showdown against Hull City aiming for a fourth-straight clean sheet in all competitions for the Blues.



Throw in another two for the Three Lions over the international break and you could be forgiven for thinking his spot as the country’s No1 was assured.

But the 93-capped star’s international place is under threat for the first time in almost a decade after he was benched twice for his country in favour of James Trafford over the past three weeks.



With England boss Thomas Tuchel watching his every move — and Leeds’ Trafford breathing down his neck — Pickford cannot afford any slip-ups at the MKM Stadium.

And legendary Three Lions ‘keeper David Seaman says the Everton stalwart MUST perform under the intense heat of competition if he wants to be Tuchel’s first-choice come Euro 2028.

Speaking via Betway, Seaman said: “That’s going to be close. When you look at Jordan and what he’s done for England, you’re not really expecting him to be left out.

“But James is going to be pushing him now, and this is what he needs.

“Now Trafford’s playing for Leeds regularly, and he’s been given the nod by Tuchel to show that he trusts him against the world champions Spain.

“That was a massive boost of confidence for James Trafford. We saw a goalkeeper that’s very capable of performing at that level.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I’m 50/50, if I’m honest, and that’s because of how highly I rate James Trafford.

“Jordan’s level is up there because of what he’s doing for England, and he’s now doing it more regularly for Everton as well.

“It wasn’t his best World Cup, he knows that, but he’s still got all that experience. Now it’s about seeing how he can perform when there’s a real contender.”

Sports.title: Under-pressure Burnham urged to come clean about ALL his dealings with Man City & their UAE owners
Sports.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham has been urged to come clean about all his dealings with Manchester City and their UAE owners.

The PM is facing pressure to publish all correspondence and financial links to the club, found guilty of widespread cheating.



It comes after the ex-Manchester mayor was accused of “political interference” by saying he would be “really concerned” to lose City’s owners.

He later clarified, saying: “It’s important to separate the football issues from wider investment.”



The Tories have written to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy demanding the Government is “open and honest” about its involvement in the case.

This includes disclosing all contact with Man City and its owners and any relevant correspondence with the Independent Football Regulator.

It comes after The Sun revealed Labour politicians received nearly £300,000 of freebies from the UAE and City.

Deputy leader Lucy Powell, whose constituency covers City’s Etihad Stadium, got tickets to five matches worth £2,360.

Louie French, shadow sports minister, wants to know all financial links with ministers or advisers.

He also called for all details published about a meeting between City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds at No10 last month.



The PM’s City links go back to 2018 when he attended the opening of a club office in China.

City deny breaking Prem financial rules and have launched an appeal.

Mr French said they had “sincere concerns” about perceived Government interference in the process, calling the PM’s comments “highly inappropriate”.

Sports.title: Burnham must come clean about EVERY government contract with Man City – then stay out of football
Sports.content:
Next

KEEPING politics and Government out of sport is a belief that unites the vast majority of the public, regardless of football or political allegiances.

When news first broke that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges and were likely to appeal via their small army of lawyers, my first instinct was, “This is going to get very messy for English football so do not make it worse by providing a quote to a journalist.”



The vast majority of MPs were of the same opinion, no doubt because we are also warned to avoid commenting on live legal cases.

So why was the Prime Minister so keen to get involved and defend City?



Within a day of the verdict, he was on the BBC saying how worried he would be to lose City’s owners — ignoring the widespread concerns and the millions of fans who believe in fair play and healthy competition.

He appeared to find a new spirit of the blues, but why?

The Premier League says the independent commission found City inflated their accounts by more than £900million over nine seasons.

City deny it, and that is for the appeal process to settle.

For decades, the global success of the Premier League and EFL has seen vast sums flood into English football, attracting the best players and a new generation of international owners.

But this success has also attracted a renewed focus on the long-term sustainability of club finances, with the leagues implementing new spending rules to try to ensure fairness and healthy competition on the pitch.



It is no surprise, then, that other Premier League clubs were astonished by the Prime Minister’s remarks and fear political interference in the appeal.

Days before news of the verdict broke, City’s chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak reportedly held a private meeting with the Business Secretary in Downing Street, wearing his other hat as boss of Abu Dhabi’s sovereign wealth fund.

In recent years, investment from Abu Dhabi has helped transform great swathes of Manchester while Mr Burnham was Mayor.



Then there is the regulator, which may yet have to decide whether City’s owners are fit and proper people to run the club.

Its chairman, David Kogan, is a Labour donor who backed both Lisa Nandy and Keir Starmer — a link ministers later had to apologise for failing to declare.

I want to be clear that none of this proves anyone has done anything wrong.

But taken together, it raises questions that any fair-minded fan would want answered.

That is why I have written to Lisa Nandy, who has served as Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport since 2024, demanding that her department publish every financial link or exchange it has had regarding Manchester City and its owners, across Whitehall and with the regulator.



I have also asked whether the Government has taken legal advice on the regulator’s ability to judge this case fairly, if required, given the impact of its political links and Andy Burnham’s inappropriate comments on perceptions of natural justice.

Put in footballing terms, this is a VAR review to help improve transparency and ensure the Government is not involved in any foul play, which would make this difficult situation for football even worse.

The Prime Minister promised to do politics differently, and the first test of that promise is honesty.

Mr Burnham was never elected Prime Minister by the country, but he answers to it all the same.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If everything is above board, publishing the paperwork costs him nothing, yet every day he dodges the questions, the smell grows stronger and football’s reputation suffers.



The Prime Minister must now come clean and stay out of football.

Sports.title: 'Man City must've kicked themselves when I joined Liverpool - I was better than players there'
Sports.content:
'Man City must've kicked themselves when I joined Liverpool - I was better than players there'

This ex-Liverpool star opened up about his move from Manchester City to the Reds

View 3 Images Kolo Toure joined Liverpool in 2013 (Image: 2016 Getty Images)

Former Liverpool defender Kolo Toure previously admitted that Manchester City would have "kicked themselves" over their decision to let him join the Reds. Liverpool will face City on Sunday in the Premier League, with Toure leaving the Etihad for Anfield in 2013.

‌



‌



The defender, who was part of Arsenal's 'Invincibles' squad, left north London for Manchester for £14million in 2009. He helped City secure the 2011/12 Premier League title.

‌



However, in his last two years at City, Toure found himself falling down the pecking order behind the likes of Joleon Lescott and Matija Nastasic. The Ivory Coast star was not offered a new contract at Eastlands and departed on a free to Liverpool.

‌



After joining the Reds, Toure, now 45, insisted he was better than the players who had usurped him in Manchester. "I was better than certain players at Manchester City, but I was left on the bench," Toure told The Sun.

"Before I left the club, I told the people in charge that they would regret letting me go. People said I was finished and that I could never get back to my former level. But now I am at Liverpool - and I am sure that City must be kicking themselves when they see how I am performing."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Jarell Quansah opens up on competing with Trent Alexander-Arnold for England place READ MORE :

Toure compared his situation to the issue his brother, Yaya, faced after his move from Barcelona to City in 2010. "I have had a similar experience to Yaya," Kolo said.

"Managers come to clubs bringing players with them, and they want to pick them at all costs - whether they are any good or not. Yaya was much better than Sergio Busquets at Barcelona. But he was behind him in the pecking order, and he found that hard to accept."

View 3 Images Kolo Toure said City would have "kicked themselves" for letting him go (Image: Getty Images)

‌



In a 2015 interview with LFCTV, Toure reflected on his switch to Merseyside. He said: "I was at the end of my contract at City and I wanted to still play in the UK, because the way I finished at City for me wasn't right. I knew that I could keep doing something.

"I received a phone call from [Brendan Rodgers]. For me, when he spoke to me and he told me that he was considering me to come to the club, I was like 'wow'. To be able to play at Arsenal, City and now Liverpool was amazing and I thank God again.

"I could have maybe gone to Turkey or other places but when Brendan told me to come to Liverpool I was so happy, because I knew I could come here and do something and help this great football club. This was another chance to bounce back. What a perfect club to bounce back for me."

‌



View 3 Images Toure claimed Liverpool was a "perfect" club for him (Image: 2013 Getty Images)

The ex-defender spent three years at Liverpool before leaving in 2016. He later returned to City to work as an assistant coach to Pep Guardiola in 2025.

Sports.content:
Man City are in the centre of a major Premier League charges storm

Manchester City are back in Premier League action for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules

Hello and welcome to The Mirror's live blog on Saturday, October 10, as Premier League action returns following the extended international break.

Manchester City are set to return to the pitch for the first time since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The club have already launched an appeal after an Independent Commission found them guilty of 114 out of 115 charges relating to the period between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

The allegations include claims that more than £830million in owner funding was used to inflate the club’s revenues through so-called 'sham' agreements. Speculation continues to mount over the potential sanctions City could face, with possible punishments ranging from a substantial fine and points deduction to the prospect of expulsion from the Premier League.

"Personally, I'm very calm to be honest," said Maresca. "The club has been quite clear. We trust completely the club.

"We understand the noise, but the focus for us is just what we can control and we can control just the football side."

Sports.title: 'I played for Man City and Liverpool - it's clear which is the bigger club'
Sports.content:
'I played for Man City and Liverpool - it's clear which is the bigger club'

The Premier League icon represented both teams but claims he knows which one is the bigger club

View 3 Images James Milner has enjoyed a trophy-laden career (Image: Getty Images)

Former Liverpool star James Milner previously admitted that the Reds are a bigger club than Manchester City. Milner played for City between 2010 and 2015 and at Liverpool from 2015 to 2023.

‌



‌



Sunday afternoon will see Milner's two former clubs, Liverpool and City, face off at Anfield. The midfielder left the Etihad at the end of his contract in 2015, after winning two Premier League titles, an FA Cup and a Capital One Cup in his time with the Blues.

‌



Milner, who retired from football in June at the age of 40, says he made the transfer to ensure maximum playing time. Speaking in 2015, he said: “It’s a huge club and Man City, maybe over the course of history, isn’t as quite as big as Liverpool.

‌



“At this moment in time, City are doing very well and expected to win trophies. The set-up is all there. I had a lot of conversations with the hierarchy at City and they never said a bad word about me. It was just their opinions on where I fitted in.

“They saw me as a big part of the club. However, when we come to it, getting to finals and things like that, the default was for me not to play. That was the way it is and I want to play as much as I can and look back on my career.

“I could have easily stayed at City and been there another four or five years helping them win things. But over the next few years I wouldn’t have played as much and my game time would have reduced.

"When I’m older I want to look back and say that I became the best player I could. I thought at times at City I won player of the month and then didn’t play for three, four or five games after. I feel here if I play well, I’ll keep the shirt. It’s down to me.”

Upon joining Liverpool, he made it clear that the club's size appealed to him. He said: “Obviously the club does not need selling. It’s a massive club globally, with the history. But I spoke to the manager [then Brendan Rodgers] about his plans for the team and for myself. He knew a lot about me.

Sports.content:
Adam Johnson proposes to girlfriend who got back with disgraced ex-pro after prison stint

The shamed former footballer and his partner rekindled their relationship and are set to marry

View 4 Images Adam Johnson leaving Bradford Crown Court with his girlfriend Stacey Flounders (Image: Daily Mirror)

Disgraced football star Adam Johnson is engaged to his partner. Seven years after spending time away in prison, he is now planning his wedding.

‌



‌



The former Manchester City and Sunderland winger was jailed in 2016. He served three years of his six-year sentence for grooming and sexual activity with a 15-year-old girl.

‌



The former star has proposed to long-time partner Stacey Flounders. Flounders initially broke off the relationship with Johnson shortly after he was charged with his offence.

‌



An insider told The Sun: “Stacey and her inner circle have put Adam’s time behind bars well behind them and are really excited for the next chapter of their lives. Their family and friends are over the moon for them and wedding planning is in full swing.

“They’ve been through a lot as a family and this feels like the perfect way to leave the memory of the hard times in the past and focus on a happy future with their two kids.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Every Man City player Roy Keane wants to throw out medals after damning 115 charges verdict READ MORE :

Flounders, 36, was pregnant with the pair's daughter, Ayla, in 2014, as Johnson began contact with the teenage girl. They ended their union ahead of his court case when Johnson confessed to cheating with at least 12 other women.

Court details revealed that Johnson and the girl had exchanged 834 WhatsApp messages and that the girl had informed Johnson that she was in Year 10 at school. Information about their meetings and sexual activity in his car was also made public.

View 4 Images Stacey Flounders got back with Johnson in 2020 (Image: PA)

‌



After being released from Prison, Johnson said: “I am very sorry for the effect my conduct had on those directly and indirectly involved. It should never have happened and I deeply regret what I did.

“I now want to concentrate on the future and want to demonstrate through my actions that I am committed to repaying them for their support.”

Flounders and Johnson are believed to have rekindled their relationship in 2020 and welcomed their second child a year later. The former air hostess said she didn't believe he was a paedophile, telling the Daily Mail in 2019 that he was a sex addict.

‌



View 4 Images The couple are planning their wedding (Image: Getty Images)

She said: “To be honest, I don't see Adam as a paedophile. For me, a paedophile is somebody who abuses tiny young children. I think that he was a sex addict. He told me he was a sex addict.”

After he was released, it didn't look as though they were going to get back together, but the pandemic struck a year after he got out and that gradually changed things.

‌



During his time at City, Johnson lived in a £4million mansion that previously belonged to Cristiano Ronaldo and earned £80,000 per week. While the premature end of his football career is believed to have cost him around £10m in earnings and sponsorship deals, he had already made enough to be financially secure for life.

View 4 Images Adam Johnson, pictured in 2010 playing for Manchester City (Image: 2010 Getty Images)

Having previously lived in a £1.8m six-bedroom property in a private community, they downsized to a £470,000 home. It's believed that Johnson doesn't work and has been spotted playing golf at his local club.

Article continues below

An unnamed family member told the Mail: “Money will have played a part. He hasn't worked since he ended his football career. He put away enough money during his playing career that they can live a very good lifestyle without worrying. They have a nice life, the children won't want for anything.”

Sports.title: 'People say my dead dad's still alive – I block out conspiracies as I seek England career'
Sports.content:
'People say my dead dad's still alive – I block out conspiracies as I seek England career'

One of Manchester City's rising stars has endured quite the journey in his footballing career

View 3 Images Lakyle Samuel currently plays for Exeter City (Image: Newcastle United via Getty Image)

Lakyle Samuel isn't letting conspiracies surrounding his father's death stop him from achieving his ultimate dream. The Manchester City academy graduate, who signed on loan for Exeter City this season, is the son of the late former Aston Villa star Jlloyd Samuel.

‌



‌



Jlloyd enjoyed an eight-year career at Villa Park before various stints across England, Wales and Iran led to his return to the UK as a player-manager for the Cheshire-based side Egerton.

‌



His time with the club was brutally cut short in May 2018 when he died in a car crash. The former defender's Range Rover had collided with a van, leaving his vehicle ablaze. Years after his passing, the circumstances surrounding the latter years of his life and his tragic death remain ominous.

‌



After departing Bolton Wanderers in 2011, Jlloyd joined Iranian side Esteghal and reportedly married a second wife and converted to Islam without his family's knowledge. His second spouse, a fashion designer named Helia Sahimi, insists that the former footballer is in fact alive - a belief held by Jlloyd's sister, Leslie-Ann.

Jlloyd's death came just hours after taking his children, including Lakyle, to school. The footballer opened up about his memories of spending time with his father in a wide-ranging interview with the Daily Mail. The 20-year-old said: "I've got memories of playing football in the garden with dad, him doing drills with me in the hallway.

Man Utd eye JJ Gabriel reconciliation with new contract offer amid under £1m exit nightmare READ MORE :

"He's influenced me a lot. My mum tells me what he did in the past. I just want to be the best person I can be. He was a great person to a lot of people. They say he was the life of the party, and whenever I meet someone who knew him, they speak really highly of him.

‌



"I take that on. I always want to be a bubbly character and as nice as possible." Lakyle has made a bright start to what is a burgeoning career, having already trained with the England and Man City senior teams. He possesses a clear goal in mind and admitted that the conspiracies about his father are something he blocks out.

View 3 Images The former footballer's son has had to contend with claims that his father is still alive (Image: Instagram)

He added: "I just hope he's proud. I've given a lot to get where I am, especially going through that. It's tough to deal with. I just try and block it out (conspiracies about him). It doesn't have much to do with my life.

‌



"I've had my experiences with him and if other people want to say other stuff, I'm not too bothered. I've had what I've had with him and it's not going to change my point of view on him. He gave us a really good upbringing. He’s dad, innit?"

Lakyle - who plays for England's U20 side - cited the advice he's received from Kyle Walker on how to become a better defender and explained how his experience training with the Three Lions came about. The right-back said: "Kyle Walker was a really good role model.

View 3 Images Lakyle Samuel has his heart set on playing for England (Image: Frankie OKeeffe/PPAUK/Shutterstock)

‌



"He told me some key details on defensive body shape. The level of detail Pep (Guardiola) goes into is mad. It raises your game because you have to be on it. I'd go and train with them quite a bit. Last October, England came calling."

The defender was on duty with the U20s when Thomas Tuchel was in need of extra players in training. "I only knew about half an hour before!" he revealed. "The tempo of the session was high because they're the best players in the country. I didn't feel I did too bad! I was really proud to have that experience."

Lakyle's first foray into the professional game last year came with League Two side Bromley, and he has returned to the fourth tier with Exeter City this season. Expectations are high on the youngster, who certainly has lofty ambitions for himself.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola forced to defend second player as Reds ready to raid Prem rival
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola forced to defend second player as Reds ready to raid Prem rival

Liverpool news as Andoni Iraola speaks up for one of his players ahead of the showdown with Manchester City

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is without some key players for the Manchester City game (Image: Getty Images)

The eyes of English football will be on Anfield on Sunday as Liverpool prepare to face Manchester City. The sides have been involved in some titanic, often title-deciding, battles in recent times.

‌



‌



However, there hasn't been a build-up quite like this after City were found guilty of breaking 114 Premier League regulations, raising questions over their last 15 years of success, when the Reds were so often the bridesmaids.

‌



Potential punishments include expulsion from the Premier League, a points deduction and even the removal of titles, which, in theory, could see the Reds' tally of 20 league crowns increase retrospectively.

‌



For now, Andoni Iraola's side simply have to focus on facing the side sitting at the top of the Premier League with maximum points from five games. Ahead of the big match, here's the latest Reds news…

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Iraola defends another star

Iraola has rejected suggestions that summer signing Bradley Barcola is struggling for form after the forward was criticised for his France performances. The 24-year-old received some brutal reviews after Monday's 4-1 Nations League win over Belgium.

‌



Piers Morgan and Jamie Carragher’s social media row IN FULL as Liverpool icon hits back READ MORE :

With his two senior forwards, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo, both absent with injury for the Man City game, Iraola needs Barcola to deliver the kind of display he regularly produced for PSG.

The Reds boss said: "I don't think he's in a bad moment. The problem with wingers or strikers is if they don’t score a goal, 'They haven’t played well.' We have to see the games, we have to watch. I said it the first game against Atletico Madrid, he missed two or three quite clear chances. I don't care, honestly.

"I care but I want him to see [it's] there. With the national team, I have seen he has had a couple of good situations to score. He hasn’t scored, but I want him to be there."

‌



His defence of Barcola comes just a month after he did similar with Florian Wirtz amid the German's continued struggles to live up to his price tag.

View 3 Images Liverpool need a big performance from Bradley Barcola (Image: Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images)

Reds ready to pounce

Liverpool are among a flurry of clubs being credited with an interest in Nottingham Forest's Murillo. The Brazilian has established himself as one of the Premier League's most reliable centre-backs.

‌



As a result, he finds himself on the radar of numerous leading clubs. According to TeamTalk, Liverpool, Manchester United and Chelsea are keen on the 24-year-old, who has made more than 100 appearances since joining Forest from Corinthians in 2023.

View 3 Images Nottingham Forest's Murillo is attracting attention (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Having signed a new contract in the summer, tying him to the City Ground until 2030, Murillo would carry a hefty price tag and a January departure would reportedly require an 'exceptional offer.' But with Virgil van Dijk in the latter stages of his storied career, the Reds will be looking to future-proof their defence.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick disagrees with Sky Sports pundit's Man Utd claim after blowing win vs Tottenham
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick disagrees with Sky Sports pundit's Man Utd claim after blowing win vs Tottenham

Manchester United could only manage a draw against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford with the Red Devils now said to be lacking confidence

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has questions to answer (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

Michael Carrick was left to bat away suggestions that Manchester United's slow start against Tottenham was due to a lack of confidence, as they drew at Old Trafford. The Red Devils gave up a 1-0 lead against the Lilywhites as the match ended all square, with accusations that Carrick's team are without self-belief.

‌



‌



The United boss witnessed boos at both the half-time and full-time whistle as his team continued their disappointing start to the season. The club picked up their sixth Premier League point of the season as they failed to hold on against their 10-man opponents, their lowest tally after four matches for 40 years.

‌



With the hosts leading 1-0, Rodrigo Bentancur received his marching orders after headbutting Luke Shaw, yet United couldn't see out the victory as Dominic Solanke struck a late leveller. That saw some fierce criticism after the match.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Redknapp delivered a damning verdict on the Premier League's 12th-placed side, slamming the team's organisation. He added that the team's lack of confidence is an issue that Carrick does not have the required squad to deliver the results expected of the club.

"Brighton in the Carabao Cup, 2-0 up and lose 3-2, that is unprecedented and does not happen at Old Trafford, except it does with this team," Redknapp vented.

‌



"I do not see enough connections in that midfield and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back and Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is just a theme this season.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick does not believe confidence was an issue in United's slow start (Image: Shaun Brooks - CameraSport via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"Their energy levels are not good enough and they look loose going forward, there was no real structure. The squad is not good or strong enough and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect."

While Carrick was frustrated with the result, he did not think confidence caused United to start the game slowly. "I don't think it is lack of confidence," he said after the match.

"But a game can get away from you very quickly. We found a way right back into the game, and got ourselves in a great position - that is one of the most disappointing things."

Article continues below

When questioned about the boos directed at his team, he said: "It's not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment. The reality is what it is; we need to get back to winning games."

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho embarrassed and Vinicius Jr sent off in incredible Real Madrid hair pull drama
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho embarrassed and Vinicius Jr sent off in incredible Real Madrid hair pull drama

Real Madrid ace Vinicius Junior went mad after being shown a red card for pulling their hair of his opponent and seeing his goal cancelled out against Villarreal

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr saw his goal ruled out and he was sent off for a hair pull (Image: La Liga live)

Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior was shown a red card for an audacious hair pull and had a goal ruled out in the process. The Brazilian winger looked to have silenced his haters after getting on the scoresheet, having been booed onto the pitch by Villarreal supporters.

‌



‌



Vinicius entered the fray early in the second half before getting on the scoresheet after 72 minutes. Jubilant scenes followed as the Brazilian enthusiastically celebrated with Jude Bellingham and boss Jose Mourinho.

‌



The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager had even gone racing down the sideline, such was his joy. Both his and Vinicius' moods soon changed as VAR intervened and fury emerged.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The video assistant referee spotted the 26-year-old pulling the hair of Villarreal ace Nathan Saliba as he raced into the opposition half, while Bellingham was in possession of the ball out wide. The England international ultimately provided his team-mate with the ball to double Los Blancos' lead but it was all for nought.

Instead of adding to his goal tally, Vinicius was eventually given his marching orders, provoking a furious reaction as he practically chased referee Isidro Díaz de Mer before leaving the field. It marked the first time VAR had overturned a goal and provided a red card simultaneously

‌



The decision meant that Real were required to defend a one-goal lead with 10 men, which they managed successfully. Yann Diomande made the important contribution after the summer signing started ahead of Vinicius.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr celebrated with Jose Mourinho following his disallowed goal (Image: Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr was furious to be shown red (Image: Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

‌



Real Madrid TV has already broadcast their frustration with the referee's performance. "You can call it a foul by Vinicius, but the problem arises when this VAR referee hasn't called for the red card shown to Carlos Romero in the match against Espanyol for two seasons," says Real Madrid TV.

Referee Pablo González Fuertes revealed that his colleague made the right decision to send off the Real Madrid star, however. Speaking on Radio Marca, He said: ""A correct sending-off because it was a very blatant hair-pull on Saliba.

"It was violent conduct on the part of the Real Madrid forward. And, logically, the goal was correctly disallowed."

Article continues below

Depending on the referee's report, Vinicius could now miss the Clasico against Barcelona in two weeks.

Sports.title: Carrick must share burden of Man Utd's failings with his players
Sports.content:
"We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game. With the ball, without the ball, we were off it." A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.

Stuck in the mire of Manchester United's worst start to a league season for 40 years, the manager appeared lost for legitimate reasons. His margin for error is shrinking by the week.

Why were his side outplayed at home by the Premier League's bottom club? Why can't they hold onto leads? Why do they seem incapable of playing against 10 men?

Image: Michael Carrick looks on during Man Utd's draw with Tottenham

All of these are fair questions to put to the man himself and many were asked of Carrick in the wake of Saturday's 1-1 draw with Spurs. None were answered with enough detail to satisfy, though, only really serving to hold a mirror up to what was delivered on the pitch: inadequacy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United's match against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League

Clearly the manager can only accept so much of the blame. His players are yet to offer a single complete performance, only bit-part displays of individualism and self-direction. Where is the cohesiveness that shaped the backend of last year? What happened to the clarity that transformed a broken season into a third-place finish?

Fans who turn up to Old Trafford every week are back to being unsure. They do not know what to expect from one game to the next, only how to voice their dissatisfaction at what transpires. Three separate choruses of boos could be heard from the terraces on Saturday.

"I think the fans will stay with the project," reflected Gary Neville from Old Trafford. "I don't think the boos are against Michael Carrick for one minute. But what I would say is, they're turning quite quickly."

When United needed a calm voice to steer the ship at the beginning of this year, they turned to a man whose entire playing career was built on it. That version of Manchester United feels far removed from the side that have begun this season, though.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville feels the midfield partnership of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo lacks dynamism and is not suited to the Premier League

In midfield is where the problems are most evident. And yet, that is the department that received the biggest injection of cash this summer, a complete overhaul in terms of personnel and profiles. The Kobbie Mainoo-Youri Tielemans axis is not working. Andrey Santos is barely getting a look in.

Hopes that Carlos Baleba can hit the ground running after an injury-hit start were audible; his introduction after an hour lifted the whole stadium. Almost every touch was positive and he took care of the ball, completing 16 of 18 passes and creating as many chances as Bruno Fernandes managed all game (2).

Still, the space and freedom with which Spurs operated presents issues that cannot be solved by one midfielder. United were carved open time after time, gaps appearing in a myriad of ways. The visitors were able to win possession in the final third five times in the first half alone. Five of United's work-shy starters did not go away for international duty over the break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dominic Solanke snatched a late equaliser for 10-man Spurs

And it was not just the aggressiveness of Spurs' press that was effective. They picked holes in United with the ball, too, using slick one-touch combinations to move through the thirds with pace and purpose. Savio attempted 10 dribbles. He only completed half but the recurrence was evidence of his belief that United could be got at. He was right.

Then there are concerns over the mentality of a side who repeatedly fail to beat 10 men. Yet again, United were outrun and outpaced - this time by a team who played with a man less for 21 minutes, including stoppage time.

"If we're ahead in the game, we have to see it out," says Carrick. That much is obvious. What is less clear is how some of these patterns of missteps are going to be addressed.

"Football is character," concluded opposition boss Roberto De Zerbi. United are lacking exactly that. They must summon some resolve from somewhere, or risk being eaten up by the competition. Because if the last few weeks have taught us anything, it's that the Premier League is in no mood to be doling out sympathy.

Sports.title: Van Gerwen dumped out of Swiss Darts Trophy as nightmare year goes on
Sports.content:
Michael van Gerwen's nightmare year went from bad to worse as he was dumped out of the Swiss Darts Trophy in his opening match by Mensur Suljovic 6-4 on Saturday night.

Suljovic led 5-2 before Van Gerwen threatened a comeback but three missed darts to force a decider allowed Suljovic to take advantage.

It was Suljovic's fourth straight win over Van Gerwen and the fifth time in six tournaments that the Dutchman has exited after one match.

Van Gerwen's woes continue

Defeat in Basel marks the first time Michael van Gerwen has lost his opening match in FOUR European Tour events in the same season since its inception in 2012



European Darts Trophy ❌



German Darts Grand Prix ❌



Flanders Darts Trophy ❌



Swiss Darts Trophy ❌



Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Colin Lloyd discusses Van Gerwen's ongoing struggles

Luke Humphries, Gian van Veen and Jonny Clayton all advanced to Finals Day as ten seeds crashed out on a remarkable day of action in Basel.

Newly crowned World Grand Prix champion Humphries was among the headline acts on Day Two at the St. Jakobshalle, where he prevailed against Kevin Doets.

Despite racing 3-0 ahead with 122 and 121 checkouts, Humphries was forced to survive a furious fightback from Doets, defying the Dutchman's 105.64 average to triumph in a breathless decider.

"I was really pleased with that performance," reflected Humphries, who averaged almost 103 and pinned 67% of his attempts at double.

"I felt like I was the better player for most of the game, but Kevin was really strong at the end there, so I had to really work my socks off."

European Champion Van Veen also impressed on Swiss soil, producing a hat-trick of ton-plus checkouts to whitewash a shell-shocked Niko Springer in just under ten minutes.

Clayton, meanwhile, stole the show with an irrepressible display against Maik Kuivenhoven, averaging 108.81 and landing two bullseye finishes to kick off his title bid in style.

The Welshman will take on Rob Cross for a place in the quarter-finals, after the former world champion halted Luke Woodhouse's mid-match fightback to close out a battling 6-4 victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Stephen Bunting looks back on that viral interview with Raymond van Barneveld at Ally Pally

There will be a new champion crowned at the St Jakobshalle on Sunday evening, as former champions Stephen Bunting and Martin Schindler crashed out on a day of upsets in Basel.

Swedish star Jeffrey de Graaf put in a clinical display of doubling to account for reigning champion Bunting, while Schindler was swept aside by Tom Bissell, who will feature at Finals Day for the first time in his European Tour career.

Dirk van Duijvenbode recorded a fifth straight win against James Wade to end the left-hander's bid for back-to-back European Tour titles, and a resurgent Michael Smith now awaits the Dutchman in the last 16.

The 2023 world champion delivered one of his best performances of the year to seal a 6-4 against Jermaine Wattimena, converting consecutive 116, 124 and 144 checkouts in the process.

Smith averaged just shy of 103 to cap off a quality display, which also preserves his hopes of qualifying for the Machineseeker European Championship later this month.

Sports.title: NFL Gameday Guide: Jags and Eagles land in London
Sports.content:
The Jacksonville Jaguars return to London this week to play what will mark their 15th and 16th regular-season games in England's capital since 2013, featuring as part of the league's 44th and 45th games in the UK since 2007 as well as a record slate of nine international matchups in 2026.

It will see Jags punter Logan Cooke play in an NFL-record 10th international game to surpass former Jacksonville offensive lineman Tyler Shatley, per ESPN stats.

But this has a different feel to that of the Jags teams from years gone by, who have monopolised London without ever truly inserting themselves among football's Super Bowl contenders. The 2017 team that stunned the NFL to reach the AFC Championship Game, perhaps, being the exception to that rule.

This time they arrive to take on the Philadelphia Eagles behind a true MVP candidate in Trevor Lawrence and a head coach in Liam Coen knocking on the door of the elite. It is not a team brimming with star names, but instead an expertly-drilled reflection of their coach's vision for contention.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Philadelphia Eagles at the Chicago Bears from Week 3 of the NFL season

The Jags are 3-1 and purring at the top of the AFC South, their one blemish a defeat to the Denver Broncos in which they can been control before letting the game slip away.

Momentum is on their side after back-to-back statement wins over the New England Patriots and Cincinnati Bengals, in contrast to an opponent battling to steady a ship rocked by injury, retirement and consecutive losses. There is an overwhelming case of deja vu for the Eagles, whose soaring expectations can occasionally make for a gloomier fan outlook than is actually the case.

The last time the Eagles faced the Jaguars, Saquon Barkley conjured one of the greatest plays in NFL history with his reverse hurdle over Jacksonville cornerback Jarrian Jones back in November 2024.

"Everybody DM'd me like I'm supposed to be mad or something," Jones said on Wednesday. "I don't give a damn. He made a good play. It is what it is."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Eagles running back Saquon Barkley hurdle a defender backwards in an incredible play from last season

Barkley's availability for Sunday is in doubt after the running back exited Week Four's defeat to the Los Angeles Rams with a hamstring injury. The Eagles had already been missing leading wide receiver DeVonta Smith due to a hamstring issue, the former Heisman Trophy winner having become Jalen Hurts' unequivocal top target this offseason following the marquee departure of AJ Brown.

This week meanwhile saw stalwart offensive tackle Lane Johnson announce his shock retirement to focus on his mental health, before center Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. What's more, wide receiver Hollywood Brown, edge rusher Jonathan Greenard and linebacker Jihaad Campbell all missed practice this week through injury.

On paper, it is a decimated Eagles team so far failing to demonstrate the kind of offensive resurgence expected under Sean Mannion after he replaced Kevin Patullo as offensive coordinator in the offseason. Philly's offense enters Sunday's game at Tottenham averaging the fourth-fewest yards per game, second-fewest passing yards per game, 26th in scoring and 29th in EPA/play.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jason Bell believes Trevor Lawrence is showing a 'maturity' that has changed 'everything' for the Jacksonville Jaguars

Jalen Hurts also continues to be one of the most divisive quarterbacks in football as critics wrestle over his true value, who is suffering in a system lacking serious punch on the ground and the consistent presence of a Brown on the outside - with the greatest of respect to the always-reliable hands of Smith.

The Jags have their identity. The Eagles are still searching desperately for theirs.

Nick Sirianni's side have elected to fly in just 36 hours before kickoff in London, following a similar plan to that of Sean McVay and the Los Angeles Rams when they travelled in on the eve of their dominant win over the Jaguars at Wembley.

Sports.title: Neville's Man Utd warning: 'Get a grip or face worrying few weeks'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville warned Manchester United could be in for a "worrying few weeks" if their players don't "get a grip" on their season after they were booed in their draw with Tottenham.

Michael Carrick's side's poor start to the campaign continued as Dominic Solanke's 92nd-minute goal rescued a point for the 10-man visitors at Old Trafford on Saturday.

There were boos from the home fans, both at half-time and full-time, as United extended their winless run to four games in all competitions, keeping them 12th in the Premier League.

They now face a daunting run of fixtures, starting with a Champions League away game against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday before Sunday's Premier League trip to Elland Road to face Leeds, live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the game between Man Utd and Spurs

Speaking on The Gary Neville Podcast, Neville questioned the midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo and said the side's plight could worsen if their players do not show improvement.

"Tielemans and Mainoo, I think we've seen enough of it now," Neville said.

"I'm not calling time on it because that's probably too drastic, but I've seen enough to think that's not a midfield that's dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.

"I think they are both good players individually. But sometimes you just have players that don't quite knit together or don't quite suit each other.

"I think when [Carlos] Baleba came on with Mainoo, it looked like there was a lot more energy.

Image: Spurs missed a succession of chances to go ahead before Man Utd's opener

"There's going to have to be something done in there, and the rest of them are going to have to get a grip because they are going to Diego Simeone's Atletico Madrid and Elland Road.

"If you're not quite right there from a mental and physical perspective, you're going to get found out.

"They've got a couple of days to recover, pick themselves up from this and get going, because if they don't get going it's going to be a worrying few weeks."

'Fans are turning quite quickly'

Neville felt the boos inside Old Trafford were not aimed at head coach Carrick but described the performance as "worrying" and said supporters are picking up on a lack of effort and energy from the players.

"It was worrying because I think the three-week break was the reset moment," he added. "This was the start of a big period of eight games in 28 days.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking after Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Tottenham at Old Trafford, Gary Neville questioned the energy and enthusiasm of Michael Carrick's side

"What I really would have expected today from Manchester United was a really enthusiastic, energetic performance from minute one.

"I didn't see an enthusiastic, energetic performance from those red shirts for an hour, and Spurs should have been three or four-nil up.

"I think the fans will stay with the project. I don't think the boos are against Michael Carrick for one minute. But what I would say is they're turning quite quickly.

"Manchester United fans are incredibly loyal, beyond loyal, to their managers and to their players, but what they won't accept is a lack of energy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville feels the midfield partnership of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo lacks dynamism and is not up to the required standard

"They won't accept a lack of what they deem to be effort. I don't like saying effort but the reality is they're not running enough, they're not showing enough tenacity, determination, fighting spirit. They're just not.

"They booed after 22 minutes, they booed at half-time and they booed at the end. That tells you that they're really despondent with what they're watching.

"My daughter comes and watches every single week. She texted me at half-time, 'What's that?' My daughter's 16 years of age. You can't kid or con a football fan. No matter who they are, they know what they're watching.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United defender Harry Maguire was seen saying 'bye bye' and waving Rodrigo Bentancur off the pitch after his red card

"I don't mind winning here, don't mind losing here, but there's got to be a massive amount of effort and it can't be boring, simple as that.

"You can have a shootout and lose 4-2 and think, 'OK, well at least we saw a Manchester United that went forward with verve and all those things that you'd expect'.

Image: Bryan Mbeumo's goal was cancelled out by Dominic Solanke

"But what we're seeing at the moment is a team that looks like they're curling up in a ball. For some of them right now, it looks like the club is getting a bit big for them.

"A lot of them played well last season here, but it just looks like now it's coming on top for them a little bit and it's starting to just get to them.

"It did a little bit under Ruben Amorim towards the end where they just started to go a little bit like that.

"So look, Michael Carrick has got to get something out of them, the boos I don't think are against him, but the pressure's on him, the questions are obviously always with the manager and you just hope they can come out of it in these next few weeks."

Sports.title: Sherrock, Hayter qualify for Worlds as Greaves sweeps up on Women's Series
Sports.content:
Fallon Sherrock and Gemma Hayter have qualified for the 2027 PDC World Championship as Beau Greaves won Events 21-22 at the Women's Series in Wigan on Saturday.

'The Queen of the Palace' will return to the place where she wrote history in 2020, after she confirmed her spot in the top five of the Women's Series.

Sherrock became the first (and only) woman to pick up wins at Alexandra Palace, beating Ted Evetts and Mensur Suljovic before losing to Chris Dobey.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fallon Sherrock became the first woman to defeat a man at a World Championship with victory over Ted Evetts

She has since returned five times but came up fruitless against the likes of Steve Beaton, Ricky Evans, Jermaine Wattimena, Ryan Meikle and Dave Chisnall.

She will make her seventh appearance in December, despite only picking up one title so far on the Women's Series.

Hayter's run to the Event 22 final was enough to confirm her World Championship return.

Hayter qualified after reaching her third final of the year; she is now confirmed to finish in the top five on the Women's Series Order of Merit, hence booking her spot at a second World Championship.

She lost on debut to Josh Rock last year but took a set in a good performance.

She also picked up the WDF World Masters Title in 2026, as well as her first win at the Women's World Matchplay.

Hayter will be joined at Alexandra Palace by Lisa Ashton, Sherrock and Greaves, with Vicky Pruim currently in pole position to claim the final qualification spot via the PDC Women's Series rankings.

Greaves continued her PDC Women's Series domination with another brace of titles in Wigan on Saturday.

The reigning three-time Women's World Matchplay champion claimed back-to-back titles on a bumper day of action, as the year's final weekend of Women's Series action got under way at the Robin Park Leisure Centre.

'Beau 'n' Arrow' breezed to the Event 21 title in emphatic style, conceding just five legs in scooping her 14th title of the campaign.

The Doncaster superstar opened her challenge with successive whitewash wins against Laura van den Berg and Ruby Grey, before overcoming Dutch star Aileen de Graaf in round three.

Greaves then averaged north of 101 in a sensational quarter-final blitz of Rhian O'Sullivan, which she backed up with a five-leg drubbing of Sherrock in the semi-finals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's World Matchplay final between Beau Greaves and Fallon Sherrock in Blackpool

This set up a winner-takes-all showdown against Sweden's Pruim in the Event 21 showpiece, which saw Greaves fire in a superb 13-darter to wrap up a hard-fought 5-3 success.

Greaves extended her winning run with comfortable wins over Sharon Godbeer and Gemma Reynolds in the early stages of Event 22, before recovering from 3-1 down to deny Lisa Ashton.

Ashton squandered multiple match darts to complete a 4-1 win, and after frittering away further opportunities in a last-leg decider, she was duly punished by a ruthless Greaves.

The World Youth Championship runner-up then swept aside Steph Clarke, Joanne Oldershaw and Leanne Topper to maintain her charge, which set up a fascinating clash against Gemma Hayter for the Event 22 crown.

There was little to separate the pair for large periods of the contest, but Greaves eventually prevailed in a high-quality affair, overcoming some late double trouble to celebrate her record-extending 61st Women's Series title.

Image: Gemma Hayter also confirmed her spot at Ally Pally

Despite missing out on a first title of 2026, Hayter's run to the Event 22 final was enough to confirm her Ally Pally return.

Ashton, meanwhile, will also feature in next month's Mr Vegas Grand Slam of Darts, with the Lancashire stalwart now assured of a second-place finish on the Women's Series rankings.

The 2026 PDC Women's Series season will culminate with Events 23-24 in Wigan on Sunday.
