Sports.title: Arsenal given major injury scare as star carried off during warm down after Leeds win
Sports.content:
Arsenal given major injury scare as star carried off during warm down after Leeds win

Piero Hincapie had to be carried off the pitch during Arsenal's post-match warm down following their win over Leeds United.

The defender was seen clutching his right ankle after going down at the Emirates Stadium.



3 Hincapie was forced off during the warm down on Saturday Credit: Getty

Hincapie made an eight-minute cameo during the comeback victory after replacing Riccardo Calafiori in the 82nd minute.

However, he will now be a doubt for Tuesday's Champions League clash with Lille.

Hincapie injury setback

The Ecuador international was one of several players to complete extra winning after the final whistle.



It is a common practice used by the majority of clubs for those players who did not start the match.

Hincapie had been introduced to help see out the win after goals from Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes gave Arsenal the lead.



The hosts had trailed earlier in the second half following James Justin's opener for Leeds.

It marked just a third Premier League appearance this season for Hincapie, with all of them coming as a substitute.



Prior to Saturday's match, he had not featured since the Gunners' win over Chelsea on September 6.

However, he did play the full 90 minutes against Napoli in the Champions League three days after beating the Blues.

The 24-year-old was also left out of Ecuador's squad for the recent international break.

3 Hincapie made an eight-minute cameo off the bench against Leeds Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



Hincapie was not included for matches against South Korea, Japan and Panama.

His exclusion was in part due to a suspension dating back to the World Cup in the summer.

A red card in Ecuador's last 32 defeat to Mexico in June resulted in a ban to be served outside of the tournament.

Arsenal injury latest

Hincapie could now become the third player unavailable to Mikel Arteta through injury after his latest blow.



Arsenal are already without both Christos Tzolis and William Saliba.

The former has been ruled out for the remainder of the month after picking up a hamstring injury on international duty with Greece.

3 Hincapie could become the third Arsenal player ruled out through injury Credit: Getty

As for Saliba, he has not featured since suffering a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain.

The centre-back is also targeting a return to action in November having not required surgery on his injury.

Sports.title: Manuel Neuer howler leads to fastest goal in Bundesliga history
Sports.content:
Manuel Neuer had a nightmare moment as his mistake led to Bayern Munich conceding after just six seconds against Augsburg.

Bayern endured the worst possible start on Saturday when their No.1's howler allowed Robin Fellhauer to score the fastest goal in Bundesliga history.

4 Neuer saw his hopes of a clean sheet disappear in less than 10 seconds on Saturday Credit: Getty

Straight from kick-off, Luis Diaz played what looked to be a harmless backpass towards Neuer.

But disaster struck when the Germany stopper took a heavy touch, and then tried to chip the ball over the onrushing Fellhauer.

This ended badly for Neuer though, as Fellhauer blocked the clearance, which then dropped straight into the Augsburg player's path and allowed him to roll the ball into the empty net.

With the ball hitting the back of net after just six seconds, making this the fastest goal in Bundesliga history.

While Augsburg celebrated, Neuer was shown visibly frustrated in his own goal before gesturing in apology to his teammates.

The previous record was shared by Karim Bellarabi of Bayer Leverkusen and Kevin Volland for TSG Hoffenheim - with the pair both scoring after nine seconds.

Bellarabi first set the record in 2014, playing for Bayer Leverkusen against Jurgen Klopp’s Borussia Dortmund, before Volland equalled it a year later, while playing for Hoffenheim against Bayern of all teams.

How did Bayern's clash with Augsburg unfold?

While Neuer's early blunder left Bayern with plenty of time to get back into the game, their equaliser didn't come until the second half.

Ismael Saibari pulled the Bavarians level on 55 minutes, but they didn't stay level for long.

Just eight minutes later, Neuer had another moment to forget as he parried Calvin Brackelmann's effort straight to the feet of Rodrigo Ribeiro, who tapped home to put Augsburg back in front.

4 Neuer led his Bayern team out as captain against Augsburg, but things soon turned sour Credit: Getty

4 Fellhauer could hardly believe his luck when Neuer's attempted pass bounced off him and gave him an open goal to score into Credit: Getty

This left Bayern staring at their first league defeat of the season, before Nathaniel Brown struck on 90 minutes to spare their blushes.

Having started the day two points off top spot, Vincent Kompany's side had looked to capitalise on league leaders Borussia Dortmund’s late collapse against Werder Bremen on Friday.

Dortmund were 2-0 up in the 85th minute before two goals in four minutes from the away side meant they had to settle for a draw.

But after Bayern were held to a 2-2 draw of their own, they remain two points adrift of Dortmund at the top of the table.

End of an era?

Neuer's huge mistake comes in what looks increasingly likely to be the last season of his playing career.

Having brought his international career to an end with Germany's round of 32 exit at the World Cup, the 40-year-old has previously hinted that he could retire at the end of the 2025/26 campaign.

4 Neuer's performances at the 2014 World Cup will go down in history Credit: Getty

Bayern would appear to have a ready-made successor in the form of Jonas Urgig, who has served as back up since his arrival in 2025.

Should the German make this season his last, it would spell the end of his historic career, which has seen him become the most decorated German footballer in history.

Neuer boasts a staggering 36 major trophies from his 21-year senior career, with his most notable achievements his 2014 World Cup glory with Germany and Champions League wins in 2013 and 2020.

Sports.title: Robbie Savage makes stunning EFL debut to put Russell Martin in deep trouble
Sports.content:
Robbie Savage enjoyed a stunning EFL debut as Peterborough United manager to pile further misery on Leicester City.

Posh, who started the match 23rd in League One, looked anything but a relegation-threatened side as they swept aside Leicester 3-1 at the King Power Stadium.

2 Leicester's season went from bad to worse at the hands of a former player Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands Saturday’s defeat leaves Leicester boss Russell Martin’s future in serious danger.

Martin’s counterpart Savage was appointed Peterborough boss earlier this month but had had to wait for his first taste of league action.

And it was well worth the wait for the travelling Posh fans who watched on as Owira Edwards fired them in front after just 12 minutes.

There was more to come as Harry Leonard took full advantage of a defensive mix-up to fire his side into a two-goals lead.

With Leicester now on the ropes, Savage’s men went for the jugular and an unfortunate deflection from Foxes defender Warren O’Hora handed Posh a 3-0 lead going into the break.

Leicester did pull one back in the second half through Emil Riis, but it was a case of too little too late for the rapidly decaying Foxes who are showing no signs of progression under Martin.

As had been the case in previous games, the atmosphere at the King Power Stadium quickly turned ugly.

Much of the disdain was again aimed at boss Martin who has now picked up just nine points from a possible 24.

The defeat heaped further pressure on the former Southampton and Rangers boss who is yet to win over the club’s supporters.

Fan disgruntlement towards the 40-year-old stem from his possession-hungry style of play.

2 Things go from bad to worse for Russell Martin at Leicester Credit: Getty

His method has created much debate since his arrival with many believing his style is both not fit for the rigours of League One and for the players at his disposal.

And it didn’t take long for Leicester fans to show their disapproval with the all-too familiar chant of ‘Russell Martin, your football is s***.’

Martin has now overseen three home league defeats including a brutal 4-0 thumping at home to Oxford last month.

The Leicester boss later insisted the bruising defeat was merely an anomaly after former Foxes star Matt Piper had labelled it ‘a sackable offence’.

"I'm not concerned about that happening again,” Martin previously said only to see his side put in a similar performance just five weeks later.

Martin has continued to stick to his philosophy in the face of much public criticism.

Following the midweek defeat at Stevenage, Martin was filmed interacting with a concerned Leicester fan where he defended the team's style of play, pointing to his side’s 135 shots on goal in the last five matches.

Savage by name, Savage by nature

But the day belonged to former Leicester midfielder Savage who has made a blistering start to life at Peterborough.

The early signs show that Savage has brought back a strong attacking identity in his side.

Posh scored four times in less than 10 minutes in Savage's first game in charge, a 4-1 victory over Ipswich Town in the EFL Trophy.

Three further goals at the King Power Stadium are encouraging signs for Peterborough fans as they aim to steer clear of the drop zone.

‘Best day of my life”

"Great performance," Savage told talkSPORT at full time. "The boys have embrace how we want to play.

"To change that mentality in four training sessions and two game, I can’t thank them enough.

"I think we deserved to win. Both teams could have scored more goals. They had some good chances. I’ve watched them numerous times .

"They create so many chances and when it clicks for them, because it will click, they’ll be at the top of the table,

"I’m just in disbelief. It’s one of the greatest days of my life."

Meanwhile, Martin claims he is not feeling the pressure despite having registered just two league wins this term.

He said: "I just feel hurt and the manner of the goals we conceded.

Teams just don have to work very hard. We gave three terrible goals away.

"I love my job," he added. "This club has the potential to be so brilliant. I take full responsibility today. What the fans are feeling in the stands, I feel too."

Sports.title: Arsenal make 27-year history during Leeds comeback win
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s 2-1 victory over Leeds was tinged with history as the Gunners got themselves back to winning ways.

Mikel Arteta’s men were given a fright at the Emirates against a dogged Leeds side who went ahead early in the second half through James Justin.



4 Mikel Arteta was delighted with his team's endeavour in the 2-1 win over Leeds Credit: AFP

4 Bruno Guimaraes netted a superb 70th-minute winner Credit: Getty

The Gunners were staring at back-to-back league defeats until Riccardo Calafiori stabbed home from close range to level the score.

Substitute Bruno Guimaraes finished off a brilliant team move in the 70th minute to provisionally draw Arsenal level with leaders Manchester City at the top of the table.



Ahead of the match, Arteta opted for a revised starting line-up consisting of a heavy English presence.

Arsenal boasted six English outfield players in a starting XI for a Premier League game for the first time since a match against Manchester United in February 1999.



Ben White, Ezri Konsa, and Myles Lewis-Skelly lined-up from the start against a Leeds side unbeaten in the league prior to kickoff.

They were joined by Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for the lunchtime clash.



Arsenal’s previous line-up consisting of six Englishmen included Lee Dixon, Nigel Winterburn, Steve Bould, Tony Adams, Ray Parlour and Stephen Hughes.

Saturday’s victory was the perfect response to the 3-0 defeat at Brighton prior to the international break.

The Gunners have had three weeks to stew over the thrashing at the Amex Stadium and it appeared as though Leeds were next in line to upset the reigning champions.

The defeat left Daniel Farke’s side still without a win over the north London side since 2003.



4 Arteta's line-up consisted of six English players for the first time in 27 years Credit: Getty

4 The last time it happened came in a fixture against Man United in 1999 Credit: Getty

Arteta's post-match reaction

Arsenal boss Arteta was delighted with his side's character after coming from behind to take a crucial three points.

He said: “Before the game we talked about two things: the challenge ahead against a team that hadn't lost in the Premier League and the second to restore our identity.



“We weren't pleased about what we did against Brighton and today we had a chance to make it right. We wanted to prove we are something special and unique."

Asked about the difficulty of playing against Leeds, the Spaniard added: "They are very physical and committed in what they do. We didn't finish in some great areas in the first half and they kept running.

"It's incredible the way they attack the box. They could've punished us in one or two moments in the first half and then they did. It's a good testament to the league.

"When you play 12:30 at home and go 1-0 down, you have to restore a lot of things and energy is one of them. The finishers came in and made a big difference."

Sports.title: Dominic Solanke led the line expertly and repaid Roberto De Zerbi for his show of faith - his rescue act needs to be the catalyst to kick-start Spurs' season, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
Dominic Solanke led the line expertly and repaid Roberto De Zerbi for his show of faith - his rescue act needs to be the catalyst to kick-start Spurs' season, writes MATT BARLOW

Roberto De Zerbi has a lot hinging on Dominic Solanke. Perhaps not all of it by design but by ostracising Richarlison, selling Will Lankshear and signing Omar Marmoush who does not look like a natural fit at centre forward in this system, the Tottenham boss needs Solanke’s fire to rekindle.

Having spent the international break working on him and the three forwards in support, none of whom were away playing for their countries, the Spurs boss asked him to lead the team at Old Trafford in every sense.

Solanke was given the honour of pulling on the armband and being the captain despite not being part of the five-man captaincy group.

It was, according to De Zerbi, a popular move to show faith in a striker who has been the target for criticism during Spurs’ sluggish start to this season.

He started by missing a sitter and the time it took to collect the ball and work it into a shooting position portrayed his fragile confidence. Senne Lammens made a good save, but the Spurs skipper should have scored.

Dominic Solanke netted his first of the season to lift Spurs' spirits

Then he missed another glorious chance at the start of the second half but to his credit he kept going. He refused to let the misses haunt him. He held up the ball, fought to protect it when he could and drew Manchester United’s centre halves into a physical contest.

In the end, Solanke earned his reward, outmuscling Lisandro Martinez to reach the teasing, inswinging cross from Sandro Tonali, the midfield general signed for a club record £100million who finished the game at left back from where he delivered his most significant contribution in a Spurs shirt.

Tonali’s relief was clear. He is impatient to make an impression and produce a return on what he realises is a huge investment, and yet it will be nothing compared to Solanke’s.

Centre forwards need to score, and he was his first in the Premier League since March. His problems in front of goal since returning from an ankle injury which ruled him out of the first half of last season have been amplified by the team’s problems finding the net.

There was no way Solanke was going to let anyone think he had not applied the slightest touch to the ball. He raced away to a jubilant away end to bask in the glory.

Solanke's header was his first league goal since March

De Zerbi applauded his performance. 'We need this Dominic Solanke because Dominic Solanke is able to make the difference in this team,' said the Spurs boss.

Having been reduced to 10 men, his team showed some of the fighting spirit they have been accused of lacking in the last 12 months.

As a collective, Solanke’s equaliser cast a positive glow across another game when they have failed to win.

Three points from six games is barely cause for celebration but De Zerbi has been searching for what he called a ‘click’.

Perhaps this goal will be it. Something to change the narrative. Perhaps to instil faith in what they are trying to do.

Something also to remind them they can fight back. De Zerbi adored the reaction. 'The first time we have played as a team,' purred the Italian.

Spurs have not come back from behind to win in the Premier League for almost two years and the counter has ticked to 49 games.

It is an embarrassing statistic but fighting back to take a point with 10 men will go down as progress and De Zerbi will be thrilled at Solanke’s part in the rescue act.

Rodrigo's red mist

Spurs have often been guilty of emotional fragility in the last two seasons. Start well but fail to score, make a mistake, go behind and then crumble. It has been a familiar routine.

So when they started well at Old Trafford only to fade and go behind, then see Rodrigo Bentancur lose discipline and leave them a man down as well as a goal down it seemed like another one of those days.

Bentancur is one of De Zerbi’s favourites because he is canny and experienced, and a little bit cynical.

Rodrigo Bentancur saw red in the second-half and was sent off for headbutting Luke Shaw

He started on the bench after a long-haul international break playing friendlies for Uruguay in India, South Korea and Japan, and came on when the game was goalless.

Within seven minutes, Spurs were behind and within five more he had left his teammates in the lurch by losing his head. First, jumping recklessly into a tackle and then springing up to headbutt Luke Shaw.

'I gave him a kiss and said thanks,' said De Zerbi. 'It’s a mistake but the red card gave us the spark. For a long time, Tottenham played without this blood and this character. I want to see it in every game. You can’t win with only quality but with the right energy we are going to win many games.'

Senesi shines

Centre halves in modern football are invariably the players with the most time on the ball and the most touches and it helps if they have vision and a good range of passing.

As Marcos Senesi’s composure shone in the first half it was tempting to wonder if Micky van de Ven’s future at Spurs will be at left back, where he plays for the Netherlands.

Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke seemed perfectly comfortable together and relished the late rearguard.

Sunshine break

Spurs will go to Spain for a training break before the next game at home to Coventry on Monday week.

Sports.title: Christian McCaffrey and Olivia Culpo welcome their second child in the midst of NFL season as they reveal baby boy's adorable name
Sports.content:
San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey and wife Olivia Culpo have welcomed their second child, a baby boy named Roman Augustus.

Culpo, a former Miss Universe, revealed the name and Roman's birthday, September 29, in a Saturday post on Instagram. The slides included shots of both her and McCaffrey holding the infant, as well as a photo of Roman meeting his big sister, Colette, who was born in July of 2025. Another slide shows Culpo smiling alongside McCaffrey as she prepares for a C-section birth.

It's unclear if the couple has a particular affinity for Roman history or their young boy's namesake, the emperor born Octavian in 63 BC.

McCaffrey, the son of three-time Super Bowl champion Ed McCaffrey, and his model-influencer wife tied the knot in June 2024 in her native Rhode Island.

Previously, Culpo said she wanted to wait to have another child, but realized she was four months pregnant just six months after giving birth to Colette.

'I did not think that this was going to happen the way that it did,' she said on TikTok in May. 'I am so fortunate to be able to bring another child into the world. Few things that have been running through my mind, 'cause I just really didn't plan on this at all. … Well, I hope that this baby is healthy.'

Christian McCaffrey and wife Olivia Culpo have welcomed their second child, a baby boy

McCaffrey, the son of three-time Super Bowl champion Ed McCaffrey, and his model-influencer wife Olivia Culpo tied the knot in June 2024 in her native Rhode Island

She did note that she was 'definitely not totally healed' from her previous C-section.

'In the beginning, I was like, 'Oh, my God, can I even do this? Is this allowed? Like, what's gonna happen?' she recalled. 'I just wish that I had planned a little better.'

Culpo first made her pregnancy announcement on her 34th birthday with a series of adorable family snapshots from a photoshoot with their daughter Colette and their puppy.

McCaffrey has enjoyed becoming a father, as he told Us Magazine in February.

'It's the best, man,' McCaffrey said. 'Good day or bad day, you come home and seeing her smile takes all the pressure off. It takes all the worries of life away. It's been the biggest blessing in our life.

Culpo shared a photo of her daughter Colette, while pregnant with her new son, Roman

It's unclear if the couple has a particular affinity for Roman history or their young boy's namesake, the emperor born Octavian in 63 BC and later immortalized in countless statues

'Watching Olivia become a mom has been so cool. We had [Colette] in July, which was right before training camp so I was kind of in go-mode and went through the whole season. There's challenges that come with that. So, to now take a breath and be able to be a dad has been really, really fun.'

Since welcoming Colette, the couple have been adapting to their new role as parents while also juggling McCaffrey's commitments on the football field.

She lifted the lid on how fatherhood has changed McCaffrey's perspective on losses in an interview with the New York Post in January while discussing his playoff loss to the Seattle Seahawks.

'Well, first and foremost, I have always been worried about his health and safety,' she told the New York Post. 'If he's feeling good and if I notice, "Okay, he's walking okay or he doesn't look too banged up." I'm really excited and happy. And he feels that way too.

'I think ultimately it's just such a physical sport that you just want to be healthy enough to reach the goals that you have for yourself,' she continued. 'I think just being there for him and definitely being sensitive to the fact that it does mean a lot and sometimes he will be upset.

Last summer, the couple announced the birth of Colette, their first baby together

In addition to their two children, the couple also shares a small dog named Oliver Sprinkles

'Having a baby there really has changed that and made everything feel a little bit more grounded and light — and just have a better perspective because… win or lose, you still have to show up for her.'

Culpo continued: 'I always knew he would be a really good dad because he's just a really good person. And his parents [Lisa and former NFL wideout Ed McCaffrey] are just a great example.

'But I feel like I'm happy for the perspective that it's able to give him, especially with his career,' she said. 'So I'm very grateful for that.'

A three-time All-Pro now in his 10th NFL season, McCaffrey had a successful campaign in 2025 after becoming a father, rushing for 1,202 yards and 10 touchdowns to go with 924 yards and seven more scores through the passing game.

Most importantly, he appeared in all 17 games for the 49ers, who fell to the eventual Super Bowl-champion Seahawks in the Divisional Round of the playoffs.

This year, the 49ers are off to a 4-0 start thanks to 340 yards from scrimmage and four touchdowns from McCaffrey.

Sports.title: Inside Man City's dressing room after guilty verdict: We reveal Enzo Maresca's inspiring words which left squad 'ready to go to war' - plus the two most 'vocal and calming' stars
Sports.content:
In scenes that felt symbolic of the last fortnight at the Etihad Stadium, a huge lorry contracted to work on the site’s ongoing £300million redevelopment was impaled by an electronic bollard at about three o’clock on Friday afternoon.

Just stuck there in the car park, gallons of liquid leaking out of the bottom. Mercifully, the skewer puncturing the vehicle marginally evaded the fuel tank.

Almost exactly 24 hours earlier across Ashton New Road at the training ground, Manchester City bosses had been plugging any problems or uncertainty among their players.

Chief executive Ferran Soriano spoke to them as a collective, as he had with the Treble class of 2023 inside the first-team auditorium when the Premier League charges initially dropped. But it was the blunt, forthright message imparted by Enzo Maresca that had the squad sitting up and listening.

Maresca is forging a reputation as a strong communicator, as seen during his media duties before heading to Anfield, and there was one takeaway from his short private address.

‘Forget the noise,’ he told them. ‘We’re here to win a league. Let’s go and win the league.’

Man City boss Enzo Maresca has urged his side to win the Premier League despite the cloud hanging over the club after they were found guilty of breaching the top flight's financial rules

City CEO Ferran Soriano spoke to the squad as a collective after they returned from the break

Maresca stalks a dressing room when he talks, repeats mantras over and over, louder and louder. City’s players are listening to him and following him and it is little wonder that one source talked about being ‘ready to go to war’ because that is exactly the tone their manager is taking, with a delivery to boot.

This is also where previous relationships with Erling Haaland and Ruben Dias come in handy, the pair of them at the club when Maresca was Pep Guardiola’s assistant.

Those two are said to have been the most vocal among the squad since the guilty verdict was released a week last Tuesday, calming influences as others rightly worried about the ramifications of such a one-sided result that has taken everybody at City aback.

There are staff who are struggling to put the pieces together of what has transpired, comparing the certainty with the independent commission’s findings and the certainty of their employers that they will prevail on appeal.

Debating the seismic judgment with the credibility they see in Soriano and the affection they have for chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. These are confusing times for those in the offices.

‘A perceived external threat can strengthen a sense of togetherness, creating a feeling that the team needs to prove people wrong,’ said Dr Nikita Rowley, sport psychologist at Coventry University.

‘It is a double-edged sword. If it creates defensiveness, resentment or a siege mentality, it could increase pressure and distract players. The key is whether that feeling translates into positive collective focus and cohesion, rather than a preoccupation with outside opinion.

‘Breaking things down into manageable, immediate goals helps bring attention back to the present. Strong leadership, consistent messaging and an environment where people feel supported can help maintain trust and stability.’

Maresca has confronted drama before, the ex-Juventus midfielder interviewed and subsequently cleared of betting on Serie A matches as part of the Calciopoli scandal when his former club were demoted to the second division. He can lean on that experience with his players, who are waiting to be led.

That even goes for the more senior heads, with Haaland taken off media duties while away with Norway the day after news broke of the guilty findings for fear he would become the club’s spokesman before an official judgment had been published.

Once the globetrotting striker sat down with Sky Sports in the days before boarding the bus for Merseyside – an interview that had been slated for weeks beforehand – there had been discussions between the broadcaster and City about what might be appropriate to ask and how that was framed.

Together with Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland has been a vocal and calming member of the squad

Similar took place with Norwegian powerhouse Viaplay and other television rights holders before a Friday press conference that surprisingly passed off without incident.

And there is an understandable feeling within the club that footballers – however decorated and however articulate they are – should not present the face of this.

In Maresca, like Guardiola before him, they possess somebody adept at navigating this situation. In a different way, with a smile and quick line rather than confrontation, but somebody they can rely on nevertheless.

Those similarities extend to how to manage the squad, with Haaland having spent a few days in Marbella playing golf after being given time away from international duty at the end of the Nations League window, with those not away with their countries – the suspended Phil Foden, Antoine Semenyo – given breaks to travel too.

Semenyo is labelled ‘David Beckham’ this season by Haaland after stunning assists and got married during his time off.

Still smiling after the bombshell news and City will need to take that attitude with them on Sunday if they are to thrive in an environment that many will not have experienced before.

Sports.title: Declan Rice is worn out - it's time for Mikel Arteta to heed warning signs and give exhausted midfielder a rest, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Declan Rice is worn out - it's time for Mikel Arteta to heed warning signs and give exhausted midfielder a rest, writes ISAAN KHAN

It took Bruno Guimaraes just six minutes to take the match away from Leeds’ defiant grasp — something the clearly exhausted Declan Rice struggled to do during his first hour on the pitch.

The Brazilian's strike, well taken after latching onto Rice’s clever flick to fire past James Trafford from just inside the area, sealed victory for Arsenal, adding to Riccardo Calafiori’s earlier goal, after what had been a testing lunchtime affair.

Arsenal had been the masters of their own downfall before Guimaraes' intervention. Errant passes and a lack of composure in the final third were hallmarks of a tepid first-half display.

That was a surprise; not least since it came off the back of the 3-0 drubbing by Brighton, a scoreline which could have and should have been wider. Pre-match, Leeds had been pencilled in as the unfortunate victims of revenge by the champions.

Instead, quite the opposite transpired. Daniel Farke’s men were impressive. Their physicality proved too much for Arsenal to handle. David Raya managed to keep them at bay initially before Leeds took a deserved lead through James Justin on 55 minutes.

It was the performance of Rice, though, who particularly stood out. And not for the right reasons.

Declan Rice struggled in Arsenal's win over Leeds on Saturday and he desperately needs a rest

Mikel Arteta relies so heavily on Rice - and rightly so - but he must heed the warning signs

He is, quite simply, worn out, both mentally and physically. And who can blame him? He made 55 appearances in all competitions for Arsenal last season, starting 49 of those 55 matches and playing 4,454 minutes. That was 91 per cent of Arsenal's available minutes - no Arsenal outfielder played more.

It’s why, despite withdrawing from England duty recently to have a well-deserved three weeks away from playing matches, the midfielder still looks in desperate need of careful management going forward.

If Rice wasn’t ready to start on Saturday lunchtime then he should have been rested. If he wasn't fit enough for international duty, why would Rice be ready for the first match back after the break?

The problem is Rice’s ability to produce a moment of magic, like the neat flick to set up Guimaraes, makes him so hard to drop for Mikel Arteta.

But his body can only sustain so much and he is edging near breaking point, as the Leeds display reflected.

His wayward passing stifled the Gunners’ play in the first half. He was uncharacteristically lax on the ball, taking too many touches before having his pocket picked as he struggled to reach his free-flowing best. Rice's sluggishness on the ball also hurt his side when Arsenal had opportunities to break forward.

Ultimately, Rice managed to salvage a decent display because that's what top players do. He, like Arsenal, improved in the second half.

But Rice shouldn't be allowed to continue to play through the pain. Don't forget he did so at the World Cup, where he managed neural pain in his hamstring.

Rice himself last month said: ‘I think for the last six seasons, even since my West Ham days when it was in Europe, I've played 60 plus (games) every season.’

At his best, the 27-year-old glides forward, leaving opponents in his wake before quickly distributing the ball into attacking areas.

It makes any drop off all the more noticeable. Arteta must heed the warning signs and rest him soon before his star man hits breaking point.

Rice salvaged his display and set up Bruno Guimaraes' winner but he is nearing breaking point

Arteta puts faith in Dowman

16-year-old wonderkid Max Dowman had a spot on the bench against Leeds, but Cristhian Mosquera was not so fortunate. Arteta loves a defender, and Mosquera proved to be a fine one during last season's title success.

Yet, Arteta opted to go with Dowman, whose time to fully breakthrough can’t be far away now.

With Christos Tzolis injured, Noni Madueke played on the left wing, leaving Dowman as the obvious cover for Bukayo Saka on the right flank.

If Saka were to pick up a knock or underperform, Dowman is the next cab off the rank.

From his showings thus far, the teenager would take his chance and not look back. Watch this space.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer casually announces his new Chelsea contract on awkward mock livestream just HOURS before clash with Bournemouth - as Blues star returns to Twitch after being banned for streaming EA FC27 too early
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer has claimed Chelsea are 'going in the right direction' after signing a new long-term contract until 2034. The Chelsea star announced his new deal on a mock Twitch livestream, which saw him respond to fake questions from fans. Palmer read out the question 'How long are you staying at Chelsea then?', with the attacker responding: 'Well, I've just signed a new contract about 20 minutes ago.' 'So I'm staying for about eight more years. 'So hopefully you can sing that song a bit more that you all sing.' The mock Twitch stream comes after Palmer was temporarily suspended from the platform last month after playing EA Sports FC 27 before the game's release, leading to the midfielder appealing for them to lift his ban. Cole Palmer has signed a new long-term deal committing him to Chelsea until 2034 Palmer announced his new contract on a mock Twitch live stream before an official announcement Palmer has insisted Chelsea are heading in the right direction in their pursuit of major trophies Palmer had seven years left to run on his previous deal, but has agreed improved terms with the new contract extending his commitment by a further 12 months. The 24-year-old expressed his belief the Blues are making progress and will be in contention to win major trophies. 'Chelsea means a lot to me and I think the club is going in the right direction, so I'm delighted to sign and I'm obviously very happy,' Palmer said. 'Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence so it was only right to sign. 'Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we can win major trophies here consistently and I want to be a part of that and play a big role in it too.' Palmer has scored 58 goals and provided 34 assists in 138 appearances for Chelsea since joining from Man City in 2023. The attacking midfielder has played a key role in helping the Blues win the FIFA Club World Cup and Conference League in 2025. Palmer has enjoyed a strong start to the season having scored four goals and provided two assists in seven matches. He now boasts one of the longest contracts in the Premier League, with team-mates Joao Pedro and Geovany Quenda also on deals until 2034. Erling Haaland's long-term Manchester City contract also runs until 2034. Despite his performances for Chelsea, Palmer has made just 14 appearances for England. Palmer has enjoyed a strong start to the season, scoring four goals in seven matches Palmer withdrew from the England squad during the recent international break, with Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel stating he 'misses way too many camps' and that this was 'another missed opportunity'. Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso defended Palmer, with his withdrawal through injury related to the groin problem which has previously plagued him 'We were cautious, and he was cautious as well, he wanted to be,' Alonso said of Palmer. 'He wouldn't have played the way he wants to play. It's sometimes better to take a step back and wait until you feel better and do it the right way. 'There is always a risk. With Morgan (Rogers), there was a risk. Nothing happened. With Jamie (Gittens), there was a risk. We've lost him for a few weeks. With Cole, it was the right decision.'

Sports.title: 'Worried' Gary Neville tells struggling Man United stars to 'get a grip' after Spurs draw ahead of tough run - as he warns midfield duo CAN'T play together and calls out lack of fight in Michael Carrick's men
Sports.content:
'Worried' Gary Neville tells struggling Man United stars to 'get a grip' after Spurs draw ahead of tough run - as he warns midfield duo CAN'T play together and calls out lack of fight in Michael Carrick's men

A frustrated Gary Neville has again accused Manchester United's players of lacking effort in their draw with Tottenham and warned they risk being 'eaten alive' by Atletico Madrid in midweek if they don't buck their ideas up.

The Red Devils were twice booed off at Old Trafford on Saturday evening as they conceded a late equaliser against ten-man Spurs to take their winless run to four games in all competitions.

But there seems to be a lack of fight from the team, according to Neville, with fans already questioning the side's desire to run after Youri Tielemans said they didn't do much work in that area of the game over pre-season.

Coupled with United's poor running numbers so far this season, and there are serious questions around the team's play – and Neville has once again taken aim.

'What United fans won't accept is what they deem as a lack of effort and the reality is they're not running enough, they're not showing enough tenacity, determination and fighting spirit,' he said on The Gary Neville Podcast. 'The boos tell you they are really despondent with what they are watching.

'What we are seeing at the moment is a team that looks like they are curling up in a ball and the club, for some of them right now, is getting a bit big for them.

Gary Neville has told Manchester United's players to 'get a grip' following their draw with Tottenham on Saturday

United are winless in four and were poor against 10-man Spurs, who scored a last-minute goal

'The shake of Carrick's head will be... are they doing it for me? What's happening with that lot? Have they lost their confidence? Have they switched off? Are they going under? What is going on? Because these aren't the players I was working with last season.'

United will face Atletico in midweek in the Champions League and face the prospect of a tough task at the Metropolitano despite a win in their first match of the Champions League league phase.

Atletico are second in LaLiga and beat Real Madrid in the Madrid derby the week before the international break.

There is also, meanwhile, concern around United's personnel – particularly in midfield. Something that Neville thinks needs to be looked at.

'With (Youri) Tielemans and (Kobbie) Mainoo, I think we've seen enough of it now,' Neville said. 'I'm not calling time on it because I think that's probably too drastic - but I've seen enough of it to think it's not dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League. They are both good players individually but sometimes you have players who just don't quite knit together and suit each other.

'When (Carlos) Baleba came on with Mainoo, that certainly looked more like there was more energy but there is going to have to be something done in there and the rest of them are going to have to get a grip.

'They're going to Atletico and then to Elland Road, and if you're not quite right there mentally and physically, you're going to get found out. If they don't get going, it's going to be a worrying few weeks.'

Neville also said it's time for United to stop playing Youri Tielemans (left) and Kobbie Mainoo (right) in midfield together

Michael Carrick's side will head to Spain to take on Atletico Madrid in the Champions League this week

Speaking on United's lack of apparent effort, he added: 'It is a real concern, going into a slog where you are playing every three days and the Champions League is going to hit you hard.

'You've got tough matches and all of the games coming up are going to need real personality and character, and it needs a group of players who are resilient and at the moment you do worry about them going into that run of matches and how they are going to come out of it.

'That three-week break was supposed to be a reset moment. But how you can perform like that in the first 20 minutes is really difficult to understand.'

Sports.title: Liverpool's clash with Man City is a ghost game that may as well be played in a circus tent: Grudge match starts slow period of torture for the top flight after guilty verdict - and Anfield's anger is real, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Liverpool's clash with Man City is a ghost game that may as well be played in a circus tent: Grudge match starts slow period of torture for the top flight after guilty verdict - and Anfield's anger is real, writes OLIVER HOLT

Is this an apparition that we see before us? Is it real? Is Liverpool-Manchester City at Anfield a football match or a ghost-game? Will it remain in the sport's history books or will it be erased when City’s guilty verdicts on 114 charges of financial chicanery meet their punishment sometime in the months ahead?

There was a time when any Premier League clash between these two sides would have been regarded as the best  for the English game that there could be. Not anymore. This game is being played at a wonderful stadium but it might as well be in a circus tent. It is not a match. It is a giant and terrible curiosity.

The great managers who helped to define this collision between modern giants – Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola – are both gone and now this clash stands for something else: it marks the start of a period of slow torture for the top flight in this country, a period when we cannot know whether there is any permanence attached to results that involve City. A period when we will not know whether we should believe what we see.

If – as many expect them to be – City are expelled from the Premier League before the end of this season, what happens to this afternoon’s result then? It will be declared null and void, presumably. The same fate, perhaps, will befall all matches involving City this season. ‘We’re not really here,’ City fans love to sing and its lyrics have never felt more apt.

‘We are not, we're not really here,’ the chant goes. ‘We are not, we're not really here, just like the fans of the Invisible Man, we're not really here.’ And that’s the thing: none of us know whether City are really here or not now. We have been told that everything they achieved under their ownership by Abu Dhabi was just an illusion and yet the illusion lingers still.

City are top of the league. Or are they? Are they just waiting for a fall? Or will they conjure an escape? Perhaps, against all expectations, their appeal will succeed. Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, has already expressed his admiration for City’s owners before attempting to recant.

Liverpool's showdown with Man City marks the start of a period when we cannot know whether there is any permanence attached to results that involve City

It marks a major change from the era where the meeting of Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola's sides provided the best  for the English game

If Man City win at Anfield and stay clear at the top of the table, it is unclear whether it will matter as the club awaits its punishment and the outcome of their appeal

God only knows what machinations are whirring in the corridors of power as the appeal plays out and football wrestles with its new place as a puppet of geopolitics. And while City play on, while they await their punishment, the damage that the whole affair does to English football multiplies.

The credibility of the Premier League is at stake. If City win at Anfield and stay clear at the top of the table, does it matter? If they’re going to get docked 100 points or kicked out of the league, then today’s result and today’s points will vanish into thin air. What’s the value in even playing?

Some will say that the value is in vengeance. That is what much of the rest of the Premier League wants to gain over City. After so much arrogance and so much intransigence and so much dissembling and depriving fans of other teams of memories that would have lived with them forever, it is hard to blame them for wanting to see City humbled on the pitch.

But there must be limits to that lust for retribution. So much resentment and so much anger about glories stolen away and trophies unfairly won, will follow City into Merseyside on Sunday afternoon that it is only right to acknowledge that an occasion that will be one of the most extraordinary in the history of our game will bring with it extraordinary demands.

There is only one meaningful target to be achieved at Anfield and in the terraced streets that surround it, and it is not the kind of goal that can be scored in front of the Kop or the Anfield Road End.

For all the animosity towards their club, the only thing that really matters on Sunday afternoon is keeping City’s players, staff and fans safe in a febrile atmosphere where emotions will be running wild.

The City team coach has been forced to run the gauntlet at Anfield several times before, most notably when the two teams met in a Champions League quarter-final first leg there in 2018. On that occasion, the bus was damaged enough by a range of missiles which rained down on it on its crawl along the Anfield Road for it to be rendered unable to carry the team back to Manchester.

It is not a problem germane to Anfield. Ten years ago, the Manchester United team coach was attacked on Green Street on its way to Upton Park to face West Ham in the final game played at the old stadium.

Man City can expect a hostile welcome and their team coach has run the gauntlet at Anfield before, but the thing that really matters is keeping City’s players, staff and fans safe

Hostilities are often inflamed in English football but it would be foolish to deny that this match is loaded with so much visceral disdain for the visiting team that there will be concerns about ensuring City have effective and comprehensive security. Many in the blue half of Manchester have felt unease for some years about travelling west to this fixture.

Some fan accounts on social media have called for Anfield to be the ‘most toxic we have ever seen it’. Some have encouraged the throwing of bottles of cider at the City coach. ‘Bus greeting vs Cheats,’ one Liverpool fan X account call to arms urged last week, mentioning a place to congregate two hours before kick-off. ‘Bring flags, banners, pyros, flares, koppabergs. Let’s make it a sea of red. Show them. Scare them.’

In the days since the findings of an independent commission established City’s guilt and the Premier League released a strongly-worded statement accusing City of constructing ‘sham’ arrangements to inflate sponsorship revenues artificially, the club has become a pariah.

Many believe the most suitable punishment for the club which won the Premier League four times in a row under Guardiola and has dominated the English game for much of the last decade is for them to be expelled from the top flight and demoted to League Two.

In Liverpool, the resentment against City centres on what was taken from the Anfield club unfairly. Steven Gerrard, one of the club’s favourite sons, never won a Premier League winners’ medal but he would have done in 2013-14 had City not been able to stack their side with players they bought because they cooked the books. Klopp would have built a dynasty in Liverpool had he not been denied by City sides.

All that is hard to oppose. A hostile reception is inevitable. And of course, City’s players and fans will be mercilessly baited during the match. That is to be expected but let us hope it begins and ends there. Punishment for City’s infractions must not be something to be meted out in violence. It should be handed down in the months ahead in fines, deductions and relegations.

Part of what fuels the resentment is the impression City give of being willing to use their fabulous wealth and endless legal resources to tear apart the fabric of the English game in their fury at being held to account. They have launched their appeal against the guilty verdicts and no one knows quite how long that appeal will take.

Until it is resolved, English football will be in limbo. Perhaps it would be more accurate to say that it will be in purgatory. This afternoon’s ghost game at Anfield is just the beginning of a period of our football lives when we will look at the agonised contortions of Manchester City and the desperate dysfunctionality of the Premier League and wonder what the hell we have become.

Sports.title: England legend Ian Botham labels Ben Stokes a 'stupid boy' and a 'self-indulgent has-been' in latest twist in war of words with former Test captain
Sports.content:
Lord Ian Botham has reignited his war of words with fellow former England all-rounder Ben Stokes, branding him a 'stupid boy' and 'has-been' in his latest rant.

Stokes retired from England duty earlier this year after an incident in a London nightclub alongside Gus Atkinson, having made his Test debut back in 2013.

Botham, meanwhile, who is, like Stokes, also considered one of England's greatest-ever all-rounders, has traded words with Stokes over the last 12 months – starting with Botham's criticism of England's preparations for last year's Ashes.

Now, though, he has chimed in again. He said of Stokes to the Times Magazine: 'Stupid boy. I'll mention him only briefly because his self-indulgence is not something I enjoy.

'He's a good player. A great player. But to say that and then lose, it's backfired, hasn't it? Then after losing the first two matches they go to Noosa, probably one of the most popular summer retreats for Australians.

'Really? They were p****d as rats. Look, if you want a drink, don't go to the high street. We used to go to wineries.'

Ben Stokes (left) and Ian Botham (right) have once again butted heads after the latter took aim at the former England star

The duo, pictured in 2021, have clashed since Botham criticised England's Ashes preparations last year

Botham had initially criticised Stokes' side's poor preparation last year down under, saying: 'Not one (state match), which borders on arrogance. You've got to give yourself the chance.'

Stokes hit back, saying: 'There's quite a few factors that play into why we can't prepare how the has-beens maybe prepared in the past.

'The landscape of cricket has changed and that affects preparation.'

After Stokes' retirement, meanwhile, Botham took aim again.

He said on Test Match Special: 'As we know Michael Vaughan and I, we don't know what we're talking about. Couple of old has-beens.

'Ben, if you're listening, congratulations, you've joined the club - you're now a has-been.'

Stokes, though, hit back again, saying on X: 'The quote "it's better to be a has-been than a never-been" originates from Lord Ian Botham.'

It seems Botham, though, has had the last laugh.

Upon releasing his new book, he said: 'This is for you, Ben. Welcome to the has-beens club.'

Sports.title: Kai Rooney nears Man Utd target date amid JJ Gabriel uncertainty as verdict approaches
Sports.content:
Kai Rooney nears Man Utd target date amid JJ Gabriel uncertainty as verdict approaches

Kai Rooney will soon find out his next step at Manchester United

View 2 Images Kai Rooney is nearing a major step in his footballing career (Image: Getty Images)

Kai Rooney is fast approaching a major career milestone at Manchester United. The 16-year-old forward, son of Red Devils legend Wayne Rooney, has risen through the ranks since joining the academy at 11 years old and currently stars for the Under-18s, who are managed by former United hero Darren Fletcher.

‌



‌



After signing a scholarship agreement in July to enter the club's Professional Development Phase, Rooney will become eligible to sign his first professional contract when he turns 17 on November 2 - a path that looks significantly less clear for fellow prospect JJ Gabriel.

‌



The 16-year-old requested his release from United last month and has failed to return to Carrington, instead spending the past three weeks in Castelldefels, Catalonia, training with a private coach.

‌



Gabriel is considered one of the most promising young talents in global football, and his potential exit would represent a crushing blow for United's academy. The club have reportedly put forward a scholarship contract to Gabriel - an agreement he qualified for after celebrating his 16th birthday on Tuesday.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd fans revive brutal Man City banner after Premier League guilty verdict READ MORE :

The forward has attracted attention from some of Europe's elite clubs, with Barcelona and Real Madrid both holding discussions over signing the teenager. Sky Germany reports that Bayern Munich have initiated talks with Gabriel's representatives.

‌



With Gabriel's future at Manchester looking uncertain at best, United have the chance to secure the second generation of the Wayne family in the form of Kai.

The teenager predominantly operates on the right wing, in contrast to his father, though the pair share a strikingly similar approach to the game, according to the United legend.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has not reported to Carrington since asking to leave Man United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Article continues below

During the Disney+ documentary series, The Real Rooneys, Wayne explained: "Kai plays for Manchester United in the academy and he is very driven. He scores goals and he wants it. It's very similar to me, it's like watching myself with a left foot. It's mad."

Kai netted twice at U18 level last season and even made his bow at the Theatre of Dreams during an FA Youth Cup victory over Derby County. His campaign was unfortunately cut short, however, by a foot injury that ruled him out of United's FA Youth Cup final loss to Manchester City.

Sports.title: David Beckham's staggering cash boost, upcoming Netflix series and son's family announcement
Sports.content:
David Beckham's staggering cash boost, upcoming Netflix series and son's family announcement

David Beckham's bank balance has been boosted again as England hero star circles a brand new Netflix show

View 2 Images David Beckham has a staggering net worth (Image: Getty Images)

Brand Beckham is showing no sign of stopping. Former Manchester United legend David has spent decades building himself up as one of football's most prominent figures, both on and off the field.

‌



‌



He is now amongst the world's most instantly recognisable personalities with a commercial empire to match. Sir David amassed hundreds of millions throughout his two-decade playing career with the likes of United, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



Through partnerships with brands such as adidas, he has arguably become the most famous name to ever play the sport. Together with wife Victoria, former Spice Girl and businesswoman, and their four children, the Beckhams have achieved near-royal status, such is their influence and reach.

‌



Here, Mirror Football examines David's net worth following another financial windfall and with a new Netflix documentary on the way. The Beckhams have also added a new member to the family.

£38m boost

It has emerged that Beckham pocketed a staggering £38million in less than 12 months . A significant portion came from a string of highly profitable sponsorship agreements at this summer's World Cup.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Michael Carrick takes Man City charges 'personally' as Man Utd boss makes appeal demand READ MORE :

Man Utd fans revive brutal Man City banner after Premier League guilty verdict READ MORE :

Newly released accounts show that David's firm, DRJB Holdings, recorded profits of £50m for the year ending December 2025.

The business is half-owned by American brand Authentic, and paid out £38.9m and £46.6m in dividends to shareholders in 2026. This handed Beckham personally over £38m.

The former winger has secured long-term partnerships with major global brands including McDonald's and Pepsi. It's proved a profitable spell for his empire, which surpassed the $100m (£75m) mark in the United States .

‌



Beckham's net worth is now believed to exceed £750m, while David and Victoria together are thought to have a combined fortune of £1.185billion.

Netflix show

Beckham is poised to feature in a fresh series. The Netflix-backed programme will offer a glimpse into the England icon's life.

It follows the enormous success of his four-part documentary, Beckham, which debuted in 2023 and drew 12.4m viewers during its opening week.

‌



View 2 Images The Beckham's at the premier of the Netflix documentary in 2023 (Image: PA)

The Inter Miami co-owner also helped produce the three-part series Victoria Beckham in 2025, a widely watched documentary that chronicled the former pop sensation.

Beckham's brand partner Jamie Salter said: "Following the Beckham documentary on Netflix, he is making more episodes with the channel.

‌



"David Beckham and Netflix are making another show, which is really cool. The last series has driven his business through the roof. Likewise, Victoria's business is now going through the roof after her docuseries too. You will definitely see him make more content. Content drives the message to the consumer."

Cruz makes announcement

While the Beckhams continue to expand their worldwide appeal, they've also welcomed a fresh addition to their clan. David and Victoria's youngest son, Cruz, and his girlfriend, Jackie Apsotel, have become the proud owners of a dog.

Cruz took to Instagram to post photos of their new dog, called Sandy Jean Beckham. Cruz, 21, and Jackie, 30, uploaded multiple images of the Labrador.

The youngest Beckham son has also set up an Instagram profile for Sandy, which has already racked up thousands of followers. Victoria is evidently smitten, as she wrote: "Soooooo sweet! ! ! We love you Sandy! ! !" beneath a snap of the adorable pooch.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Merino's dad reveals exit terms as January swap deal available
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Merino's dad reveals exit terms as January swap deal available

The latest Arsenal round-up includes Mikel Merino's father discussing the midfielder's future

View 3 Images Mikel Merino's father has opened up about his son's future (Image: PA)

Arsenal were as defiant as ever as they came back from behind to defeat Leeds United 2-1. The Gunners were seeking a return to winning ways after their 3-0 loss to Brighton before the international break.

‌



‌



The Premier League champions got off to an awful start in their quest for victory when James Justin put the Whites ahead in the second half at the Emirates Stadium. However, Riccardo Calafiori levelled the scoring just seven minutes later before substitute Bruno Guimaraes scored a stunning strike to give Mikel Arteta's side the lead and the three points.

‌



Normality has been restored in north London with the triumph, although the club are facing potential departures when it comes to their title-winning squad. Mikel Merino's father has opened up about his son's future, while reports of a blockbuster swap deal in January has emerged.

‌



Mirror Football takes a look at the latest stories surrounding the champions...

Merino's dad opens door

View 3 Images Mikel Merino hasn't started a Premier League game this season (Image: Marco Canoniero/Shutterstock)

Mikel Merino has had to settle for a largely bit-part role at Arsenal this season, despite playing a key role in Spain's World Cup triumph this past summer. It's a situation that may not last for long following comments made by the midfielder's father, Miguel.

‌



Merino Sr. appeared on Goles con Parrado to discuss his son's career and was asked whether the 30-year-old could possibly return to La Liga. The Spaniard's father suggested his son would prefer to join a Champions League club if an exit from north London became a reality.

Declan Rice pinpoints exactly what sets Mikel Arteta apart from Premier League rivals READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta gives telling one-word answer over his conscience amid Man City verdict READ MORE :

Miguel said: "If he comes to La Liga, well, I suppose he’ll want to continue in that rhythm of competing in the Champions League and keeping that motivation, but obviously he’s in a comfortable situation there at Arsenal, isn’t he? Because he’s experiencing exactly what he wanted when he left Real Sociedad."

Arsenal signed Merino in a £27million deal from Real Sociedad and Miguel was questioned as to why Real Madrid didn't come in for him. Insistent on his son's quality, he answered: "Well, look, it’s not just about Real Madrid.

‌



"I think he’s a player who’s at Arsenal and has won the Premier League, has reached the Champions League final, he got to the semi-finals last year. He’s part of a world class squad, so he’s a world class player."

Gyokeres swap deal

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres could be on his way out of Arsenal (Image: Getty )

Arsenal reportedly remain interested in Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez after failing to acquire the striker in the summer transfer window. The Argentine international pushed for a move away from Madrid and sought Barcelona as his only possible departure, but bad blood between the two clubs stopped a move from happening.

‌



According to Sport, Arteta is still keen to sign the 26-year-old and would be willing to pull the trigger on a swap deal that would see Viktor Gyokeres move in the opposite direction. The Swedish striker has lost his place in the Gunners' starting line-up and has yet to score in six games across all competitions.

Reports in Spain on Saturday suggested that Atletico are seriously considering letting Alvarez leave in January.

Article continues below

It's been a similarly difficult start to the campaign for the attacker, having managed 173 minutes of football due to the summer saga spilling over into the new season, as well as suffering muscular issues.

Sports.title: Dapper Laughs DRAWS boxing fight with Joey Essex in controversial decision
Sports.content:
Dapper Laughs DRAWS boxing fight with Joey Essex in controversial decision

Reality TV star Joey Essex took on comedian Dapper Laughs as Misfits Boxing returned to London on Saturday night

View 2 Images Joey Essex punches Dapper Laughs

Dapper Laughs was denied victory over Joey Essex as their boxing fight was controversially scored a draw.

‌



‌



Dapper - real name Daniel O'Reilly - has attempted to rehabilitate his image having been cancelled 16 years ago. He now tours the country doing stand-up comedy under his real name and accepted this fight with Essex on two weeks' notice - primarily to promote his upcoming film.

‌



Both Dapper and Essex had one fight to their name ahead of meeting in the ring with the former stopping Simple Simon three years ago before retreating from the influencer boxing scene.

‌



Misfits Boxing results including Big Stacks and Joey Essex vs Dapper Laughs READ MORE :

Essex, meanwhile, made his Misfits Boxing debut last year, outpointing Numeiro in a slug-fest. The reality TV star, who has appeared on TOWIE and Love Island, is the nephew of renowned boxing trainer Tony Sims and promised a more measured approach on his return to the ring.

And while he was not as gung-ho as he was 12 months ago, Essex struggled to impose himself in the opening round. Dapper, perhaps accepting his fitness would ultimately let him down, looked determined to take the fight to the favourite and landed the bigger shots. Essex laughed off his attacks but was on the end of another right hand in the second session as Dapper looked to take control.

‌



Dapper landed another right hand in the third round as he looked to turn the fight into a brawl. Essex responded with the same shot. But Dapper pushed the younger man back towards the ropes with a right-left combination. Dapper appeared to be tiring as the round drew to a close as Essex marched forwards.

View 2 Images Dapper Laughs punches Joey Essex

Both men began the final session as if they knew they needed to impress the judges. But it was Dapper who had more success with his right hand as he looked to defy the odds. Essex attempted to respond but it was he who was forced backwards under a final assault as the seconds ticked away.

Article continues below

Dapper and his team were the more expectant at the final bell but both men had to settle for a share of the spoils with the judges scoring the fight 37-39, 40-36 and 38-38.

Earlier in the night, Big Stacks, who calls himself the UK's Hardest Man, outpointed former West Ham defender James Collins. The Welshman had stepped in to replace bed salesman Thomas Skinner and did not look out of place.

But Stacks dropped Collins in the third of four rounds with the ex-footballer doing well to get back to his feet. Ultimately, two of the three judges gave Stacks the nod.

Sports.title: Andy Carroll's abuser's own daughter labels him a 'monster' and would say sorry if they met
Sports.content:
Andy Carroll's abuser's own daughter labels him a 'monster' and would say sorry if they met

Andy Carroll has opened up about a sexual assault that he was the victim of in 2021, naming the man involved, and his daughter has come out and praised his bravery

View 2 Images Andy Carroll was opened up on a sexual assault that took place five years ago (Image: 2025 Jacques Feeney/Offside)

The daughter of the man who abused Andy Carroll has claimed her father was a "monster" and the footballer was right to publicly name him.

Former Newcastle and Liverpool striker Carroll recently confirmed the man who sexually assaulting him was Kevin Adams. The dance coach who starred on now-cancelled BBC show Fame Academy was convicted at Chelmsford crown court in 2023.

Carroll revealed that he was abused in his autobiography which was published last month, with the incident occurring in 2021. After recently learning that Adams' name was in publicly available court documents Carroll confirmed his identity.

Avia, 21, claimed her father was a “sick individual” and told The Sun after hearing about Carroll's story: “I feel really bad for him. I just think my dad is a monster.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

She went on to add: “As far as naming him, he’s done something terrible to you so name him. If I was in that position I’d do the same.”

Avia also admits she’d say “sorry” to Carroll if they met. “Obviously, I know it’s not my fault but it’s just like, that’s my dad. It’s just disgusting. And I’m sorry that that’s happened to him," she said.

Avia and her sister had little contact with her father after his marriage to their mother broke down in 2011. Adams married Avia’s mother in September 2005, six months after Avia was born. She has not heard from him since the revelations - and plans to change her surname to sever the ties they currently have.

View 2 Images Kevin Adams' daughter, Avia, has called her dad a "monster"

Article continues below

The incident involving Carroll and Adams happened in 2021 after the footballer had returned home following a game for Newcastle. He said in his book that ex-wife Billi Mucklow had convinced him to invite Adams round to watch a boxing match and they let him stay in their spare room.

Carroll explained how he suddenly woke up to the man trying to attack him underneath his bedsheets. He responded by throwing him out of the house and smacked Adams "as hard as he could" when he tried to re-enter before calling the police and crying into (his children's) nanny's arms.

He said he added the story into his autobiography at "the last minute" and hopes that it will help other victims of sexual assault.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has nowhere to hide as Man Utd fans turn in draw with 10-man Tottenham
Sports.content:
Tottenham secured a much deserved point as Dominic Solanke scored in stoppage time to deny a Manchester United team who had been outclassed in front of a frustrated Old Trafford.

It was a shock when Bryan Mbeumo scored on 70 minutes to put the hosts ahead after the home fans had jeered throughout such was the level of Tottenham dominance.

They looked poised for three points, even more so when Rodrigo Bentancur was sent-off, but Solanke was on hand to head home with 92 minutes on the clock, leaving the north Londoners with something to show for their efforts, although their performance deserved all three points.

In the opening exchanges Tottenham looked like the team that they dreamed they would be under Roberto De Zerbi, dominanting the ball and the territory, albeit aided in part by United themselves.

‌



The hosts seemed to be on a mission of self harm such was their desire to play out in and around their own box, which saw Solanke gifted with a one-on-one chance, only to fluff his lines. Senne Lammens needed quick feet shortly after as he was again under pressure.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Old Trafford crowd, clearly not prepared to be subjected to another abject display, begun jeering as Tottenham came forward in waves. Those boos peaked when Lammens booted a clearance straight out of play.

United did steady the ship as the game went on, but it was a shock that it was a goalless contest come half-time. The home supporters still ensured the Red Devils stars walked off to a chorus of boos.

‌



Tottenham's onslaught continued with Savio racing to the byline, only for his cutback to somehow get cleared. Solanke missed his second chance minutes later, firing over to leave De Zerbi feeling like he should almost laugh otherwise he'd cry.

That feeling was only emphasised when Mbeumo converted in front of the Stretford End. The Tottenham boss saw his team finish with ten men as his midfielder was dismissed for a clash with Luke Shaw, but they would get the last laugh as Solanke headed home in stoppage time.

OLD TRAFFORD TURNS AS CRACKS EXPOSED

They're renowned for the patience. If this were any other club the amount of toxic games over the past decade would be through the roof, but every fanbase has their breaking point.

View 3 Images Tottenham rescued a much deserved point

‌



It takes a lot to boo one of their own, you can see that by how long they stood by Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. But Carrick tasted the Old Trafford jeers after they squandered a 2-0 lead to lose against Brighton in the Carabao Cup only weeks ago.

During their shocking first-half showing against Tottenham the boos came as Tottenham continued to dominate, and they reached boiling point midway through the opening 45. United did rally and improve as the half went on, but this simply isn't good enough and the supporters are now willing to let the players and the boss know.

Against any other team this game would've been done on the hour. That is something United and Carrick cannot escape as their direction of travel seems to be, front their perspective, heading in the wrong direction, and for good measure the home side were booed at full-time.

WHERE'S THE MONEY GONE?

For so long former players and pundits would cast their eye over United's squad and wonder just where the tens of millions actually went. Its no secret how much money they've spent in the years since Sir Alex Ferguson, desperately trying to find that level once again.

‌



But their investment has often not been reflected in the squad, owing to overpaying for players or struggling with a direction with their recruitment. Last summer the money spent on the attack seemed to look smart business, which was a rarity for United.

And yet 12 months on and that feeling is back again. Over £150million was spent on their midfield options - Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba all arriving.

There's been some injury issues, but Tielemans isn't looking like he has in recent years and Santos is struggling for minutes. Their engine room was constantly over run, and after a matter of games we're already questioning those transfer decisions.

View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo's strike wasn't enough for the win after Tottenham's late leveller

‌



PRETTY FOOTBALL DOESN'T WIN GAMES

Probably something of a backhanded compliment but watching Tottenham in that opening 20 minutes was similar to watching Manchester City during Pep Guardiola's first season when they were purring.

Throughout that season City quickly adopted the principles that had made Guardiola such a success elsewhere in Europe. They were in charge of the ball, they won it back quickly, their attacks seemed to be relentless, they seemed like it was a case of when, not if, they would score.

But Guardiola himself would bemoan their inability to turn their dominance into goals. It was scoring the goals that turned them into a machine. Tottenham did everything but score. That perhaps sums it up. You can coach a team up until the final bit of the game, but converting chances requires a killer instinct Tottenham are struggling with, although this was a display they can be proud of.

‌

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Tottenham descends into chaos as red card sparks huge clash
Sports.content:
Man Utd vs Tottenham descends into chaos as red card sparks huge clash

Tottenham went down to 10 men when players from both teams clashed late in the match at Old Trafford with Spurs already a goal down against Manchester United

View 2 Images Rodrigo Bentancur clashes with Luke Shaw (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off after clashing heads with Luke Shaw as Manchester United vs Tottenham threatened to descend into chaos. With United 1-0 up, Bentancur reacted rashly after being shoved to the ground.

‌



‌



Shaw pushed over his rival after Bentancur had launched the ball away following some flying tackles. The Uruguay international quickly got back to his feet and moved his head towards the United defender.

‌



The full-back hit the floor, dramatically clutching his face as bodies from both teams quickly came together. A melee ensued as Shaw and Jan Paul van Hecke came away with yellow cards in addition to Bentancur's red.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The offence means Tottenham have received five red cards since the start of last season, with London rivals Chelsea the only side to have earned more, having racked up eight.

On commentary, Gary Neville was in disbelief over Bentancur's actions. "It's madness from Bentancur to get involved," he said.

‌



"Lack of discipline is not what he needs. The scissors tackle, that's a yellow, Shaw pushes him and he comes up... He just gets up and leads towards him doesn't he? It'll always result in a red, especially after the challenge, it's just stupidity."

View 2 Images Tempers flared at Old Trafford (Image: Sky Sports)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Former Tottenham star Chris Waddle believes that Shaw also should have been given his marching orders. Waddle said: "Luke Shaw has stepped out of line there and has sort of held his head as though he's been headbutted.

"If Rodrigo Bentancur's got a red for it, Luke Shaw should have a red too. You can't raise your hands. Where's VAR?"

Sutart Atwell's decision to send off Bentancur for a headbutt was checked by the video assistant referee. “I’ve got a red card for Bentancur for a headbutt," said Atwell.

‌



VAR, Jarred Gillett, responded: “He puts his head into Shaw with some force – that’s violent conduct. He stands up and into Shaw and there’s a movement of the head”.

Spurs were able to come back from behind despite being down a man against United. They were trailing thanks to Bryan Mbeumo's strike when the melee ensued.

Dominic Solanke was able to hold off Lisandro Martinez to gently glance the ball past Lammens to earn Spurs a point away from home.
