According to Fitch, the Outlook revision reflected ongoing reform of Nigeria’s policy framework and its increased confidence that the momentum will not be disrupted by upcoming elections.

It affirmed that the monetary and exchange rate reforms had supported greater naira flexibility, disinflation and faster-than-expected FX reserve accumulation, while improved reserve quality enhances resilience to shocks.



Fitch stressed that the continued reform implementation was strengthening monetary policy transmission and should support further disinflation, although inflation will remain well above Nigeria’s peers.

It said, “Nigeria’s ratings reflect its large economy, a relatively developed and liquid domestic debt market, large oil and gas reserves and an improved macroeconomic policy framework.



“The rating is constrained by weak governance indicators, high hydrocarbon dependence, high inflation, security challenges and structurally low government revenue relative to peers.”

On the expected policy continuity metric, Fitch said, “The incumbents are well positioned to win the early 2027 elections due to the ruling party’s control of the majority of Nigeria’s 36 states and a fragmented opposition.



“As a result, we expect broad economic policy continuity, including in relation to reforms that have contributed to improved policy credibility, higher external liquidity and enhanced resilience to external shocks.

“Risks to our baseline stem from significant policy slippage, including fiscal loosening, weaker capital inflows or major social instability.”



It also observed that gross FX reserves rose to $54.9 billion on September 25, 2026, from $32 billion in mid-April 2024, supported by increased formalisation of FX transactions, strong portfolio inflows and higher export receipts and remittances.

“We forecast the current account surplus will widen to 6.4% of GDP in 2026, but we expect it to narrow in 2027 amid our expectation that global oil prices will fall to 70/barrel from 87/barrel in 2026,” Fitch said.



Providing more context, it pointed out that reserve quality had improved as the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) reduced its FX liabilities, with net FX reserves at $34.8 billion at the end of 2025 from about $4 billion at the end of 2023.

“We expect the naira to trade broadly around the current level through end-2026, despite the prospect of lower oil prices in 2027-2028,” it stressed.



On restrictive monetary stance and reduced inflation, Fitch viewed the CBN’s September policy adjustment as a calibrated easing consistent with improving policy transmission.



Fitch said it expected the CBN to remain cautious amid high food and fuel prices and external risks, while forecasting average annual inflation to moderate, due to naira stability and tight monetary policy, to 15.4 per cent in 2026, less than half the 2024 level, but well above the forecast ‘B’ median of 5.6 per cent.



On higher oil production and refining, Fitch noted that crude oil production, excluding condensates, rose 10 per cent quarter -on-quarter (Q-on-Q) in 2Q26 and has met Nigeria’s 1.5mbpd OPEC target since May 2026, averaging 1.52mbpd.

“We expect production to remain around this level in the near term, supported by improved security and domestic investment, but below pre-pandemic levels.



“Dangote refinery’s ramp-up and rehabilitation of other facilities leading to increased production of refined products has reduced refined oil imports and FX demand, but limited domestic crude supply will partly maintain reliance on imported crude, Fitch said.

Overall, Fitch noted that Nigeria has a low World Bank Governance Indicators (WBGI) ranking at the 20th percentile, reflecting weak institutional capacity, uneven application of the rule of law and a high level of corruption.

Despite Nigeria’s positive outlook, the ratings agency outlined downside risks or sensitivities that could individually or collectively lead to negative rating action/downgrade.



They include: A deterioration in the credibility and consistency of monetary and fiscal policymaking and FX management, resulting in renewed inflationary pressures and greater distortions in the FX market.

It also cited renewed external liquidity stress arising, for example, due to lower oil prices and more constrained external financing sources.



Fitch also cited sustained widening of the fiscal deficit, which significantly increases the debt/GDP burden and weakens financing prospects.

Oyedele: Outlook Further Validates FG’s Difficult But Necessary Reforms

Reacting to Fitch’s positive outlook, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Oyedele, reaffirmed the federal government’s determination to sustain its reform momentum and a disciplined, market-reflective, and transparent foreign exchange regime.



Oyedele said Fitch’s latest action followed positive rating actions by all three major international rating agencies on Nigeria in 2026, citing S&P Global Ratings, which upgraded Nigeria to ‘B’ from ‘B-‘ in May, and Moody’s Ratings, which revised its outlook to Positive in August.



He noted that separately, FTSE Russell returned Nigeria to Frontier Market status with effect from September 21, 2026, adding that taken together, these decisions reflected a converging and increasingly favourable assessment of Nigeria’s reform trajectory.

The minister explained that Fitch’s Positive Outlook further validated the difficult but necessary reforms implemented under the current administration, saying its medium-term ambition was to place Nigeria firmly on the path to investment grade.



Oyedele assured that the administration would, among other things, focus on raising revenue through full implementation of the new tax laws and efficient tax administration, and improve fiscal governance through spending efficiency, budget execution, and transparent debt management.



According to him, the government would pursue structural reforms that support non-oil growth and economic diversification and accelerate the conversion of macroeconomic stability into shared prosperity through food security, decent jobs, human development, and support for small businesses.

World.title: 30 Days Petrol Discount: Atiku Accuses Tinubu of Turning NNPC into Political Spectacle
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of turning a petrol discount into a political spectacle at NNPC Limited’s expense.

The former vice president reminded President Tinubu that the petroleum corporation was no longer the NNPC of the old, but now a quoted limited liability company, according to the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA).

He said the PIA established the petroleum company to operate as a public liability-quoted company.

In a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said: “Tinubu wants Nigerians to cheer for ₦66 off a litre before they ask who ordered NNPC to surrender the money. He wants credit for the discount without showing the board approval, the cost or the account that will carry it. Nigerians are not so desperate for relief that they have forgotten how to ask a simple question: who pays for Tinubu’s applause?

“NNPC Limited is no longer the old NNPC corporation. The Petroleum Industry Act established it to operate as a commercial company. Yet the Presidency announces a discount, claims the applause and tells NNPC to surrender its margin. Is the government exercising its rights as shareholders through proper corporate channels, or treating NNPC Limited as a drawer of campaign money it can open whenever an election approaches?

“When Nigerians demand affordable petrol, Tinubu’s officials deliver a lecture about market forces. They say prices cannot be wished down. But when Tinubu needs a headline, the Presidency reaches into NNPC’s margin and calls it relief. Apparently, the market is sacred until the president needs applause”

Atiku questioned where Nigerians are supposed to find the relief when the NNPC Retail has just over 900 stations for a country of roughly 242 million people?

“That is a narrow network for a national promise. Motorists are already queuing at some outlets. Must a driver burn petrol travelling to an NNPC station, spend time in a queue, download an app and pay through it to save ₦66 on each litre? How much of the savings survives the journey?

“What happens to the family whose nearest NNPC station is miles away? What happens when a station runs out of petrol? Tinubu announces relief for the whole country, then delivers it through a fraction of its filling stations. A press release can reach every Nigerian in a second. His discount cannot.

“Where is NNPC’s board in this performance? Did it approve the decision before the Presidency announced it? What figures did it examine? What margin will the company forgo, and where will that cost appear in its accounts? Or was the board expected to discover its decision in the government’s press release?

“The administration says this is not a subsidy. Changing the name of a cost does not make it disappear.

He said after mocking the proposal for a transparent production subsidy, Tinubu turned around and borrowed its central lesson that Nigerians needed targeted relief.

World.title: 2027: Makinde Reaffirms Four-year Single Term, Says Tinubu Failed in His Electoral Promises
World.content:
*Challenges president to publish fuel pricing template

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde has expressed his commitment to a four-year term of government of national unity if elected president in 2027, insisting that his administration would not last beyond four years.



Makinde spoke yesterday at the APM’s North-east town hall meeting with stakeholders in Yola, Adamawa State, where he described President Bola Tinubu’s administration as a failure to deliver on all its electoral promises in 2023.

The governor said, ”I stand before you today to tell you that the government you will put in place from May 29, 2027, will be a transitional government of national unity.



”Our government will not last beyond four years. And it will be an all-inclusive government, Makinde said.

This clarification followed the popular agitation for presidential power to go to the North after eight years in the South.

The presidential candidate challenged the federal government to publish its petroleum pricing template to clarify how fuel prices are determined and ensure transparency, insisting that Nigerians have the right to know how fuel prices are determined.

He stated, “The current administration came in and told us that it had the magic wand to solve the challenges confronting us. In fact, the President said that if he failed to fix electricity for Nigeria in four years, Nigerians should not vote for him again. So, we are all aware that they have failed to provide electricity and other things they promised. So, I believe we all know how to cast our ballots.



“They came up with the presidential policy on CNG and electric vehicles. That policy failed. They introduced the naira-for-crude initiative. That policy also failed. Yesterday, I listened to the Minister of Finance on television. He said they are now adopting price modulation for petroleum products.



“We are asking for only two things. We do not want too much grammar; we want relief for Nigerians. So, we ask the federal government to release its pricing template so that citizens will know how they arrived at the current petroleum price and let Nigerians see how things go. If they have a better solution, they will present it.

“The fact that you are in government or the Presidential Villa does not make you the only Nigerians with sense. We have other citizens who can dissect issues and proffer solutions. So, please make your pricing template available to all, and we will make our input.”

The APM presidential candidate identified insecurity, poverty, and inadequate electricity supply as major challenges confronting Nigeria, stressing the need for urgent measures to tackle them.

Makinde said addressing the problems required a sincere approach and inclusive policies that would reflect the needs and aspirations of Nigerians.

He continued, “I want to say to you that 2027 will mark the end of the politics of lies and deceit. It is a time when we will all come together to establish a reset agenda and tell Nigerians the whole truth. Nigeria is home to several million people. We are the most populous Black nation on earth. We do not deserve what we are getting right now.

On his part, the National Leader of APM and Bauchi State Governor, Senator Bala Mohammed, said the party was emerging as a formidable opposition platform, highlighting its two governors and other elected representatives.

Mohammed added that the APM was gaining acceptance among Nigerians and expanding its membership, adding that the party had the political experience and leadership capacity needed to play a meaningful role in the country’s political development.

“APM is the number one opposition party in the country. We have two governors and other elected leaders. Whether we like it or not, we are a force to reckon with. We are a force to reckon with. Whoever does not reckon with us will do so at their peril.

“We have members with the experience and the knowledge. I can see people trooping into our party. I wish we had started this earlier, and I wish we had discovered APM a long time ago. But God’s time is the best. We are still not late.

Also speaking, the APM vice-presidential candidate, Mr Lawal Daura, said the party provided a platform for patriotic and honest Nigerians, stressing its commitment to tackling the country’s problems and setting Nigeria on a new path for the benefit of all citizens.

Daura thanked residents of the region for the warm welcome extended to the party’s delegation, adding that the APM would unveil its policies and programmes to Nigerians at the commencement of its nationwide campaign.

World.title: Sultan Urges Muslims to Sight Jumadal Ula Crescent Today
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA), Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has called on Muslims across the country to begin preparations for the sighting of the new crescent moon of Jumadal Ula 1448 AH today, October 11, 2026.

The directive, which underscored the importance of the Islamic lunar calendar in determining religious dates, was conveyed in a statement issued yesterday by the Wazirin Sokoto, by the Chairman of the Sultanate Council’s Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs, Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu.

According to the statement, Sunday, October 11, corresponds to the 29th day of Rabi’us Thani 1448 AH and has been designated for the nationwide moon-sighting exercise to determine the commencement of the Islamic month of Jumadal Ula.

The Sultan urged Muslims in all parts of Nigeria to actively participate in the exercise by observing the western horizon after sunset for any possible sighting of the new crescent.

The statement further directed anyone who successfully sights the crescent to promptly report the observation to the nearest district head or village head for onward communication to the Sultan.

The directive is in line with the established Islamic tradition of relying on the sighting of the new moon to determine the beginning of lunar months, subject to the appropriate religious authorities’ confirmation.

Muslims who observe the crescent are expected to provide accurate information through the recognised traditional and religious leadership structures to facilitate the verification and official announcement of the outcome.

The Sultan, as the nation’s leading traditional Islamic authority and President-General of the NSCIA, plays a central role in coordinating moon-sighting announcements that guide Muslims across the country in observing the Islamic calendar.

He called for cooperation among Islamic scholars, traditional rulers, community leaders and the wider Muslim population to ensure a credible and orderly reporting process.

The Sultan urged the Muslim faithful to remain attentive to official communication following the exercise, as the outcome of the sighting will determine the commencement of Jumadal Ula 1448 AH.

World.title: ActionAid Condemns Marriage of 33.4% of Underage Girls, Demands Enforcement of Child Marriage Laws
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

ActionAid Nigeria has called on federal and state governments to strengthen enforcement of laws against child marriage and increase investment in girls’ education and rights, warning that early marriage has deprived millions of Nigerian girls of opportunities to determine their futures.

The organisation, in a statement issued yesterday ahead of the 2026 International Day of the Girl, said 33.4 per cent of young Nigerian women aged 20 to 24 were married before the age of 18, with the prevalence approaching 50 per cent in the North-east and North-west.

The statement, signed by its Country Director, Andrew Mamedu, cited an analysis of the 2024 Demographic and Health Survey, alongside UNICEF estimates that more than 3.7 million women aged 20 to 24 were married before turning 18.

The International Day of the Girl, marked on October 11, is being observed this year under the theme, “End child marriage and invest in girls’ rights.”

ActionAid said child marriage was not merely a cultural practice or a family matter but a violation of girls’ rights that could disrupt their education, restrict their economic prospects and expose them to violence and early pregnancy.

It added that more than 12 million girls globally were married before adulthood every year, underscoring the need for sustained action by governments, communities and development partners.

The organisation identified poverty and limited access to education as major factors contributing to early marriage, noting that girls from poorer households and those with lower levels of education faced greater risks.

According to the statement, UNICEF analysis indicates that ensuring every girl in Northern Nigeria completes secondary education could reduce child marriage by as much as two-thirds, while also lowering adolescent pregnancy and improving economic productivity.

To illustrate the impact of interventions that empower girls, ActionAid recounted the experience of Aisha Aliyu, who was 16 when her family began preparing for her marriage to her cousin.

Aisha, who participated in the organisation’s Girl-led Research and Action Project, learnt about girls’ rights, the importance of education and the risks associated with early marriage.

Armed with that knowledge, she found the confidence to speak to her parents about her desire to continue her education. Her parents eventually called off the marriage, allowing her to return to school.

ActionAid said her experience demonstrated how access to information, safe spaces and opportunities for participation could help girls challenge practices that threatened their futures.

Through its Girl-led Research and Action initiative, the organisation supports girls to investigate issues affecting their lives, generate evidence and use their findings to advocate for change.

It also works with women’s rights organisations and communities through its Local Rights Programme to address harmful gender norms, violence, barriers to education and the exclusion of girls from decision-making.

The organisation said its Renewed Women’s Voice and Leadership Nigeria Project, funded by Global Affairs Canada, also supports locally led initiatives to advance gender equality and strengthen women’s and girls’ leadership.

Mamedu said investment in girls must go beyond protecting them from abuse to recognising their rights and enabling them to participate in decisions affecting their lives.

“Investing in girls is not simply about protecting them from harm; it is about recognising their rights, supporting their leadership and creating the opportunities they need to shape their own lives and contribute meaningfully to society,” he said.

World.title: Negative Perceptions Discouraging Youths from Joining Military, Says Soludo
World.content:
David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka

Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has said negative public perceptions of the military and other security agencies sometimes discourage young people from joining the services.

Soludo spoke at the weekend at the memorial service for the late Lt. Gen. Chikadibia Obiakor (rtd.) at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka.

He said the exemplary lives of officers such as Obiakor could inspire younger generations to embrace military service and other forms of national service.

The governor urged community leaders and elders to maintain close relationships with their people and serve as role models for younger generations.

Soludo described Obiakor as an illustrious son of Anambra State whose distinguished military career and international peacekeeping service brought honour to Nigeria.

“We have come to celebrate the life of one of our best,” he said.

He described the late general as “Anambra’s export to Nigeria and the world”, noting his global service in promoting peace and maintaining law and order.

However, Soludo stressed that an individual’s greatest achievement lay in the positive impact made on their immediate community.

“The impact on the community is the most important impact, that his people were able to testify that he was good,” he said.

The Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, expressed condolences to the Obiakor family and joined people of Anambra and Nigeria in mourning the late officer.

Oluyede was represented by the Director-General of the Nigerian Army Heritage and Future Centre, Maj.-Gen. Tariweriye Gagariga.

He described Obiakor as a decorated veteran whose distinguished service brought honour and dignity to the Nigerian Armed Forces.

Earlier, the deceased’s son, Mr. Nonso Obiakor, reflected on his father’s life, highlighting his discipline, international peacekeeping commitment and dedication to humanity.

The memorial service attracted family members, senior military officers, government officials and other mourners celebrating Obiakor’s contributions to Anambra State, Nigeria and the international community.

World.title: SANParks welcomes guilty verdict in decade-long rhino poaching case
World.content:
SANParks has welcomed the guilty verdict against former Kruger Park ranger Rodney Landela and Kenneth Mochocho over the illegal killing of a white rhino. Image: Wikimedia

South African National Parks (SANParks) has welcomed the guilty verdict against former Kruger National Park Regional Ranger, Rodney Landela, and former State Veterinary Service Animal Health Technician, Kenneth Mochocho, who were found guilty of the illegal hunting and killing of a white rhino in a protected area, as well as possession of a firearm with the intent to commit a crime.

READ | GOOD news on World Rhino Day: Decline in poaching

The judgement brings closure to a matter that has been before the courts for approximately 10 years and represents a significant victory in the fight against wildlife crime and the protection of South Africa’s natural heritage.



Found guilty

The accused initially faced six charges.

Four charges were subsequently withdrawn, namely theft relating to the stolen rhino horns, conspiracy to commit a crime, disposing of or tampering with evidence, and escaping from lawful custody.

The court found the pair guilty on the remaining charges of illegally hunting a protected species, namely a white rhino, and possession of a firearm with the intent to commit a crime.

The organisation commends the National Prosecuting Authority, investigators, law enforcement agencies, witnesses, and all individuals who contributed to ensuring that justice was ultimately served.

World.title: Pirates dealt injury scare as defender leaves MTN8 final on crutches
World.content:
Orlando Pirates could be without Kamogelo Sebelebele for their upcoming matches after the defender picked up an injury during their 2-0 defeat to Mamelodi Sundowns in the MTN8 final.

Goals from Teboho Mokoena and Iqraam Rayners handed Masandawana their first MTN8 title in five years, ending Pirates’ hopes of winning the competition for a fifth consecutive time.

For the Buccaneers, however, the defeat came at a cost, with Sebelebele potentially facing a spell on the sidelines.



The 23-year-old sustained an injury in the first half and was replaced by Oswin Appollis at half-time. The change did little to alter the course of the match, as Pirates struggled to find a way back into the contest.

What Sebelebele’s Injury Means for Pirates

Pirates could face a selection headache at right-back after parting ways with three players who could fill the position during the pre-season.

With Sebelebele potentially unavailable for the coming matches, head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou may have to convert Ghampani Lungu into a right-back.

Lungu started on the right wing against Sundowns but endured a difficult evening. The Zambian international struggled to make an impact and missed a penalty that could have given Pirates a route back into the contest.

The situation raises questions about Pirates’ decision to part ways with Thabiso Lebitso and Deano van Rooyen before the start of the campaign.

Had either player remained at the club, Ouaddou would have had another natural right-back option to call upon. He could have replaced the injured Sebelebele with one of them, allowing Lungu to move out of the firing line and making room for an attacking substitution, such as bringing on Mohau Nkota or Kabelo Kgositsile earlier in the second half.



Instead, Sebelebele’s potential absence could leave the Pirates coach with limited options as the team looks to recover from the disappointment of losing the MTN8 final.

The defender was seen on crutches after the match, raising concerns about the severity of his injury. However, the extent of the injury and how long he could be sidelined remain unclear.

Pirates will hope Sebelebele’s setback is not serious, as his absence could create further selection problems for Ouaddou in the coming matches.

Who should replace Sebelebele?

World.title: Transfer report: The Premier League and La Liga teams targeting Bafana star
World.content:
Olwethu Makhanya plays for Bafana Bafana against Guinea at the Orlando Amstel Arena. Image: Olwethu Makhanya Instagram

Bafana Bafana’s Olwethu Makhanya is the subject of interest from Brentford in the English Premier League, while Sevilla are monitoring him in Spain. In Italy, Bologna are keeping tabs on the Rangers FC central defender.

“Brentford, Sevilla & Bologna closely monitoring Rangers CB Olwethu Makhanya (22, South Africa) after his impressive start,” Turkish transfer reporter Ekrem Konur revealed.

BAFANA BAFANA’S OLWETHU MAKHANYA MAKES A NAME IN SCOTLAND

The former Marumo Gallants and Stellenbosch FC star joined Rangers FC from Philadelphia Union in Major League Soccer.



Makhanya’s defensive performances have helped Rangers record seven clean sheets in his first 11 consecutive starts across all competitions. His growing partnership with Emmanuel Fernandez has also strengthened the team’s defensive unit.

The South African international’s impressive performances earned him the Scottish Premiership Player of the Month award for September 2026.

He has also impressed in high-profile matches against Celtic, including a 1-0 victory at Celtic Park and a 3-0 win in the Scottish League Cup.

A move to one of Europe’s major leagues would represent another significant step in Makhanya’s career. However, the reported interest has not yet confirmed a formal bid or an agreement with Rangers.

SOUTH AFRICANS IN ENGLAND, SPAIN AND ITALY

A catalogue of Mzansi footballers have graced the shores of England, Spain and Italy.

In the English Premier League, Lucas Radebe became a Leeds United legend, while Steven Pienaar impressed at Everton and Benni McCarthy featured for Blackburn Rovers. Quinton Fortune played for Manchester United, while Mbulelo Mabizela and Bongani Khumalo turned out for Tottenham Hotspur. More recently, Lyle Foster continued the South African presence in England with Burnley, as well as Percy Tau at Brighton & Hove Albion.



In Spain’s La Liga, Fortune represented Atlético Madrid and Mallorca, while McCarthy played for Celta Vigo. Defender Nasief Morris featured for Recreativo de Huelva and Racing Santander, while Tsepo Masilela made 13 appearances for Getafe. Sizwe Motaung and David Nyathi also represented CD Tenerife.

In Italy’s Serie A, Phil Masinga became a fan favourite at Bari. Defender Mark Fish played for Lazio before moving to England, while Siyabonga Nomvethe featured for Udinese and Empoli. Midfielder Eric Tinkler also played for Cagliari.

World.title: Two teams fight for Malcolm Marx’s prized signature
World.content:
The Sharks have reportedly entered the race to sign star Springbok hooker Malcolm Marx from his Japanese side. Image: Bokrugby/ Instagram

The Sharks have reportedly entered the race to sign Springbok hooker Malcolm Marx, potentially complicating the Bulls‘ efforts to bring the double Rugby World Cup winner back to South Africa.

According to reports on Sunday, the Sharks are exploring the possibility of recruiting the 32-year-old, who is currently contracted to Japan’s Kubota Spears until June 2027.

The Bulls have made no secret of their interest in Marx and have reportedly been pursuing his signature for the past two months.



However, they could now face competition from their United Rugby Championship (URC) rivals in Durban, where uncertainty surrounding Bongi Mbonambi’s future has added to the Sharks’ need to consider their options at hooker.

Sharks explore Malcolm Marx move

Sharks coach JP Pietersen, general manager Dave Williams and head of recruitment and retention Ruan Jacobs have reportedly already discussed the possibility of signing Marx.

The potential move comes amid uncertainty surrounding Mbonambi, who is reportedly facing an internal disciplinary hearing over alleged misconduct during a Sharks team-building session.



Fellow hooker Fez Mbatha is also dealing with a leg injury, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the position.

Marx, a key member of South Africa’s successful Rugby World Cup campaigns in 2019 and 2023, would bring considerable international experience to either franchise.

However, with his Japanese contract running until June 2027, any move would depend on the circumstances surrounding his existing agreement and the possibility of securing his services.



Best hooker in the world

Marx, unquestionable the best hooker in world rugby, has played 94 Tests for the Springboks, scoring a record 29 tries for a South African forward.

He is also the reigning World Rugby Player of the Year and SA Rugby Player of the Year.

READ | John Smit: Malcolm Marx is South Africa’s best ever hooker

World.title: Springboks hang onto World Rugby No 1 ranking despite big All Blacks win
World.content:
The All Blacks beat Australia in the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park in Auckland, but stayed at No 2 in the World Rugby rankings. Image: AFP

The All Blacks beat Australia in the first of two Bledisloe Cup Tests at Eden Park in Auckland on Saturday.

New Zealand won 50-19 after leading 17-14 at half-time.

The second Bledisloe Cup match will take place in Sydney next weekend.



READ | All Blacks pay heavy price for Bledisloe Cup win

Springboks still No 1

However, New Zealand’s impressive win was not enough to see them overtake the Springboks at the summit of the World Rugby rankings.

The win saw the Kiwis add 0.66 World Rugby ranking points, while the Wallabies lost an equivalent amount.



New Zealand moved to 91.81 points, 1.28 behind the Springboks.

Meanwhile, despite their heavy defeat, Australia remained in sixth place on 84.89 points.

World.title: Tragedy as 9-year-old boy drowns at Kleinmond Lagoon
World.content:
A nine-year-old boy has died after being found underwater at Kleinmond Main Beach Lagoon. Despite extensive CPR efforts, paramedics could not save him. Image: Facebook

A nine-year-old boy has died after being discovered underwater at Kleinmond Main Beach Lagoon in the Western Cape on Saturday, 10 October.

The National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) Kleinmond duty crew was activated at 15:12 following eyewitness reports of a drowning in progress.

Visiting the beach

According to NSRI Kleinmond station commander Schalk Boonzaaier, the child had been visiting the beach with his family when the incident occurred.



Bystanders were already attempting to recover the boy from the water when emergency responders arrived. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was started by bystanders, including a clinical practitioner.

NSRI rescue swimmers and medics responded alongside the Critical Care Medical ambulance service, ER24, Overstrand Fire and Rescue Service and the South African Police Service (SAPS).

Extensive efforts to save boy

NSRI medics continued CPR after arriving at the scene, with paramedics joining the resuscitation efforts.



Despite extensive attempts to save the child’s life, he was declared deceased by paramedics after all efforts to resuscitate him had been exhausted.

His body was handed over to the police and the Government Health Forensic Pathology Service.

Police are providing support to the child’s family following the tragedy.



Police open inquest

SAPS has opened an inquest docket to investigate the circumstances surrounding the drowning.

The NSRI has conveyed its condolences to the family of the deceased boy.

The incident serves as a tragic reminder of the dangers associated with water, particularly at beaches and lagoons where conditions can change unexpectedly.



The circumstances surrounding the incident have not yet been established.

World.title: Shocking figures reveal rise in rape allegations against SAPS officers
World.content:
IPID registered 116 rape cases against police officers in 2025/26. Image: Pexels, for illustrative purposes

Rape allegations against police officers in South Africa have increased, with the Independent Police Investigative Directorate (IPID) recording 116 cases during the 2025/2026 financial year.

That is up from 95 cases in the previous financial year, while 72 of the allegations reportedly involved officers who were on duty when the incidents occurred.

The figures have renewed calls for police officers accused of rape and gender-based violence to be suspended while allegations are investigated.



IPID is responsible for investigating serious allegations of misconduct and criminality involving members of the South African Police Service (SAPS).

What IPID’s figures reveal

The 116 rape cases formed part of 332 gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF) cases recorded against police officers during the financial year.

According to the reported figures, the cases included:

122 referrals , mainly involving domestic violence.

, mainly involving domestic violence. 116 rape cases.

58 assault and torture cases.

24 murder cases.

10 cases involving the discharge of an official firearm.

Overall, IPID registered 5,259 cases of alleged police misconduct during the 2025/2026 financial year.

The increase in rape allegations has raised further questions about accountability within the police service, particularly when officers are accused of committing offences while on duty.

It is important to note that registered allegations do not necessarily result in convictions.



How many cases reach court?

IPID investigators made 281 arrests during the financial year.

By 31 March 2026, a total of 994 cases had been enrolled in court following recommendations by IPID that the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) prosecute police officers.

SAPS also concluded 277 disciplinary recommendations referred by IPID, with sanctions ranging from written warnings to dismissal.

IPID secured 84 criminal convictions during the year, including 26 relating to GBVF cases.

The figures highlight the different stages involved in dealing with alleged police misconduct, from the initial investigation and arrest to prosecution, disciplinary action and conviction.

DA calls for accused officers to be suspended

On 5 October, the Democratic Alliance (DA) called for all police officers accused of rape and GBVF to be immediately suspended from service.

The party also called for allegations to be investigated swiftly and thoroughly, with officers found guilty facing dismissal.

According to the DA, the 116 rape cases recorded by IPID amount to an alleged rape involving a police officer being reported approximately every three days.

The Independent Policing Union of South Africa (IPUSA) has also expressed concern about the figures.

IPUSA president Bethuel Nkuna highlighted the gap between the number of cases registered and the number of convictions.

The calls have placed renewed focus on how SAPS handles allegations against its own members and what measures are needed to protect victims while investigations are under way.

Concerns over police screening and accountability

Questions about police accountability have also been raised over the screening of officers against the National Register for Sex Offenders (NRSO).

A parliamentary reply in 2025 reportedly revealed that only 245 of the police service’s approximately 180 000 members had been screened against the register.

Separately, Build One South Africa (BOSA) said fewer than 5% of police officers accused of murder and rape had been referred for prosecution.

These figures have contributed to concerns about the effectiveness of existing safeguards and the consequences faced by officers accused of serious crimes.

Police face renewed scrutiny

The latest figures come amid wider concerns about gender-based violence in South Africa, where violence against women remains a serious social challenge.

Separately, suspended deputy national police commissioner Lieutenant-General Shadrack Sibiya has appeared in court on charges including rape, human trafficking and child sexual grooming. He has not been convicted, and that case is unrelated to IPID’s annual figures.

The allegations against individual officers must be determined through the appropriate legal processes. However, the rising number of reported cases has intensified calls for stronger oversight and accountability within the police service.

The South African has approached SAPS for comment on the figures and the DA’s demand for the suspension of officers accused of rape and GBVF. A response had not been received at the time of publication.

This article will be updated if SAPS responds.

World.title: Ex-Sundowns star sparks controversy with Soweto Derby comment
World.content:
Simba SC star attacker Keletso Makgalwa has South African football fans talking following the comment he made about the Soweto Derby.

Makgalwa was with his Simba teammates for their 10-day training camp in Polokwane ahead of their clash with arch-rivals Yanga SC.

And speaking to iDiski Times about what it meant to play in the Kariakoo Derby, Makgalwa said it is just unexplainable.



Where the 29-year-old infuriated South African fans was when he placed the Kariakoo Derby ahead of the Soweto Derby.

It is worth mentioning that Makgalwa has never played a Soweto Derby as he was at Mamelodi Sundowns before moving to Sekhukhune United.

EX-SUNDOWNS STAR MAKGALWA PUTS KARIAKOO DERBY AHEAD OF SOWETO DERBY

“The atmosphere of that derby is wow, I can’t explain it,” said Makgalwa.

“That game is tough, to be honest, because it’s a Tanzanian Derby, and the fans demand a lot.

“I think, to be honest, it’s a better derby than the one we have in South Africa, the Soweto Derby,” he added.

SIMBA BEAT YANGA IN KARIAKOO DERBY

The two teams – Simba and Yanga – met in the Kariakoo Derby on Saturday, and for the first time in history, this titanic clash involved two South African coaches in Steve Barker and Manqoba Mngqithi.



Simba got the better of Yanga on the day, beating them 2-1, thanks to goals from Neo Maema and Elie Mpanzu who was assisted by Makgalwa himself.

Yanga had opened the scoring in the 6th minute through former Sundowns striker Peter Shalulile who left them at the end of last season.

World.title: Pastor accused of killing 4-month-old baby arrested
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - An alleged Gauteng pastor is expected to appear before the Atteridgeville Magistrate's Court on Monday.

This is in connection with the murder of a four-month-old baby and the rape of her mother.

Officers found the 36-year-old hiding in a back room at an informal settlement in Diepsloot.

Police said the man and his two wives had accompanied the mother and infant to the Hennops River in Pretoria, for a ritual earlier this week.

He had gone ahead with the 43-year-old mother, leaving the baby with his wives.

Police understand that’s when the woman was raped before she managed to escape.

The infant’s body was later discovered in a shallow grave near the river.

The pastor’s two wives have already been arrested, one of them led police to the baby’s body.

World.title: Four killed in KwaMsane tavern
World.content:
ESHOWE – A police constable allegedly shot and killed three women and injured a man before turning the gun on himself at a tavern in KwaMsane, KwaZulu-Natal.

Police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said police responded to reports of a shooting at a liquor establishment at Nkodibe area in KwaMsane, and when they arrived they found four bodies with gunshot wounds, and one victim with a gunshot wound who was taken to hospital.

“It was reported that the off-duty police constable also disarmed another man of his firearm during the incident. Both firearms were found at the scene. The cause of the shooting is unknown at this stage.”

In a separate incident, police in Eshowe are tracing a suspect who allegedly shot and killed three people at a grocery chain store in Eshowe on Saturday.

“Reports indicate that the suspect, who is former employee of the store, had gone to the store for his internal disciplinary hearing. The suspect allegedly produced a firearm and shot three people who were declared dead at the scene. A manhunt for the suspect is underway.”

World.title: SANDF arrives in Durban
World.content:
DURBAN - The army has been spotted in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, amid tensions over asylum applications and illegal immigration.

Protests erupted after the Constitutional Court ruling that everyone must be given a fair chance to apply for asylum, regardless of documentation.

Violent unrest led to looting and the torching of vehicles.

Government has called for calm as tensions simmer.

World.title: Joburg Water warns of possible outages
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A power outage at the Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant has crippled pumping at the Palmiet Booster Station.

Johannesburg Water warns that parts of Sandton, Diepsloot, Rabie Ridge, and surrounding areas could face low water pressure or total outages.

The utility said it is monitoring the system and taking steps to stabilise supply.

Residents are urged to use water sparingly.

World.title: ‘Captured’ casts spotlight on prison life
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Ex-Pollsmoor Correctional Centre inmates are using visual art to depict the realities of life behind bars.

This they say helps them deal with past trauma, their reintegration into society, and also to make a living.

Dubbed "Captured", the visual storytelling project, is set to eventually become a coffee table book.

Life behind bars is often reduced to statistics, without the human factor.

Enrico Samuels, an artist, served sixteen years behind bars for armed robbery said art connected him with people helping him to navigate life now as a free man.

"I want to become a successful artist, doctor is helping me to get there with the projects...lovely projects and I enjoy myself in the projects and from there I see a brighter future from doc's side, because she is taking me that way, so I can see the sun on the other side already,” said Samuels.

Michael Sauls said art serves as a conduit in helping them deal with their past and educate the public.

“People have no an idea of what prison is like, they think that everything is happy go-lucky or it's like a journey to another paradise, it's not worth it being there...you see it's easy to commit a crime, but it's not easy serving the time."

Dr Suzette Leal, the founder of Words Set Free, said the art tells the stories of the people behind it.

"If you say the work is beautiful, that's a complement to our artists and their ability, but the story is not beautiful. It's real and true and painful and traumatic. So, I think if anything I hope it discourages someone from getting involved in crime, but I think we don't reduce crime by making prison sentences longer or by making the conditions within them worse. We reduce crime by creating opportunities for people to create a livelihood outside of crime.”

Another artist, Kleinbooi Hendricks said: "I said to myself, although the parole board gave me a date to go out of prison, I'm not going. I will either complete my entire sentence but I'm not going out if I haven't worked on myself being a changed man or a different person. I did that because I said I'd either eat out of a dustbin outside, but I'm not going to commit crime again."

World.title: Change living conditions – Ndlozi
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Real change begins with communities taking responsibility for their own development.

Those are the views of Dr Mbuyiseni Ndlozi, Founder of the Batho Pele Convention.

The initiative calls on South Africans to take the lead in improving their own living conditions.

“We are here to say you are the solution you are looking for. We are here to say you are the saviour, the developer, the healer and the builder you are looking for. We are here to vote for you to do it on your own.

“We are here to say you are the saviours you are looking for. We are not a corporate think tank. Long have we interpreted our misery from broadcast to podcast, think shops to talk shops.

“The point is to change our living conditions, one pothole at a time, one classroom at a time and one production hub at a time,” Ndlozi said.

World.title: Repairs delay Joburg's pool reopenings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg's public pools are missing out on the summer rush.

And most are still closed despite the rising temperatures.

Community leader Dulton Adams said poor planning, lack of proper budgeting and no clear management plans, are leaving residents without these facilities.

The city has 57 public pools, but only 13 are open so far.

Ten more are expected to open on Monday.

"Every season there's just no budget.

There's just no management plan. There's no vision to make sure that the children come off the streets and you look at the pool. This is not the only pool.

"Remember spring day, pools must open first. Then the City Council asked for 1 October, pools would be open. That was missed and then now the 7th," Adams said.

World.title: ‘ANC could be the biggest loser’ - political strategist
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC could emerge as the biggest loser in this year's municipal elections.

This is the view is political strategist Brutus Malada.

He said the party’s declining support could leave it with less influence across key metros and this could push it into a weakened position ahead of the 2029 elections.

“ANC will be the big loser in this. The trend is clear. It's clear that they are losing at a margin of 10 to 12 percent and that will actually mean the end of the ANC and it will become lame duck for this period in between the two elections.

“That it will sit, it will be a national government President Ramaphosa sitting in Tshwane. The Union Buildings which is led by another party and in Cape Town which is the legislative arm of the state which is led by the DA.

“So here is a political party that is running the country as the head of the State but it has no control of the economy hub, it has no control of administrative hub, it has no control of legislative hub,” Malada said.
