The courtâs intervention followed the CJPâs call for a mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar, alongside student organisations, demanding action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission.

The government thwarted the planned demonstration through an extensive security crackdown across the national capital. More than 7,000 protesters were detained, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.

World.title: 'Will talk about undeclared Emergency': Kharge says Congress to meet CJI over ‘vote chori’ allegations
World.content:
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Sunday said party leaders would meet the Chief Justice of India (CJI) to raise concerns over the functioning of constitutional institutions, while accusing the BJP of coming to power through âvote choriâ and alleging that the country was witnessing an âundeclared Emergencyâ.

According to ANI, Kharge said he and senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had written letters to the CJI and that a meeting had been scheduled between 4 pm and 5 pm. He clarified that the delegation would present its concerns rather than demand any specific action.

âWe can't demand anything from him. Only with folded hand we'll request them,â Kharge said in Bengaluru.

Kharge also alleged that the Election Commission was not being allowed to function independently and claimed that concerns over irregularities within the poll body had gone unaddressed.

âThe CEC is a constitutional body. They are independent. They can take independent decisions. But he is not allowing them to take independent decisions,â he said.

Referring to concerns raised by two Election Commission members, Kharge alleged that irregularities in the commission's functioning had been exposed but no action had followed. He claimed that the government wanted âvote choriâ to continue and alleged that electoral malpractice had helped the BJP form governments at the Centre and in states.





âWhatever 'vote chori' he has done, with that only, he has formed the government in the Centre and the states,â Kharge said.

Kharge also criticised the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, questioning the legal protection it provides to election commissioners for acts performed in the discharge of their official duties.

âThat immunity he gave. That immunity is not even for the President of India, not the Chief Justice, but that is given to one Election Commissioner. Why?â he said.

Kharge alleged that the provision weakened accountability and linked it to electoral irregularities involving electronic voting machines (EVMs). Calling it a conspiracy against democracy, he said, âIt means that it is a conspiracy to snatch votes and commit fraud on democracy, and he is doing all that, and we'll fight it.â

Kharge further accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah of creating an atmosphere of fear and political instability, describing the situation as an âundeclared Emergencyâ.

Referring to the deployment of nearly 32,000 police personnel during protests, he questioned the scale of the security arrangements and said they reflected the government's apprehension.

âYesterday, nearly 32,000 policemen were deployed. That itself shows how much fear he has,â Kharge said.

World.title: 'Starlink poses risk to security agencies': BJP MP Nishikant Dubey responds to Musk's charge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on Sunday hit back at SpaceX CEO

amid the dispute over Starlinkâs entry into India, alleging that the satellite internet service poses challenges to the countryâs security agencies and asserting that India would not change its security policy under pressure.

In a post on X, Dubey, chairman of a parliamentary committee, said the panel had examined the challenges faced by country's security agencies in connection with Starlink.

âThe ministry of defence, the ministry of home affairs, and our investigation agencies are being affected by the dangerous games of these threats,â Dubey wrote.

He also claimed that the government led by former prime minister Manmohan Singh had alerted the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) to such threats in 2013-14.

Urging Musk to focus on making internet services affordable in the United States before criticising India, Dubey said the country was a sovereign democracy and would not alter its security policy in response to pressure or social media posts.

âFirst, provide connections to the poor in your own country, America, at affordable rates, and then level accusationsâIndia is a healthy democratic, sovereign nation; it does not change its security policy under pressure or social media,â he said.





Dubey added that if financial considerations alone determined the government's decisions, it would have welcomed Starlink despite objections from security agencies.

âIf our policy were driven by money, we would have rolled out the red carpet welcome for you despite opposition from the security agencies,â he wrote.

Musk's allegations over Starlink's India entry

Dubey's remarks came after Musk argued that Starlink's entry would increase competition and give Indian consumers more choices.

SpaceX chief criticised what he described as arguments by supporters of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani against the satellite internet service.

âThe reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambaniâs profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business,â Musk wrote.

The exchange follows Musk's earlier allegations that influential business groups were obstructing Starlink's entry to protect their market positions.

He had also addressed Ambani as âPrime Minister Ambaniâ and accused him of seeking to preserve a monopoly.

The government has rejected the suggestion that Starlink is being singled out, saying commercial operations depend on regulatory and security clearances.

At the India Mobile Congress 2026 in New Delhi, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said India would not allow a monopoly in any sector.

Starlink, Reliance Jio Satcom and Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb have received licences, but the government has said security clearances remain pending for the operators. The satellite spectrum pricing framework is also being finalised.

World.title: ‘We cannot let this become normal’: AISA's Neha Bora on Delhi protest crackdown
World.content:
NEW DELHI: AISA leader Neha Bora on Sunday criticised the police crackdown on protesters in Delhi, saying, âwe cannot let this become normal,â following massive demonstrations held in national capital on October 10 demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

âWhen those sworn to protect the Constitution look away, the people must remind them what it demands. We cannot let this become normal. The fight for democracy continues, and we will not look away,â Bora said in a post on X.

Bora was among 7,000 protesters who were detained as police prevented protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar. Among those detained were also AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal and former chief ministers Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar.

Her detention came after CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were taken into custody by Delhi Police shortly after arriving at Indira Gandhi International Airport from Mumbai.

Supreme Court hear pleas over detentions

The Supreme Court is holding a special hearing on Sunday on petitions challenging the preventive detention of thousands of protesters, including opposition leaders.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The court has assured lawyers that it would hear all parties in the matter concerning the police action during protests in Delhi and ensure that no inconvenience was caused.





âWe know things have really disturbed all of you. That's why all of you are here. Not to trivialize,â Justice Joymalya Bagchi told the lawyers during the hearing.

Senior advocate Kapil Sibal submitted his plea challenging the detentions and the imposition of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which restricts assemblies under specified circumstances. Sibal told the court that people were being picked up from trains, raising concerns over the detention of individuals travelling to Delhi. He also flagged the suspension of internet services, news agency ANI reported.

World.title: 'Sikh sentiments hurt': Gurdwara body questions protesters, police for intrusion into premises
World.content:
DSGMC chief Harmeet Singh Kalka slams protesters and police over the Gurdwara Bangla Sahib incident

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Sikh Gurdwara management committee (DSGMC) has criticised protesters for entering Gurdwara Bangla Sahib during October 10 demonstrations in Delhi, saying the incident "hurt Sikh sentiments".DSGMC president Harmeet Singh Kalka alleged that some protesters had entered the premises with placards and raised slogans, and attempted to force their way into a hall but were stopped by gurdwara staff.âIt is deeply distressing to see attempts being made to turn Gurudwara Bangla Sahib into a political arena. This is a sacred institutionâa place where people come to offer prayers and seek relief from their suffering. Yet, protesters intruded and attempted to stage a demonstration there, deeply hurting Sikh sentiments,â Kalka said.He added, âOne may offer prayers inside the Gurudwara, but protests are not permitted.âKalka also questioned the criticism of police action, while objecting to uniformed personnel walking through the shrineâs grounds.âThe sight of police personnel walking through the Gurudwara premises hurts the hearts of the Sikh community.It is absolutely intolerable for police in uniform to traverse the Gurudwara grounds, as this is not a public thoroughfare,â he said.At the same time, he asked what the police were expected to do if protesters entered the premises to demonstrate. âAfter police entered to remove them, a big issue was made... If miscreants enter the premises, what will police do if not remove them? Would you prefer protesters to sloganeer inside the gurdwara?â he said.Accusing AAP leaders of politicising the episode, Kalka said the gurdwara could not be used as a venue for demonstrations. âI want to say this bluntlyâ No no one has the right to protest inside a gurdwara and we wonât tolerate any politics over this issue.He added that the committeeâs responsibility was to preserve the sanctity of the shrine, which provides food and shelter to people regardless of background.Several protesters, fearing detention, took shelter at the gurdwara in central Delhi as security was tightened across the capital.

World.title: 'No breach of peace for one year': Delhi court's condition for release of Dipke, Das, Ranka
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A Delhi executive magistrate court on Sunday ordered the release of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke,

and Ashutosh Ranka on the condition that they do not engage in any "breach of peace for one year", the party's legal affairs head Ratna Singh said.

Delhi Police informed that a bail bond as surety bond of Rs 50,000 was filled for "maintaining peace and good behaviour" for a period of one year.

The CJP leaders are set to hold a press conference at 2pm on Sunday.

Delhi Police detained them from their flight shortly after they landed in the national capital on Saturday to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Delhi Police said it had registered more than 20 FIRs over attempts to forcibly hold a protest on October 10.

The cases include charges related to disturbing law and order, obstructing government work and assaulting police personnel. Four people have been detained in connection with the cases, police said.

World.title: 'Interference in internal affairs': India rebukes UN human rights body over Delhi protest crackdown
World.content:
'Extreme selectivity': India flags UN rights body's 'double standards' over Delhi crackdown (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India on Sunday rejected the UN human rights body's concerns over the security crackdown ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed protest in Delhi, calling them âunwarrantedâ and an âunacceptable interferenceâ in the country's internal affairs.In a statement, the ministry of external affairs said "India is the worldâs largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by our Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media."âAs in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to the maintenance of public order and safety. Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for the redressal of any grievances,â the ministry said.The MEA also accused the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) of being selective in its public statements, alleging that it had remained silent on violent responses to protests in neighbouring countries and law enforcement actions closer to its own headquarters.âSuch double standards only erode the credibility of its standing and contribute to the loss of faith in multilateralism,â the statement said.The response came a day after the UN human rights chief expressed concern over reports of mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, civil society members, lawyers and journalists before and during large-scale demonstrations in Delhi.âWe call on the authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly is fully respected and fulfilled. Restrictions on peaceful protests must meet strict tests of necessity and proportionality,â the high commissioner for human rights said.The proposed CJP demonstration sought the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR of electoral rolls. The protest was met with a heavy security deployment and crackdown, and several political leaders and demonstrators were detained.

World.title: ‘Partisan role’: RJD leader moves SC over Delhi Police action, alleges sexual harassment of women protesters
World.content:

) MP Manoj Jha has approached the

challenging the

Plea alleges mass detentions, disruption of public services

Jha has sought a declaration that the police action between October 9 and 10, including detentions, internet suspension, restrictions on Metro and train services, and the alleged disproportionate use of force, was illegal.

World.title: Anti-CEC protest LIVE updates: Supreme Court directs authorities to ensure free movement in Delhi, bars illegal detentions
World.content:
Following the detention of thousands of people, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has called for another round of protests in Delhi on Sunday (October 11, 2026) to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities. Leaders of youth and student organisations have vowed to continue their protest until all their demands are met.

CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were kept in detention for nearly 24 hours since they landed in Delhi, were released by the Executive Magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station, the CJP’s legal head Ratna Singh said on Sunday morning (October 11, 2026). Meanwhile, YouTube Dhruv Rathee has also been released, a spokesperson for the Gurugram police said, adding that no charges were pressed against him.

Check out | Protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar | Highlights from October 10, 2026

Nearly 2,500 protesters were detained across the capital on Saturday (October 10, 2026), the Delhi Police sources said. These were in addition to around 1,000 people picked up in preventive operations across Delhi overnight ahead of the protest day. The Office of the United Nations Human Rights Commissioner (OHCHR) said it was “concerned” by reports of “mass detentions” at the Delhi protests, a statement that the government rejected.

World.title: DRI officials seize 5.832 kg of gold worth ₹8.98 crore near Visakhapatnam
World.content:
Officials of the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) seized about 5.832 kg of gold, worth about ₹8.98 crore, from a car near Visakhapatnam.

Acting on specific intelligence, the DRI team intercepted a car travelling from Kolkata to Hyderabad on Friday (October 9, 2026) and seized the yellow metal — 24-carat gold of foreign origin.

The gold was smuggled through the India-Bangladesh border and was being transported to Hyderabad, DRI officials said in a release on Sunday (October 11, 2026). The accused had concealed the gold biscuits in a cabin created for smuggling, beneath the leg space of the front co-passenger seat in the car, the officials said.

The two persons smuggling the gold have been arrested. The accused were produced in court and remanded to judicial custody.

The gold was seized under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962, and a detailed investigation is on. DRI officers are trying to determine the origin and destination of the seized gold, and the kingpin of the racket.

World.title: Environment group in Chennai provides  ‘Golden Wings’ to women in Vedanthangal
World.content:
Until recently, for some of the women living around Vedanthangal, the birds they saw every day were simply part of the landscape. Today, they are part of their life, even the sounds of these avians being familiar to these women’s now-trained ears. That transformation was engineered by a nature-guide training programme from Chennai-based Care Earth Trust.

With the two-fold objective of increasing biodiversity awareness and providing livelihood opportunities, the programme began with women and young people from around Vedanthangal, training them in bird identification, wetland ecology, identification of trees butterflies, and communication skills. After months of classroom lessons and practical sessions, a group of eight trained participants have come together as ‘Golden Wings’ and are now conducting guided walks at Vedanthangal.

Vedanthangal resident S. Kalaiselvi Srinivasan, now a Golden Wings guide, says the work has given her an income opportunity as well as improved her communication skills.

For Subathirai D, however, the journey began with skepticism from those around her. When she first started attending the training, women in her neighbourhood questioned why she was spending her time on it. To them, learning about birds and nature seemed unnecessary, especially when she could be spending that time on household responsibilities or other work. But that perception began to change when Subathirai returned from the training and started earning through nature walks.

This is precisely the larger idea behind the project, says B. Ramamoorthy, Project Coordinator at Care Earth Trust. The organisation wanted to address two issues at once: the limited awareness among local communities about the biodiversity around them and the lack of livelihood opportunities for women in villages such as Vedanthangal.

The team worked through the panchayat, went around houses to explain the programme and spoke to families when women were hesitant to participate. Childcare was arranged during training and nature walks, food was provided, and the women themselves suggested Sundays as the most convenient day for classes.

The initial training involved classroom sessions using colour printouts and presentations to teach the participants about different birds, trees and butterflies. They then moved to practical walks, where they learnt to identify birds through their appearance and calls and understand local and native trees and their uses. They were also taken on a week-long exposure visit to Thattekad in Kerala to learn about forest biodiversity and migratory birds. The training did not stop with bird identification. The women were taught spoken English, people management and social-media skills.

For Anjana Venkatesan, Programme Manager – Policy Research at Care Earth Trust, the project is about creating a connection between local women and the ecotourism circuit while drawing attention to the biodiversity outside Chennai. “Connecting them to the local kind of ecotourism circuit is a win-win for both of us,” she said. She also wants to challenge the perception that people have to travel to the Western Ghats to experience rich bird diversity. “Right in the outskirts of Chennai, you have these pockets with our existing forests and existing wetlands,” she said, adding that some of these areas record around 70 bird species during the migratory season.

The next phase of the programme is now taking shape in Unamancheri, Vandalur, where women are undergoing training. Among them is 29-year-old Madhumitha S., a B.Sc graduate who works in medical coding. Originally from Medavakkam, she moved to Unamancheri after marriage and has been attending the Sunday classes for around two months.

For Madhumitha, the training has meant discovering a side of the place she now calls home. Before joining the programme, she was familiar mainly with common birds. The classes introduced her to a much wider range of birds, trees, butterflies and other species. She said the experience was a completely new subject for her and that she found learning about birds and other species interesting. Having grown up in the city, she also noticed the difference after moving towards the more interior parts of Vandalur, where she began seeing peacocks and deer.

Madhumitha is now learning how to handle tourists, engage them and conduct nature walks. She plans to continue her medical-coding job during the week and take up nature walks on weekends after completing her training.

For Anjana, the project is also changing the organisation itself. “We’re not going in with this knowledge. It’s something that we’re learning and adapting as we go along,” she said. For the women at Vedanthangal, the training has opened up opportunities they may not have considered before. They are now guiding visitors through the birds and trees they grew up around. In Unamancheri, women like Madhumita are only beginning to learn about this world. For them, the journey is just starting.

World.title: Osmania junior doctors to protest on October 12 over training, working conditions
World.content:
The Osmania Medical College Junior Doctors Association (OMC JUDA) has announced a protest at Osmania General Hospital (OGH) in Hyderabad on Monday (October 12, 2026) demanding urgent action on long-pending issues affecting postgraduate training, clinical learning, working conditions and patient care.

According to an official strike notice issued on October 10, the protest will begin at 8.30 a.m. at the main gate of OGH. The association has called on interns, undergraduate students, postgraduate residents, senior residents and representatives from all departments to participate in large numbers.

OMC JUDA said several critical issues continued to affect the functioning of hospital departments and the quality of postgraduate training despite repeated representations to the authorities. The association has urged all departments to suspend elective outpatient department (OPD) services and elective operation theatre (OT) procedures during the protest, while ensuring that emergency services and essential patient care remain uninterrupted.

The association said that the protest was not directed at any individual or department but aimed at protecting the dignity of residents, ensuring a proper learning environment, strengthening clinical training and securing the infrastructure required for safe and effective patient care.

World.title: Delhi braces for CJP protest: 45 metro stations shut, trains cancelled, 23,000 security personnel deployed
World.content:
As the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), along with student organisations, social activists and farmer groups, gears up for a massive protest on Saturday (October 10, 2026), authorities have tightened security and imposed traffic restrictions across New Delhi.

The CJP, led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, along with other student bodies such as All India Students Association (AISA) and AISF, announced a nationwide march to Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the complete rollback of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Protestors allege that the SIR exercise is being misused to tamper with voter lists by deleting genuine voters, misclassifying living citizens as deceased despite producing Aadhaar, PAN and other valid documents to establish that they were alive and altering key registration documents like Form 6 without consent.

45 metro stations closed

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has announced the closure of 45 metro stations on Saturday in view of the prevailing law and order situation. The move follows DMRC’s earlier order of closure of 57 metro stations, which got revoked after Supreme Court directed Central Government to lift stringent restrictions.

On Friday night, the DMRC posted in X, “Due to security reasons, the entry and exit at the following metro stations will remain closed from 09:00 PM on 9th October, 2026 till 06:00 PM on 10th October, 2026. Further the situation will be reviewed by the security agencies and necessary updates will be shared accordingly. However, interchange facility will remain available at all the concerned metro stations except New Delhi metro station”.

Major transit hubs such as Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Kashmere Gate, Hauz Khas, and Supreme Court are among the closed locations.

Trains cancelled and diverted

Similarly, railway zones across the country, including Western Railway, Central Railway, Northern Railway and North-Western Railway, have cancelled or rescheduled over 200 trains coming into or originating from Delhi citing severe road traffic congestion around New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations.

Western Railway rescheduled the Mumbai Central–New Delhi Rajdhani Express (12951) and August Kranti Rajdhani Express (12953) by five hours, while cancelling services like the Bandra Terminus–Hazrat Nizamuddin Express (12247), Dr. Ambedkar Nagar–New Delhi Express (20155), Indore–Hazrat Nizamuddin Express (09309), Indore–New Delhi Express (12415), and Sabarmati–New Delhi Express (12957). Central Railway cancelled the CSMT–Hazrat Nizamuddin Rajdhani Express (22221) and CSMT–New Delhi Rajdhani Express (22209. The North Western Railway on Friday (October 9) cancelled 13 train services scheduled to depart for the national capital on October 9 and 10, citing “operational reasons”. Meanwhile, the Jammu railway division on Friday announced the cancellation of four key trains heading to the national capital, including the superfast Rajdhani Express.

This includes 75 Mail/Express including Rajdhani, Tejas, Shatabdi, and 170 passenger trains.

Railways has set up dedicated helpdesks and officials clarified that passengers with valid, verified train tickets will be allowed access to stations.

23,000 security personnel deployed

The Ministry of Home Affairs has provided the Delhi Police with additional companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) to strengthen security arrangements in view of the proposed protest and other potential gatherings in the national capital.

According to sources, around 23,000 security personnel are expected to be deployed across Delhi between October 8, 2026 and October 12, 2026.

The New Delhi area is expected to witness extensive security deployment on October 10, 2026, with multi-layered barricading, CCTV surveillance and Facial Recognition System (FRS)-enabled cameras being used to monitor movement.

Strict vigil will be maintained at Delhi’s borders, railway stations and bus terminals. Security agencies are also keeping a special watch to prevent criminal elements from entering protest gatherings by posing as protesters, sources said.

Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is in force, and gatherings in violation of the restrictions will not be permitted.

Depending on the situation, police may also regulate access to metro stations and markets in the New Delhi area.

Security agencies are maintaining close coordination and monitoring developments ahead of October 10 to prevent any law-and-order situation in the national capital, sources said.

Other closures: schools, colleges, liquor shops shut

The Delhi government ordered all retail liquor vendors to remain closed on October 9, 2026 and October 10, 2026, citing the prevailing situation and the need to maintain public order. Multiple educational institutions including Sardar Patel Vidyalaya, shifted classes online and postponed scheduled events

Who are joining the CJP protest

Despite the Delhi Police denying permission for the protests, citing past rule violations and short application notice, several civil groups and prominent leaders have shown their interest in participating in the protests.

Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has announced that his family and he will join the protest at Jantar Mantar. AISA national president and student activist Neha Bora urged participants across the country to hold local sit-ins wherever they are. The demonstration will continue along with the Left student groups, farmers associations and civil rights groups.

CJP leaders including Mr. Dipke, Sayrav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will be leading the agitation.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Delhi protest: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee released from detention, alleges ‘kidnapping’
World.content:
YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was released by the Crime Branch, Gurugram, around 2 a.m. on Sunday (October 11, 2026).

A spokesperson for the Gurugram police has said that no charges were pressed against him. "He can be detained again, or further legal action might be taken if he tries to go to Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders," a police source said.

Follow the Anti-CEC protest updates on October 11, 2026.

In a video posted on his X handle, Mr. Rathee alleged that he was neither arrested nor detained, but instead he was kidnapped, adding that police personnel came to his home in plainclothes and took him away.

Addressing rumours about his citizenship, Mr. Rathee displayed his passport in the video and asserted that he is an Indian citizen. He also rejected claims that he had not intended to participate in the protest.

I was not arrested or detained, I was KIDNAPPED. Thank you for your support, here's the full story 👇 https://t.co/gcN8cAUOmY — Dhruv Rathee (@dhruv_rathee) October 11, 2026

Mr. Rathee criticised the restrictions imposed ahead of the protest and described the situation as an “unofficial emergency”. He said he would continue to raise his voice on issues concerning the country.

Mr. Rathee was detained from his residence in Gurugram's Sector 56 on Saturday (October 10) as police stepped up security across the national capital to prevent protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar for a demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities related to the SIR.

The detention came amid an unprecedented security clampdown in Delhi, where more than 7,000 protesters were detained at multiple locations, police sources said.

Several opposition leaders, including former Chief Ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan, and Manik Sarkar, were also detained while attempting to join the protest.

CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were placed under preventive arrest after their detention from the airport.

Police are likely to register multiple FIRs in connection with the alleged assaults on personnel during the protest, a senior officer said.

(With inputs from PTI.)

World.title: CJP 'B-Team' of AAP, Congress: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta
World.content:
Amid a police crackdown on anti-CEC protests, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said on Saturday (October 10, 2026) that the national capital will not be held hostage and accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal of trying to turn the city into a "battleground" with their "B-Team", the CJP.

Authorities detained over 7,000 people, including top Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders, Mr. Kejriwal, leaders from Left parties and Trinamool Congress, activists and students, while foiling a planned CJP protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Also Read : Anti-CEC protest LIVE updates

The CJP accused Mr. Kumar of masterminding voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll, as well as other irregularities related to Form 6, used for voter registration. CJP convener Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained at Delhi airport on their arrival from Mumbai.

Ms. Gupta, in a post on X, alleged that Mr. Gandhi and Mr. Kejriwal, rejected by the people, sought to turn Delhi into a battleground in collusion with their "B-Team".

"Why are these leaders so hell-bent on venting frustration over their nonstop defeats on the public? What offence have residents of Delhi committed to be tormented by the chaos on the streets?" Ms. Gupta wrote.

She asserted the Party would fight resolutely against politics that spreads anarchy under the guise of democracy and challenges the public mandate. She also criticised Mr. Kejriwal, accusing him of trying to disrupt safety and peace in Delhi for his "political self-interest".

"Mr. Kejriwal, who worships anarchy and has bestowed upon himself the title of Delhi's owner, is attempting to disrupt the peace and security of Delhiites for his political self-interest," Ms. Gupta said.

Heavy security deployment and restrictions were imposed in the national capital. Several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, were also detained as they attempted to join the protest.

Ms. Gupta questioned who would be held responsible for the trouble caused to people heading to work, daily wagers trying to support their families and patients trying to reach hospitals, amid the protests.

"Are your political ambitions greater even than the livelihoods, safety and peace of millions of families in Delhi?" she asked.

"Delhi voted for development. Due to the unprecedented public support, Narendra Modi became Prime Minister for a third consecutive term," Ms. Gupta said.

However, the parties steeped in "dynastic politics and opportunism" simply cannot digest this public support for Mr. Modi and BJP, she said.

In another post on X, Ms. Gupta said what happened on the streets of Delhi was "extremely unfortunate" and accused Congress, AAP, the Left, and the CJP of wreaking "havoc" in the name of protest, and lauded the Delhi Police and security forces for handling the situation with patience and responsibility.

"The Delhi Police, engaged in ensuring law and order, and all security forces were provoked, and deliberate attempts were made to create a confrontational situation," the Chief Minister said.

"The professional agitators made every effort to spoil Delhi's atmosphere of harmony, but due to the dedication of our police and security forces, everything remained under control," she said.

The law will be enforced with absolute firmness, she said.

Delhi BJP president and Union minister Harsh Malhotra said the CJP's call for a protest at Jantar Mantar was a "complete flop", and the few "brainwashed youth" who took to the streets lost their "morale" after seeing Mr. Dipke and other party leaders detained.

World.title: Federal cabinet gives nod to imposition of emergency in KP; summary sent to president
World.content:
The federal cabinet on Sunday decided to impose emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

A summary has been sent to President Asif Ali Zardari for final nod, it added.

Constitutional provisions

Article 232 of the Constitution provides for the proclamation of emergency in a province.

It says, “If the President is satisfied that a grave emergency exists in which the security of Pakistan, or any part thereof, is threatened by war or external aggression, or by internal disturbance beyond the power of a provincial government to control, he may issue a Proclamation of Emergency.”

However, invoking this article requires a resolution from the provincial assembly of that province.

“Provided further that if the President acts on his own, the Proclamation of Emergency shall be placed before both Houses of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) for approval by each House within 10 days,” it says. According to this provision, parliament “shall have power to make laws for a province, or any part thereof, with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List” during the time of the proclamation of an emergency.

Article 233 provides powers to the president to suspend certain fundamental rights during emergency period.

On the other hand, Article 234 deals with the imposition of the governor’s rule “in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a province”. For imposition of the governor’s rule, the president simply requires a request from the provincial governor, it says.

PTI cannot be allowed to derail stabilising economy

Earlier, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif addressed an emergency meeting of the federal cabinet where the decision was taken. The premier said the PTI-led KP government cannot be allowed to derail the stabilising economy amid tensions between the two sides.

“I will not allow them (PTI) to destabilise the economy,” he said during the meeting.

At the outset of his address, PM Shehbaz spoke of the recent staff-level agreement reached with the International Monetary Fund (IMF). “It is hoped that we will unlock the $1.2 billion tranche within this year,” he said, recalling a meeting with the IMF’s Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva at the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last month.

He commended the political and military leadership for “working together day and night” in bringing fiscal discipline to Pakistan.

The premier also recalled his visit to London last month, where he had met with senior executives from leading global financial institutions.

He also spoke of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in the international community, taking note of the appreciation Pakistan has received for mediation in the Middle East conflict.

“Pakistan continues to play its role with hard work and sincerity,” he said, particularly lauding the role of the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

PM Shehbaz condemned the recent Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia, noting the long-standing fraternal ties between Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

“Our only goal is that peace should be restored in the region,” he said.

“Pakistan expresses solidarity with Saudi Arabia and stands with it. We will not tolerate any aggression against Saudi Arabia,” he said, adding that it was a “red line” for Pakistan.

Shifting his attention to terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, the premier said, “The way common citizens are being martyred, the way police officials and security officials, children and mothers [..] there can be nothing more heart-wrenching.”

At this, he recalled that Pakistan has repeatedly urged neighbouring Afghanistan to rein in the terrorist elements; however, “they still don’t understand it”.

More to follow.

World.title: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade
World.content:
At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer.

The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said.

President Donald Trump said Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.

Hospitals were flooded with wounded brought by ambulance and helicopter, some in critical condition after the attack, which occurred without warning.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the Houthi attack on Sunday, reiterating Pakistan’s commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.

The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen blamed the group for the strike on King Khalid International Airport, describing it as a “full-fledged war crime” that a diplomatic source attributed to a missile.

Earlier in the day, authorities had suspended operations at Riyadh’s international airport. The Saudi civil aviation authority had initially confirmed an attack had injured several people at the sprawling King Khalid International Airport, with a diplomatic source attributing it to a missile fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels.

The situation prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors to deal with the “serious emergency”, a medical source said, while foreign embassies warned their citizens to avoid the facility.

Houthis have repeatedly targeted the facility, claiming a series of strikes on Thursday that killed three people and damaged a plane, though they did not announce any new attacks on Saturday.

Air traffic monitor Flightradar24 said 155 arriving and 161 departing flights had been cancelled, while a total of 222 flights were delayed.

At around 6pm local time, Flightradar24 noted that flights bound for the airport were “diverting elsewhere, mainly to Jeddah at the moment”. It later shared a notice to airmen (Notam) for operations suspended till 12am.

A witness at the airport reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded and fleeing in panic.

“I was on gate 403” at the domestic terminal, the witness told AFP. “I saw 401 hit, I saw injured [people] in front of my eyes. Everyone was running.”

A medical source told AFP that the health ministry had ordered ER doctors to report to hospitals around the capital to treat the wounded on Saturday.

“We were told we are dealing with a ‘serious emergency situation’. Injured are being moved to hospitals across Riyadh”, with many in critical condition, the source said.

The aviation authority said the number of injured from the attack was still being assessed, adding that airport “operations had been temporarily suspended pending the completion of an assessment of the damage and verification of the safety of the facilities”.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July.

A source at a local hospital said five people were in intensive care there after being wounded at the airport, with “dozens of people injured” in all.

A relative of one wounded person said they had been hit in the shoulders and arms by shattered glass. Three witnesses confirmed people being evacuated from the airport.

Two doctors told AFP that several pilgrims headed to Makkah had been injured while waiting to board their flight.

A diplomatic source briefed on the matter told AFP the airport was hit by “a missile around 3:00pm” (5pm PKT).

“Houthis are attacking civilian targets. Riyadh airport is a civilian target,” the source said.

The Saudi-led coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Malki described the strike as a “cowardly terrorist attack” against a civilian facility.

“The cowardly terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia… which resulted in deaths and injuries among civilian passengers and airport staff, constitutes a full-fledged war crime,” he said in a statement on X.

US ‘may’ join Saudi strikes

Asked on Saturday whether he had changed his mind about joining Saudi strikes on the group, US President Donald Trump said: “We may.”

He said he would be speaking with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, calling what happened in Saudi Arabia “not acceptable”.

US media outlets have reported that previous Saudi requests for US military assistance in dealing with the Houthis have been rebuffed.

Embassy warnings

The Yemen conflict flared back to life after a four-year, UN-brokered truce collapsed, months into a wider Middle Eastern war that has rocked the region and roiled energy supplies and markets.

The scale and frequency of the recent strikes targeting Riyadh are unprecedented in the eight months of war in the region.

Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that supports Yemen’s government militarily, and has found itself drawn deeper into its impoverished neighbour’s civil war.

Both Riyadh and the Houthis have signalled a willingness to keep fighting rather than pursue diplomacy.

The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said it was “aware of attacks” on Riyadh airport on Saturday and called on American citizens to avoid the area.

The Canadian, German and Spanish embassies also warned their citizens to avoid the facility. Spain’s embassy, in a message on X, alerted nationals to a “new attack… by the Houthis”.

A senior Western diplomat told AFP that several embassies “indicated that they had decided to prohibit their staff’s travel to/from Riyadh Airport over the next week as a prudential step”.

Near the airport, passengers carrying luggage could be seen standing on the pavement at a metro station.

Yemen fighting

Meanwhile, in Yemen, Saudi-led government forces were advancing against the Houthis in areas they captured last month around the Bab al-Mandab strait, military sources told AFP.

The Yemeni government last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, after the group seized the country’s entire western coastline in a lightning offensive.

The Houthis confirmed that government forces had attacked in the Bab al-Mandab area — a key chokepoint for Red Sea oil and cargo shipping — but they claimed to have repelled the assault.

Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

World.title: FO reiterates Pakistan's 'firm and unshakeable' commitment to Saudi Arabia's security after Riyadh attack
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Sunday condemned a fresh wave of Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, reaffirming Pakistan’s “firm and unshakeable” commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Gulf state under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.

The defence pact , of which Turkiye is also a part, was signed on August 7 and aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The statement comes following Saturday’s attack on Riyadh’s international airport, which killed at least 12 people and wounded 309 others.

In a post on X, FO said the targeting of a civilian airport constituted “a heinous act of terrorism, a flagrant violation of international law and a grave threat to regional peace and security”.

It expressed concern over the casualties resulting from the attack, extending condolences to the bereaved families and wishing a swift recovery to the injured.

“The continued targeting of civilian population and critical infrastructure by the Houthi militia is utterly unacceptable and must be condemned unequivocally by the international community,” the statement read.

It added: “Such brazen and indiscriminate acts of aggression cannot be justified under any circumstances and must cease immediately.”

FO expressed “unwavering” solidarity with the leadership of Saudi Arabia and reiterated its “firm and unshakeable commitment” to Riyadh’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability in line with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the “recent decision” taken by its Strategic, Political and Defence Committee on October 5, in which the member states had agreed to the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities in the kingdom.

FO expressed support for Saudi Arabia’s right to self-defence against all threats and acts of aggression and went on to urge Yemen’s Houthis to cease attacks and the international community to take “a firm and unequivocal stand” against it.

“Pakistan will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, resolute in its commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, security and defence.”

Shortly before FO, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, in a post on X, also condemned the attack.

In his statement, the premier said that targeting civilian and critical infrastructure was “completely unacceptable and [constitutes] a serious threat to regional peace and stability.

“Such acts of violence, which are a flagrant violation of international law, must cease immediately.”

Expressing solidarity with Riyadh, PM Shehbaz said, “In accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the enduring bonds of brotherhood between our two countries, we reaffirm our steadfast commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.”

The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen has blamed the group for the strike on King Khalid International Airport, describing it as a “full-fledged war crime” that a diplomatic source attributed to a missile.

Houthis have repeatedly targeted the facility, claiming a series of strikes on Thursday that killed three people and damaged a plane, though they did not announce any new attacks on Saturday.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July. Against this backdrop, Pakistan has repeatedly expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

On Oct 5, in an emergency meeting of the Makkah pact in Riyadh, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye agreed to the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and was asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, to which he said both Turkiye and Pakistan had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

On September 18, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”.

Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan will “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalates. The defence minister said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries.

World.title: KP police put on alert as emergency ‘looms’
World.content:
PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed on Saturday put district police on alert for possible violent protests and sabotage in the event of the federal government imposing an emergency in the province, emphasising caution in the use of force.

A notification issued by the IGP’s office outlined guidelines for handling protests and warned that miscreants and anti-state elements could exploit demonstrations to incite violence and carry out sabotage activities.

“To protect lives and property and prevent sabotage during protests, DPOs, sub-divisional police officers and station house officers should personally monitor all protests within their respective jurisdictions,” it said.

The notification said district police must ensure that sufficient personnel were made available to SDPOs and SHOs to maintain order during protests. “The deployment should include anti-riot squads equipped with anti-riot gear, an adequate supply of gas guns and shells checked and verified for use by reserve inspectors or moharrars, special squads of unarmed personnel to identify and apprehend troublemakers and violent protesters, and plainclothes personnel deployed to identify violent protesters, troublemakers and saboteurs. Armed personnel should be deployed only at important or suitable points in extremely urgent situations.”

IGP issues guidelines for handling violent protests, stresses caution in use of force

The police chief directed SHOs to identify vulnerable locations along protest routes and deploy sufficient personnel to protect them.

“Such places may include police stations and police offices, government buildings, petrol stations, banks, shopping centres, important highways/roads and any other sensitive installations,” the notification said.

The notification said DPOs could require protest organisers to obtain a licence for an assembly or protest under Section 84 of the KP Police Act, 2017, or any other law or regulation in force, if they considered a breach of the peace likely.

According to the guidelines, a DPO, SDPO or SHO could stop a procession that violated the conditions of a licence granted under Section 84 of the KP Police Act, 2017, and order it or any assembly violating such conditions to disperse.

“Any procession or assembly, which neglects or refuses to obey any order given Under-Section 85 Sub-Section (I) of Police Act, 2017 or any other law in force shall be deemed an unlawful assembly.”

The notification said DPOs could issue appropriate directions, instructions or guidelines to regulate protests and ensure public safety. In the event of violence, they could also take necessary legal action.

It added that any police officer could temporarily close or regulate a street or public place by erecting barriers or using other means to prevent people or vehicles from entering an area for security reasons, as provided under Section 88 of the KP Police Act, 2017.

According to the notification, during peaceful protests and roadblocks, police should exercise maximum restraint and avoid using force. Protesters should be engaged in negotiations by the senior-most police officer available at the scene, who should try to persuade them to disperse peacefully.

It said to prevent serious disorder, a breach of law or imminent danger to life and property, SDPOs, SHOs or the senior-most officer present at the scene could order the appropriate use of force after assessing the situation and declaring the assembly unlawful.

The notification said the senior-most supervisory police officer during protests would determine the type and extent of force to be used to disperse an unlawful assembly. “When it is required to use force as per law, its application shall be of minimum essential standard,” the notification said.

It emphasised that the use of force should be graduated, starting at the minimum level and increasing only as necessary. In the first phase, violent protesters should be clearly warned before force was used.

According to the notification, if necessary, tear-gas shells or grenades should be used from a safe distance to disperse protesters. Rubber-bullet guns and paper-ball guns could also be used against violent protesters from a safe distance.

“In the second phase, if the situation requires, the violent protesters may be stopped with baton charge by using the anti-riot gear. The special unarmed squad will be activated to apprehend the violent protesters and take appropriate legal action,” it said.

The notification said in cases of extreme violence and an imminent threat to life and property, aerial firing could be conducted by special armed personnel or squads, but only on the directions of the senior-most officer present at the scene.

It added that if a person carried a firearm or any article covered under Section 86(1) of the KP Police Act, 2017, the police could seize it and take legal action against the carrier under Section 148 of the Pakistan Penal Code, the notification said.

“Extreme caution shall be used while using the force against protesters to avert damage to life and property. Anti-riot squad or the personnel entrusted with use of force shall be properly equipped with anti-riot gear to avoid damage/casualties to life of all concerned,” it said.

The notification said the SHO should arrange video recording of the entire protest or procession, preferably through professional cameramen. In the event of a law and order situation, DPOs should ensure briefings, rehearsals and reporting, and issue instructions strictly in accordance with OG-9/2013.

“Prior consultation and coordination should be carried out at all supervisory levels with key stakeholders, including the district administration, law enforcement agencies and other relevant bodies,” it said.

Published in Dawn, October 11th, 2026

World.title: PM takes notice of student’s suicide over visa fraud
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The death of student Laiba Aijaz on Friday drew the attention of the government, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif meeting the Islamabad police chief and chief commissioner and directing them to arrest the accused.

Sources in the police and Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) told Dawn that the prime minister called Inspector General Mohammad Sohail Chaudhry and Chief Commissioner Islamabad Sohail Ashraf and directed them to apprehend the man accused of defrauding the deceased student. The IG briefed the prime minister on the incident during the meeting.

The capital police registered a case against the accused under Sections 322 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code on Saturday, following a complaint lodged by Mohammad Aijaz, a native of Sargodha residing in G-10.

The accused allegedly defrauded the student of millions of rupees, following which she reportedly took her own life.

Orders arrest of accused agent

The minister of state for interior and narcotics control also contacted FIA officers and directed them to take strict action against the accused.

The FIA Islamabad Zone has initiated an investigation and is conducting raids at various locations to trace and arrest him, according to a statement issued by the agency.

The FIA Islamabad Zone director also visited Laiba’s residence, met her family and gathered details about the incident.

According to the FIA, the accused allegedly gained the family’s trust by misrepresenting his identity and professional status before obtaining money from them for different purposes.

He was not a registered visa agent but claimed to work as an accountant at the Supreme Court of Pakistan.

He later made conflicting claims about his identity and employment, the agency said.

The FIA statement said Rs550,000 was paid to the accused for securing employment for Laiba’s brother, while Rs7.2 million was handed over to him on the pretext of securing Laiba’s admission to Harvard University in the United States.

The agency said the payments and claims made by the accused were being examined and further legal action would follow as the investigation progressed.

Laiba had recently completed her BS degree from the International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI). The accused allegedly defrauded her with the help of a female accomplice.

According to a police report, her father contacted the police helpline after she went missing, saying she was under extreme psychological distress.

Following an analysis of call detail records and location data, a joint police and family search found her body hanging by a scarf from a tree inside a fenced enclosure on the G-10 Sunday Bazaar green belt.

The body was taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) in an Edhi ambulance.

After the autopsy, the victim’s clothes and biological samples were secured and sealed for forensic examination. The formal autopsy report is awaited.

Investigators have secured the visa documents allegedly provided by the accused. A special police team has also been formed to trace and arrest him and his female accomplice. His name has been placed on the stop list to prevent him from leaving the country.

Police sources said Laiba’s family had arranged money for the agent by selling a plot and gold ornaments.

Published in Dawn, October 11th, 2026

World.title: Indian court releases 'cockroach' movement leaders from detention
World.content:
The founder of India’s youth-led online “cockroach” movement and two other leaders were released on Sunday, their lawyer said, a day after they were detained to thwart a major protest against the election commissioner.

The group said thousands of protesters were detained before Saturday’s planned demonstration in New Delhi, the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter roll revision.

Abhijeet Dipke and two other Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders were detained before they could disembark from their flight after arriving in the capital from Mumbai.

Ratna Singh, the CJP’s head lawyer, said in a social media post that Dipke and the others had been released by an executive magistrate’s court.

She said they had been released on the condition that they made “no breach of peace for one year”.

Dipke, wearing a white shirt, was driven away in a black vehicle soon after walking out of the court, AFP reporters saw.

Authorities mounted a sweeping security operation across the capital on Saturday, detaining thousands to prevent protesters from gathering at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar protest site, the CJP and Indian media reports said.

The protest was organised to demand the resignation of the head of the Election Commission of India (ECI) over the nationwide voter-roll revision.

Media reports said the revision resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists.

Election authorities say the exercise was aimed at eliminating duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.

Critics say the process has disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims, potentially benefiting Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.

The ECI has rejected allegations of wrongdoing.

Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) talk after their release at Delhi Cantt Police Station in New Delhi, India on October 11, 2026. —Reuters

Saturday’s detentions triggered sharp criticism from opposition leaders, who accused Modi’s government of stifling dissent, and others.

In Geneva, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called for the immediate and unconditional release of all those “arbitrarily detained” in New Delhi.

Both the CJP and opposition leader Rahul Gandhi have vowed to press ahead with protests despite the crackdown.

Gandhi said his Congress party “and the youth of the country will once again take to the streets in large numbers” on Monday.

“The more Modi and his government crack down, the more the anger of Gen Z and students will grow,” he said.

World.title: Israeli strikes kill five in Gaza
World.content:
CAIRO: Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Saturday, health officials said.

Medics said an Israeli strike killed four people near Panda Mall in Gaza City, whi­le another killed one person in the Tuffah neighbourhood further south of the city.

Israel, which claims Hamas has been rea­­rming and launching attacks in violation of an October ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks. Hamas has denied trying to carry out att­a­cks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Isr­ael of undermining the Gaza peace deal.

Last year’s US-brokered ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made as negotiators have failed to agree on terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.

Israeli air strikes have continued, with at least 1,400 Palestinians killed in Gaza since the ceasefire, according to the territory’s health officials, while Israel claims four of its soldiers have been killed.

Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel’s assault on Gaza, launched in October 2023.

Published in Dawn, October 11th, 2026

World.title: CM Afridi says will not accept 'illegal move' of governor's rule or emergency in KP
World.content:
CHARSADDA/MARDAN/SWABI: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday said he will not accept any “illegal move”, including the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency.

The KP CM made the remarks while addressing his supporters in Mardan, where the PTI long march led by him arrived on its seventh day. The federal government, citing differences over the counterterrorism policy, is mulling the option of imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

Afridi said that if governor’s rule was imposed or any “wrong decision” was taken, the long march would head to Peshawar instead of Swabi, and then move towards D-Chowk in Islamabad.

He urged the public to come out for the release of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, adding that Pakhtuns would not be intimidated by threats, guns or bullets.

The KP CM asserted that arrests and other measures could not demoralise PTI workers. He said that his party would continue its struggle to end the injustices being committed against Imran and secure his release.

Speaking on the occasion, MNA Muhammad Atif Khan contended that Afridi had placed the federal government in a difficult position through his strategy.

The PTI launched the march despite warnings from the Centre after Oct 3 talks with the federal government failed to bridge their differences for multiple reasons , particularly over counterterrorism measures.

The route plan for the march has undergone multiple changes since its launch on Oct 4. While the party initially vowed to march towards Islamabad, its final destination seemingly remains tentative as the KP CM has yet to announce the plan for the trek after Oct 11, beyond Swabi.

So far, the march — being carried out to demand Imran’s release — has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power.

Swabi authorities prepare for PTI march

Meanwhile, containers have been transported to Swabi Interchange and the Indus River bridge on the M-1 Motorway to block the party’s march, but the motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remain open to traffic.

The bridge is particularly significant because it links Punjab and KP, which lie on opposite banks of the river.

Afridi earlier called on PTI supporters across Pakistan to reach the Swabi Interchange on Oct 11 to join his long march.

However, PTI district president Sohail Yousafzai said the convoy would reach Swabi on Oct 12 (Monday), adding that Afridi had directed party workers, lawmakers and office-bearers from across the country to reach Swabi by then.

Echoing a plan announced by Afridi earlier, Yousafzai said that convoys from the Peshawar, Malakand and Kohat regions would reach Swabi Interchange on Oct 13, while those from Hazara, Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan would arrive the next day, when the CM Afridi would announce the next course of action.

The KP chief executive is expected to address party workers at Shewa Adda in Razaar tehsil at 1pm, at the district headquarters at 3pm and at Topi tehsil at 5pm, which shares a boundary with Ghazi in Haripur district.

In a post on X earlier in the day, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan said the convoy will stay overnight in Mardan. He also said the future course of action will be announced on Oct 13 and they will move beyond Swabi.

Refused pressure, Afridi claims

Earlier in the day, the KP CM addressed a large gathering at Farooq-i-Azam Chowk in Charsadda, where he reiterated his opposition to any military operations in the province.

Afridi said he stood firmly with the people and would not accept decisions imposed through pressure or threats.

“I was asked to sign, but I refused,” he said, adding that he would neither retreat from his position under pressure nor compromise on his principles.

Afridi said his position on national security and the Kashmir issue was clear and unequivocal. He noted that important national matters should be addressed on the basis of principles rather than political pressure.

Referring to what he alleged were preparations for a possible military operation, the KP CM reiterated that he would not sign any document under pressure. He claimed attempts had been made to persuade him to agree to certain decisions, but he had declined.

Afridi has repeatedly voiced his opposition to the federal government’s policies on counterterrorism and Afghanistan since he was elected as the KP chief minister in October 2025.

Speaking in Charsadda, the PTI leader stressed the need to protect public rights, democratic values and the people’s mandate, saying public aspirations and ground realities should not be ignored in decision-making. He urged party workers to remain united and maintain discipline in their political struggle.

He referred to the “threats” of the imposition of governor’s rule or emergency, adding that the matter “had gone beyond seats and power” and he was ready to “sacrifice” his seat for Imran and Pakhtuns.

The chief minister highlighted that KP had suffered immense losses in the fight against terrorism, adding that the sacrifices made by its residents should not be forgotten and that their concerns regarding peace, stability and fundamental rights deserved serious attention.

Afridi reiterated he would announce the next plan of action on Oct 13 at the Swabi interchange.

He called on PTI workers to remain united in their struggle for their rights, adding that political differences should be resolved through democratic means and that the voice of the people should be respected.

The KP CM urged party supporters to remain steadfast and vigilant amid the prevailing political situation.

The gathering drew hundreds of PTI supporters to the roundabout, many wearing red caps and chanting slogans in support of Imran. The chief minister addressed the crowd from a container alongside party leaders.

Guidelines issued for police to deal with protests

While the PTI seemed determined to continue with its long march, KP Inspector General Zulfiqar Hameed issued operational guidelines to the police to deal with protests.

The document issued by the police chief, available with Dawn, noted that in “all cases of public protests there is a possibility that miscreants and anti-state elements may use an opportunity to [incite] violence and carry out sabotage activities”.

To prevent such acts, the guidelines were issued in continuation of Operational Guidelines-9/2013 and in light of Sections 83 to 88 of the KP Police Act 2017, for “strict compliance”.

The KP IG directed personnel to exercise “maximum restraint” and avoid the use of force for peaceful protests. “The protesters shall be engaged in negotiations through the senior-most police officer available.”

However, it provided guidelines for a phased use of force to disperse violent protesters. “When it is required to use force as per law, its application shall be of minimum essential standard,” it stated.

The guidelines allowed the use of force to be graduated from the minimum to the “optimum level required” in the following manner:

In the first phase, the violent protesters may clearly be warned against violence before starting use of force. If the need arises after warning them, tear gas shells/grenades shall be used at a safe distance to disperse them

Rubber bullet guns and paper ball guns can be used against violent protesters from a safe distance to disperse them

In the second phase, if the situation requires, violent protesters may be “stopped with baton charge by using the anti-riot gear”. The special unarmed squad will be activated to apprehend violent protesters and take appropriate legal action.

In case of extreme violence and imminent threat to life and property, and when the violent protesters resist dispersal, aerial firing can be conducted by the special armed personnel/squad only with the direction of the senior-most officer present at the occasion.

The guidelines directed personnel to exercise “extreme caution” while using force against protesters to avert damage to life and property.

“Anti-riot squad or the personnel entrusted with use of force shall be properly equipped with anti-riot to avoid damage/casualties to life of all concerned.”

Station house officers (SHOs) were also told to“arrange video-recording, preferably through professional cameramen, of the entire protest/procession”.

The police were directed to seize firearm weapons or any article referred to in Section 86, Sub-Section (1) of the KP Police Act from any person possessing them and take legal action against the individual.

The guidelines issued by the IG said district police officers (DPOs), sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and SHOs were to personally attend to all protests in their areas of jurisdiction.

To prevent “unlawful assemblies”, any police officer could temporarily close or regulate any street or public place to prohibit persons or vehicles from entering the area for security reasons under Section 88 of the KP Police Act, 2017.

To prevent “serious disorder, breach of the law or imminent danger to life and property, appropriate use of force will be ordered” by the sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs), SHOs, or the senior-most officer present at the site.

The police strength shall include the following formations:

Anti-riot squad, fully equipped with anti-riot gear and sufficient amount of gas guns and gas shells, properly checked and verified for use by the reserve inspectors/moharrars

Special squads of unarmed men for the purpose of identifying and apprehending miscreants and violent protesters

Plain clothes personnel spread widely to identify and point out violent protesters, miscreants and saboteurs

Armed personnel shall only be deployed at important/suitable points in extremely urgent situations, only for public safety and security under the direct command of DPOs.

SHOs were to specifically ensure deployment of sufficient police strength at vulnerable places, including police stations, government buildings, petrol stations, banks, shopping centres, and major highways and roads.

Police officers were also allowed to stop any procession which violates the conditions of a licence granted under section 84 of the KP Police Act and order it to disperse.

KP speaker writes to IG over MPAs’ security withdrawal

Shortly after the guidelines were issued, the KP information minister alleged that provincial police had withdrawn the security assigned to him and all parliamentarians.

“If any harm comes to me or any parliamentarian, the KP IG will be responsible,” he said.

In a post-midnight letter to IG Hameed, the KP Assembly Secretariat expressed Speaker Babar Saleem Swati’s “serious concern” over the withdrawal of security.

The letter, dated Oct 11 and shared by Jan, directed the IG that “any security personnel withdrawn shall be restored forthwith”.

It stated that no security personnel deployed for the protection of any MPA “shall be withdrawn, detached or discontinued without lawful justification and due compliance with the applicable law”.

The secretariat reminded the IG of the recent KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act 2026 , which made the speaker’s approval mandatory to arrest or detain an MPA.

“Any such action in violation of the law may amount to a breach of the privileges of the members and the provincial assembly,” it stated.

It further warned, “In case of any harm or untoward incident involving any honourable member arisin from the withdrawal of security, the matter would be viewed seriously and dealt with in accordance with the applicable law.”

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate.
